stories.title: SP gets 3,123 more votes than BJP in MLC polls:Graduate voters back Akhilesh; teachers support BJP
stories.summary: In the Uttar Pradesh MLC elections, the BJP won six seats, and the Samajwadi Party won five. The BJP won four of the six teachers' constituency seats, while the SP won two. In the graduates' constituency, the SP won three of the five seats, and the BJP won two. Although the BJP won more seats than the SP, the SP led in vote share. The SP received 3,123 more votes than the BJP, a difference of around 0.45%. There were 1,481,310 voters in the election. Of these, 1,185,706 were registered for the five graduates' constituency seats, while 295,604 were registered for the six teachers' constituency seats. A total of 55.54% of voters, or 658,542 people, voted on 23 October. The BJP received a total of 86,120 votes across the six teachers' constituency seats and 1,75,259 votes across the five graduates' constituency seats. In total, the BJP received 2,61,379 votes. The SP, meanwhile, received 2,12,116 votes across the five graduates' constituency seats and 52,386 votes across the five teachers' constituency seats. Thus, the SP received a total of 264,502 votes. 'Educated' class with SP, teachers with BJP The election results for the teachers' and graduates' seats in the Legislative Council have revealed an interesting trend. The state's teachers appear to be with the BJP, while graduates' voters appear to support the Samajwadi Party. The SP won the Lucknow and Allahabad-Jhansi graduates' seats. Meanwhile, SP candidate Ashutosh Sinha won the Varanasi teachers' constituency seat. The BJP won the Meerut and Agra graduates' seats. In the teachers' constituencies, the BJP won the Lucknow, Bareilly-Moradabad, Faizabad-Gorakhpur and Meerut seats. The SP won the Agra and Varanasi constituency seats among teachers.

stories.title: BSc student killed by thresher, limbs missing:Family gathers remains in sheet after intestines spill out in Farrukhabad
stories.summary: A 23-year-old BSc student died after getting trapped in a thresher while threshing millet in Farrukhabad, Uttar Pradesh, on Thursday evening. The accident happened at around 6 pm in the Nawabganj police station area. The machine severed one of his hands and a leg, which could not be found after the accident. The student, Anubhav, suffered severe injuries in the accident. People present at the spot managed to open the machine and take his body out. They wrapped the body in a sheet and informed the police. Police later sent it for a post-mortem examination. Student went to the field to thresh millet Anubhav was the only son of Tirumal Singh, 59, who lives with his family in Beg village, around 20 km from the district headquarters. His mother, Anita Devi, is 50 years old. The family also includes his three sisters, Kanchan, Ritu, 24, and Gargi, 17. Kanchan is married, while Ritu and Gargi live at home. Anubhav was studying in the third year of a BSc degree. His father has a disability in one leg. At around 5:30 pm on Thursday, Anubhav went to his field to thresh millet. After finishing the work, he began threshing millet for Pushpendra, who lives in the same village. Pushpendra, his brother Sanjeev and tractor driver Lalla were also present. Body taken out of the machine During the work, Anubhav's hand got caught in the thresher, and his body was pulled into the machine. The accident left him with fatal injuries. The people present at the spot managed to open the machine and remove his body. His injuries were severe, and his hand and leg could not be found. Police reached the spot after receiving information about the accident and sent the body for a post-mortem examination. Police investigating the incident Station House Officer Rajeev Kumar said a police team reached the spot after receiving information about the accident. stories.title: Rebellion in Kanpur BJP as regional chief defies state president:IT cell convenor, co-convenor replaced
stories.summary: The BJP's regional president in Kanpur has revolted against the party leadership. Ramkishore Sahu has refused to accept the IT Cell office-bearers announced by the state leadership. Setting aside the names finalised by the party leadership in Lucknow, he has appointed a new convener and co-convener on his own. He sent a letter regarding the appointments to the party's state office on 24 October, which came to light today (Thursday). This is the first time a BJP regional president has challenged a decision taken by the state headquarters. Speaking on the matter, Ramkishore Sahu said, "I have formed a new IT Cell team. I have appointed Mayank Bhatt as the convener and Surendra Vishwakarma as the co-convener. Surendra Vishwakarma lives in Jhansi." "The IT Cell handles day-to-day work, so we needed a worker from Kanpur itself. That is why I appointed Mayank Bhatt as the convener. The team will be expanded further," he said. Understand the entire controversy in 5 points 1. On 22 October, under the leadership of state president Pankaj Chaudhary, a new team of IT Cell office-bearers was announced for six organisational regions: Awadh, West, Braj, Kanpur-Bundelkhand, Kashi and Gorakhpur. 2. Under the announcement, Surendra Vishwakarma was appointed IT Cell convener for the Kanpur region, while Abhishek Pandey was named co-convener. 3. As soon as the list was released, Kanpur regional president Ramkishore Sahu raised objections. He said the names had been finalised by ignoring the recommendations he had submitted. 4. It was not just Kanpur. Vinod Rai, the regional president in Gorakhpur, had also expressed dissatisfaction over appointments to the IT and social media cells in his region. 5. Amid the standoff with the state leadership, Ramkishore Sahu took a firm step and rejected the list issued by Lucknow. He removed Surendra Vishwakarma as convener and appointed Mayank Bhatt in his place. Surendra was demoted to the position of co-convener, while Abhishek Pandey was removed from the team altogether. This has happened for the first time in the history of the UP BJP This is being considered the first instance in the history of the Uttar Pradesh BJP in which a regional president has directly disregarded an order issued by the state president. All eyes are now on what action the state headquarters will take over this open act of indiscipline.

stories.title: VIDEO | Lucknow triple murder:Accused opens fire as family members scream and plead for help
stories.summary: Live video of the Lucknow triple murder has emerged. It shows the accused, Rishabh, firing repeatedly at all three victims. During the incident, family members kept screaming, but the accused continued firing fearlessly. In the video, Rishabh first shot Shambhu, then Shiva Tiwari and subsequently his son Suyash. The broad-daylight incident spread panic throughout the area. A second video showing the police apprehending the accused has also emerged on social media. Police had arrested him at the scene itself. The area has remained tense since the triple murder. Police arrested the accused, Rishabh Shukla, immediately after the incident. Deputy Chief Minister Brajesh Pathak had assured that action would be taken against the accused under the NSA. Deputy CM Brajesh Pathak had met the family members After the post-mortem, people blocked the road as the bodies of the father, son and brother reached home. Meanwhile, Deputy CM Brajesh Pathak and BJP state vice-president Neeraj Singh also reached the deceased's home. As soon as people saw them, they raised slogans such as "Bulldozer rule has gone to sleep". However, the Deputy CM quietly folded his hands and went inside to meet the family. After this, the Deputy CM announced that Ruchi Tiwari, the wife of Shivendra Tiwari, alias Shambhu, would be given a government job. The daughter's education would be free for life. The family would be provided security. Action would be taken against the accused under the National Security Act (NSA). Deputy CM also shouldered the bier After the Deputy CM's assurance, the family members agreed to take all three bodies for the last rites. The Deputy CM also shouldered the bier and placed wood on the pyre. The last rites of all three bodies were performed at Gulala Ghat around 5 hours after the post-mortem. Accused's house boundary wall demolished within 6 hours About six hours after the Deputy Chief Minister's assurance, the boundary wall of accused Rishabh Shukla's house was demolished by a Lucknow Development Authority (LDA) bulldozer at 10 p.m. The LDA officials had sealed the house earlier in the evening. Belongings were removed from the homes of other family members, including the accused's uncle Girish. Meanwhile, Police Commissioner Tarun Gaba had suspended Saadatganj police station Inspector Santosh Kumar Arya and outpost in-charge Ajay Kumar Chaurasia on Tuesday. 3 people were killed in a dispute over car parking and a raised platform On Monday morning, Rishabh Shukla (30) shot dead three people in Brahman Tola, Saadatganj, over a dispute concerning car parking and a raised platform. The deceased, Shivaji Tiwari (62), was a retired Secretariat employee. He had also served as the RSS district general secretary. Shivaji's brother, Shivendra Tiwari, alias Shambhu, worked at Lucknow University. Shivaji's son Suyash (30) ran an electrical goods business. He was due to get married on 5 December. The accused, Rishabh, was a navigation officer in the Merchant Navy.

stories.title: Fatwa issued against actress Sara Ali Khan in UP:Cleric says Muslims visiting Kedarnath is forbidden, urges her to seek Allah’s forgiveness
stories.summary: A fatwa has been issued against Bollywood actress Sara Ali Khan. Bareilly-based cleric Maulana Shahabuddin Razvi said that, according to Islam and Sharia, it is unlawful and forbidden for a Muslim to worship at a temple. He said she should seek forgiveness from Allah. Sara visited Kedarnath Dham on 25 October, where she offered prayers and performed rituals. In 2017, she spent around two months there while shooting for her film Kedarnath. She has now offered prayers at the Kedarnath and Lord Tungnath temples around five times. Read the Maulana’s full statement below… Maulana Shahabuddin Razvi, national president of the All India Muslim Jamaat, expressed his religious views on actress Sara Ali Khan offering prayers at Kedarnath temple. He said several Muslim youths had asked him whether Islamic Sharia permitted such practices. He was responding to their questions. The Maulana said, “I want to make it clear that Islamic Sharia does not permit its followers to engage in shirk. This means that no Muslim, whether a man or a woman, is allowed to adopt the religious practices of another faith or worship at a temple.” He said Sara Ali Khan is a well-known Indian actress. She visited Kedarnath temple, offered prayers and stood in the queue for around half an hour. According to the Maulana, her actions are unlawful and forbidden under Sharia. He also described her as an offender and sinner from the perspective of Sharia. The Maulana said Sara Ali Khan should repent and seek forgiveness from God. According to him, if she does not do so, she would be guilty of a major sin under Sharia. Maulana Shahabuddin Razvi clarified that these were his personal religious views and statements. They should not be regarded as the unanimous opinion of all Muslim clerics or the entire Islamic community. See pictures… Sara spent three days in Kedarnath, says, ‘Baba’s shrine is my home’ Sara Ali Khan stayed in Uttarakhand from 25 to 27 October. She reached the shrine by helicopter. She was seen wearing simple clothes and a cap, which meant many people did not recognise her. Those who recognised Sara also took photographs with her. From the first day, she attended the morning and evening aarti before going out to explore the surrounding areas with friends. Sara met local residents and asked them about their lives. During her visit, she made six to seven new friends in the Kedarnath valley and asked them about nearby trekking destinations. It also snowed in Kedarnath after Sara arrived. She was seen wearing warm clothes because of the cold. On Tuesday evening, she took a helicopter to Dehradun before leaving for Mumbai. Sara says, ‘Kedarnath is my home; I have felt connected to it since 2017’ Sara told Ankit Bajpai, who has been staying in Kedarnath for several months, that Kedarnath felt like home to her. “Since 2017, I have tried to visit the shrine every year to seek Baba’s blessings,” she said. She also made several reels with Ankit Bajpai. Sara took photographs of Kedarnath Dham on her phone, which she plans to share later. At night, she also sat down for tea with local people. The actress may also visit the Third Kedar, Shri Tungnath temple. Last year, on 22 October, Sara visited Kedarnath and Tungnath and shared photographs on social media. Sara stood in the queue for half an hour to seek Baba’s blessings On Sunday, 25 October, Sara stood in the queue for around half an hour. People present at the shrine did not recognise her. Seeing her shivering in the cold, some women standing nearby offered her a shawl, but they did not realise who she was. Sara had arrived at the shrine with her friends. She also visited Baba Bhukunt Bhairav, regarded as the protector of Kedarnath. The Shri Badrinath-Kedarnath Temple Committee (BKTC) had earlier said that it would restrict the entry of non-Sanatanis into the temples. The committee had stated that Sara Ali Khan would first have to submit an affidavit declaring her faith in Sanatan Dharma before being allowed to enter Kedarnath. As the controversy grew, BKTC chairman Hemant Dwivedi said that everyone who believes in Sanatan Dharma is welcome. Sara visits Kedarnath before Diwali Sara’s first spiritual and professional connection with Kedarnath dates back to 2017, when she shot her debut film Kedarnath there. She has continued to visit the shrine since then. In October 2024, just before Diwali, she offered prayers at Kedarnath temple and shared photographs. In 2023, she visited the shrine twice. She visited Kedarnath and Tungnath on 6 May 2023 and returned to Kedarnath around six months later, in October. In November 2021, Sara Ali Khan also visited Kedarnath with her friend and fellow actress Janhvi Kapoor. Sara Ali Khan visited Kashi Vishwanath six years ago In 2020, Sara Ali Khan visited Shri Kashi Vishwanath temple in Varanasi and offered prayers. At the time, she was shooting for a film in the city with her mother, Amrita Singh. Two days earlier, she had attended the Ganga aarti. She then performed Shodashopachara puja at Kashi Vishwanath temple and touched the Shivling. Saints and scholars had objected to this at the time. Photographs from 22 October 2025 She worshipped at Mahakaleshwar three years ago In 2022, Sara Ali Khan attended the Bhasma Aarti dedicated to Lord Mahakal at the Mahakaleshwar temple in Ujjain. After the ritual, she entered the sanctum to seek the deity’s blessings and sat in Nandi Hall, chanting mantras for around half an hour.

stories.title: Schools up to Class 12 shut in 60 UP districts:PET exam expected to draw heavy crowds, says DIOS
stories.summary: Schools up to Class 12 will remain closed in 60 Uttar Pradesh districts on 30 October due to the PET examination. District Inspectors of Schools (DIOS) have issued orders in this regard. According to the Lucknow DIOS, the Uttar Pradesh Subordinate Services Selection Commission’s PET 2026 examination will be held in two shifts on 30 October and 1 November at 45 centres. Around 20,000–25,000 candidates, along with their parents, are expected to arrive for each shift, potentially leading to heavy crowds in the city. The DIOS said a one-day academic holiday had been declared for schools on 30 October following approval from the competent authority. Officials have been directed to ensure strict compliance with the order. Story being updated...

stories.title: Bhaskar sting triggers raids at 40 UP blood banks:7 licences suspended; untested blood sold to patients
stories.summary: Students in Uttar Pradesh are being forced to sell their blood to cover the cost of their education. A major nexus is operating behind this. The Daily Bhaskar sting operation has had a significant impact. Within 48 hours of the report being published, raids began at blood banks across Uttar Pradesh. Investigations are under way from Prayagraj to Lucknow. Action has been taken against three blood banks in Lucknow and one each in Agra, Aligarh, Gorakhpur and Lakhimpur Kheri. Blood was being given to patients here without testing, which could pose a risk of serious infections. In addition, several irregularities were found, including negligence in maintaining the cold chain and a shortage of technical staff. The Food Safety and Drug Administration (FSDA) has also raided 40 charitable blood banks, of which the licences of seven have been suspended with immediate effect. On 26 October, an exclusive investigation was published on the Dainik Bhaskar app. Its headline was: 'Students are selling their blood to pay for their studies; NEET aspirant in Uttar Pradesh says, "The blood will keep being produced, but I may never get another chance to study."' In the report, we exposed a gang and nexus that was exploiting their circumstances to draw blood multiple times in a single month from young students, particularly those preparing for competitive examinations. As soon as the news emerged, an uproar erupted on social media and in political circles. Former Uttar Pradesh Chief Minister Akhilesh Yadav, Samajwadi Party MP Dimple Yadav, YouTuber Neha Singh Rathore and several leaders and organisations, including the National Congress, cited Bhaskar's report and held the system accountable. The administration swung into action as pressure mounted from all sides. Simultaneous raids in 10 districts on FSDA commissioner’s orders Following the impact of the report, a special inter-district team of drug inspectors was formed on the direct orders of Dr Roshan Jacob, Commissioner of the Food Safety and Drug Administration (FSDA). The team simultaneously raided 40 blood banks run by charitable trusts and societies across 10 major districts of Uttar Pradesh. Blood was distributed without testing, putting patients’ lives at risk The shortcomings and shocking facts uncovered during the raids were enough to send a chill down anyone’s spine. Several blood banks were found supplying blood directly to patients without conducting the mandatory tests. Under the rules, to ensure patient safety, donated blood must be tested for dangerous diseases such as HIV/AIDS, hepatitis B, hepatitis C, syphilis and malaria. It is also essential to store blood at a specified temperature. However, the raids revealed that testing machines were not working at several locations, while proper cold-chain facilities were nowhere to be found. Operations of these seven blood banks halted immediately After serious irregularities and life-threatening negligence were detected, the FSDA has suspended the operations of seven major blood banks with immediate effect. 1. Little Star Blood Centre, Lucknow: The doctor in charge and the technical staff had been found absent for a long time. The most shocking finding was that the ELISA testing machine was non-functional, yet blood and its components were being sold without testing. Fragments of red blood cells were found in the fresh frozen plasma, which is extremely dangerous. 2. Rama Charitable Blood Centre, Lucknow: Blood was being issued without ELISA testing. FFP had been improperly stored in a platelet agitator. In addition, patients' relatives were being charged more than the rates fixed by the government. 3. KHS Charitable Blood Centre, Lucknow: Neither a doctor nor any technical staff member was present at the site. There was no trace of the master register or ELISA/TTI testing. Moreover, the entire centre was extremely dirty. 4. Shri Balaji Charitable Blood Centre, Agra: Neither the mandatory ELISA test nor sterility testing was being carried out here. The names, addresses, mobile numbers and even signatures of blood donors were not recorded. The temperature stock record was also completely missing. 5. New Bapu Blood Centre, Aligarh: Serious irregularities were found in infection screening (TTI) and the CPDA solution. The ELISA test was not being conducted here either. There was no trace of qualified staff or the required documents. 6. Maanya Charitable Blood Centre, Gorakhpur: When the inspection team arrived, neither the doctor in charge nor any technical staff was present. Record-keeping was found to be completely incomplete. 7. Anubhav Charitable Blood Centre, Lakhimpur Kheri: It did not even have registration for the disposal of biomedical waste (hazardous waste). The temperature-monitoring and alarm systems were completely non-functional. Advisory sent to all DMs FSDA Commissioner Dr Roshan Jacob has made it clear that the blood and blood components stored at the seven blood banks where operations have been halted will be safely disposed of. A strict advisory has been issued to all the concerned district magistrates to ensure that the unsafe blood does not reach the market or any patient. Show-cause notices are being served to the remaining blood banks where minor deficiencies have been found. The government has made it clear that there will be no compromise on patients' health or the quality of blood in the state. Dainik Bhaskar will continue to raise such issues fearlessly.

stories.title: Azam Khan’s 10-year sentence suspended:Son also gets relief as High Court rules in double PAN card case
stories.summary: Samajwadi Party leader Azam Khan and his son Abdullah Azam have received relief in the double PAN card case. The Allahabad High Court has suspended their 10-year prison sentence and granted them bail. However, the court has refused to stay their conviction. Both had challenged the trial court’s verdict, seeking a stay on their conviction, suspension of their sentence and release on interim bail. After hearing the case on October 15, a single-judge bench of Justice Samit Gopal had reserved its verdict. Following the High Court’s order, former MLA Abdullah Azam may be released from jail, but Azam Khan’s release is still uncertain. According to senior Supreme Court advocate Shariq Abbasi, two other cases against Azam Khan are pending, in which the police have not yet obtained warrants. One case is related to the Enforcement Directorate (ED), while the other concerns the Vigilance Department. Both agencies have registered cases in recent days. It is believed that Azam Khan could also be released from jail if no B-warrants are issued in these cases. This news is being updated

stories.title: No UP govt jobs for violent regime-change links:New rules cover murder, rape and paper leaks; FIR alone won't disqualify
stories.summary: Young people who take to the streets and engage in violence to bring about a regime change in Uttar Pradesh will not be eligible for government jobs. The state government has amended the rules governing character certificates for candidates selected through direct recruitment in its various departments, councils, corporations and local bodies. Gen-Z protests were held in Delhi, Lucknow and several states across the country, including Uttar Pradesh. Protests were also held against Chief Election Commissioner of India Gyanesh Kumar. Some organisations had also called for a regime change during the protests. The BJP has accused the Opposition of trying to change the government through violence in connection with these demonstrations. M. Devaraj, Additional Chief Secretary of the Appointment and Personnel Department, issued the new rules following an order of the High Court. Under the rules, a person will be considered ineligible for a government job if they are a member of an organisation whose objective is to change the system through violence. However, no one will be disqualified on the basis of their political ideology. Under the new rules, a candidate will not be eligible for a government job if they are found to be an accused or convicted in cases related to murder, robbery, rape, outraging a woman's modesty, corruption, terrorist activities, paper leaks or solver gangs. Filing of an FIR at the age of 21 could put government job at risk If such a case is registered against a person after they turn 21, and they are found to have been involved in any activity linked to changing the government within three years of the date of the investigation, this will be considered an indication that they are still active in such activities. However, if positive changes are seen in their views and behaviour during this period, their appointment to a government job may be considered. Filing of an FIR will not lead to disqualification from a job The new rules make it clear that a candidate will not be considered ineligible for a government job merely because an FIR has been registered or an investigation is under way. The candidate will also not be automatically disqualified in cases resulting in acquittal, settlement, or those covered under the Juvenile Justice law. Employees already working in government jobs will not undergo character verification again. Even if the character verification process has not been completed, the candidate will not be stopped from receiving an appointment letter. For this, the candidate will be required to submit a self-declaration and fill in the prescribed form, after which a provisional appointment letter will be issued. If the candidate provides incorrect information or is found ineligible during character verification, the appointment will be cancelled immediately. Legal action will also be taken against the candidate. Report to be submitted within 30 days The district police or the local intelligence unit (LIU) will have to submit its report to the appointing authority within 30 days of receiving the verification application. The Home Department will monitor the entire process.

stories.title: ₹5 crore cash found in blue drums in Prayagraj:3 blue drums stuffed with ₹500 notes; police cut village power before raid
stories.summary: More than ₹5 crore in cash has been found in three drums buried underground in Prayagraj. The drums were filled with bundles of ₹500 notes. Police have detained four people. An Income Tax Department team will count the notes today, Thursday. The case relates to Baraipur Ramnagar village in Nawabganj. How the police got a tip-off and dug up the drums According to the police, they received information late on Wednesday evening that money stolen from the house of Baraipur Ramnagar resident Rakesh Yadav, alias Mahakal, had been buried underground. As soon as they received the information, a police team, including DCP Gangnagar Sonam Kumar and ADCP Gangnagar Pushkar Verma, reached the spot. Before this, the police had the electricity supply to the entire village cut off. They then launched a search operation. During a search of the house, three drums buried underground were found. They were filled with bundles of notes. The police seized the cash and sealed it. Police cut off village’s electricity before conducting raid Rakesh Yadav, alias Mahakal, has his ancestral house in Bareipur village in the Nawabganj area. Police received a tip-off that he had buried stolen money inside his house. The information reached Police Commissioner Piyush Mordia. On Wednesday at 6 pm, a police team led by DCP (Ganganagar) Sonam Kumar and ADCP Pushkar Verma reached the spot. Before the raid, the police cut off the electricity supply to the entire village and then launched a search operation. ACP (Soraon) Shyamjeet Pramila Singh was also present. Search operation lasted four and a half hours According to the police, three blue drums buried in the ground were found during the search of the house. Bundles of cash wrapped in cloth had been kept inside them. The police seized the cash, sealed the house and cordoned off the area. After searching the house for around four and a half hours, the police left at 10.30 pm. They also detained Rakesh Yadav’s brother, Bablu. Police teams took the entire family with them. More than 40 police personnel have been deployed around the house. The police have also cordoned off Rakesh’s garden and vacant land, along with the house, using security tape. Villagers claim he bought 22 bighas of land within a few years Villagers said Rakesh Yadav had lived in Pune several years ago with his brother-in-law and his wife’s brother, working at a jewellery trader’s house. During the Covid pandemic, he returned to his home in Bareipur. After that, he bought 22 bighas of land worth more than ₹10 crore. He then spent around ₹1 crore building a house. He also bought two tractors, a DJ system and a pickup vehicle, before starting a cement and steel rod business in the village. Five to six days ago, Rakesh had a dispute with some neighbours, following which an FIR was registered against him. A sub-inspector visited the village to investigate the case, and an argument broke out between him and Rakesh Yadav. The police then began an investigation, which led to the discovery of claims that crores of rupees were hidden inside the house. Rakesh lives in the village with two of his brothers Rakesh has five brothers, making six brothers in total. Rakesh, Rajesh and Lavkush live in the village, while the other three—Chhotu, Rajendra and Abhishek—live elsewhere. Their father, Ram Aadhar, has died. DCP Ganganagar Sonam Kumar said: “Search operations were stopped on Wednesday night due to darkness. Police have been deployed around Rakesh’s house. Crores of rupees were recovered from three drums buried underground.”

stories.title: Did SP’s core voters not back Sanjayan?:Rajeev Yadav may have benefited from anger over ‘Yadav’ ticket denial
stories.summary: The result of the teachers' MLC election is out. Dr Sanjayan Tripathi, who was considered to be in a direct contest, was forced to finish third. The same Sanjayan had twice finished as runner-up in the graduates' constituency election from this region, and at that time he did not have the backing of any political party. This has sparked a debate: did he fail to receive the support of the Samajwadi Party's core voters? The Yadav community, considered the party's core voter base, is denying this. However, there is discussion behind the scenes that people were angry over Kamlesh Yadav being denied a ticket. The result of that was visible in the election. This resentment is also believed to have made an important contribution to Rajiv Yadav's strong contest. Akhilesh's Brahmin card, played by fielding Dr Sanjayan in the election, was not entirely successful. The party was forced into third place after failing to receive support from its own core voters. Akhilesh Yadav had initially nominated Kamlesh Yadav from the Gorakhpur-Faizabad divisional teachers' constituency. He changed the ticket just a day before Kamlesh Yadav was to file his nomination. However, Kamlesh Yadav was placated over the decision. The very next day, he was appointed national secretary. But there was resentment among Yadav leaders over the issue behind the scenes. In Azamgarh and Mau, where the Samajwadi Party appears to have a strong support base, Sanjayan received very few votes. Rajiv Yadav appeared to be quite strong there. Assembly elections likely to be affected Reports suggest that Yadav leaders are likely to be given very few tickets in the Assembly elections this time. There is still silence on the issue, but Yadav leaders are preparing in almost every Assembly constituency. In such a situation, doubts have now emerged over whether they will be able to accept someone else as the candidate. A debate has erupted on social media over Yadav voters not supporting Sanjayan, with influencers from the community clarifying that this is not the case. Political analysts say Akhilesh will have to devise a strategy on the issue, as he may have to deal with the resentment of Yadav leaders whose tickets are denied. What advantage will leaders from other castes gain? Following the results of the teachers' MLC election, there is also discussion over whether leaders from other castes will benefit from joining the SP. Given the ambitions at the local level, the development is a warning bell for newly joined Brahmin and Kshatriya leaders in the party. Doubts have emerged over whether they will receive the support of the core voters on whose strength they are joining the party in the election. Senior journalist Alok Dubey says there has been a reaction to Kamlesh Yadav being suddenly denied a ticket. The narrative that Yadavs are not being given tickets in the Assembly election could also hurt the Samajwadi Party. This, too, will have to be taken into account while distributing tickets.

stories.title: Mother, son die as Scorpio falls 30 feet in UP:Varanasi-bound SUV flips repeatedly, wheels detach; 3 injured
stories.summary: A Scorpio plunged 30 feet from an expressway in Ghazipur, killing a mother and her son who were travelling in it. Three people were seriously injured. People nearby saw the incident and informed the police. Police reached the spot, broke open the Scorpio's doors and pulled out those trapped inside. The injured were sent to hospital, where they were referred to the BHU Trauma Centre after receiving first aid. The police have placed the bodies in the mortuary. According to the preliminary investigation, the Scorpio was travelling at a speed of around 80-100. The vehicle broke through the iron grille installed on the expressway, overturned several times and fell 30 feet below. It came to a stop after hitting a pole. All the vehicle's airbags deployed. Its bonnet was badly damaged, and both rear wheels came off. The incident took place at pillar number 340 of the Greenfield Expressway, near Sheikhpur in the Jangipur police station area, 10 km from the headquarters. Here is the full sequence of events According to the police, Ballia resident Jayaram Upadhyay (58) was travelling from Ballia to Varanasi with his wife, Kshama (55), son Anmol (28) and three others. They included Ballia resident Manoj Chaubey (42), Mirzapur resident Ramesh Verma (32) and Varanasi resident Ratnesh Mishra (40). Ramesh Verma was driving the Scorpio. Scorpio falls 30 feet from expressway at 1 a.m. According to ASP Dr Rakesh Kumar Mishra, six people were travelling in the Scorpio. At around 1 a.m., the vehicle went out of control near pillar number 340 of the Greenfield Expressway in Sheikhpur, in the Jangipur police station area, broke through the railing and fell below. Kshama and her son Anmol died in the accident, while Manoj Chaubey, Ramesh Verma and Ratnesh Mishra were seriously injured. It is not clear whether Jayaram Upadhyay was also injured in the accident. Bonnet and boot severely damaged According to eyewitnesses, the accident occurred late at night. After hearing a sudden loud noise, villagers came out of their homes and saw a Scorpio breaking through the iron railing of the expressway and falling below. After hitting the railing, the vehicle fell down, somersaulting several times. The vehicle's front bonnet and rear boot were badly crushed in the accident. Both rear wheels also came off. Villagers, with the help of the police, pulled out the injured After seeing the accident, villagers called others and informed the police. The police reached the scene and, with the help of local residents, rescued the people trapped in the vehicle. The injured were then sent to the district hospital by ambulance. Mother and son die despite airbags deploying According to eyewitnesses, the Scorpio's airbags deployed during the collision, but the crash was so severe that Kshama and Anmol could not be saved. Three other people were seriously injured. After the accident, Greenfield Toll Plaza employees used a Hydra crane to pull the damaged Scorpio out of the ravine. The vehicle was then taken to Jangipur police station. ASP Dr Rakesh Kumar Mishra said: There were five people in the vehicle. All of them were travelling from Ballia to Varanasi. The bodies have been sent for post-mortem examinations. The injured are undergoing treatment in Banaras. The case is being investigated."

stories.title: 'Hold elections using ballots and you will lose entire country':Congress fires back at PM Modi after BJP loses both MLC seats in Kashi to SP
stories.summary: The results for 11 MLC seats in Uttar Pradesh are out. The BJP has won four teacher and two graduate seats, taking its total to six. The Samajwadi Party (SP) has won two teacher and three graduate seats, taking its tally to five. The SP has gained two seats. Previously, the BJP held six of the 11 seats, the SP had three, the Teachers’ Association had one and an Independent candidate held one. This time, the Teachers’ Association has failed to win a single seat. After the results, Congress spokesperson Supriya Shrinate took a dig at the BJP. She said, “Modi ji, for now, you have lost all your strongholds. Hold elections using ballot papers, and you will lose the entire country.” Congress MP Pramod Tiwari said God had punished the BJP for stealing offerings. Meanwhile, posters were put up outside the SP headquarters in Lucknow following the BJP’s defeat in Kashi. They read, “Awadhesh Pasi won Ayodhya; Ashutosh and Lal Bihari won Kashi.” In Kashi, the BJP has once again lost both the teacher and graduate constituency seats. Counting for the graduate seat continued for more than 50 hours. The uproar that began at the counting centre late on Wednesday evening continued throughout the night. BJP candidate Kedarnath Singh also staged a sit-in protest. However, he accepted defeat on Thursday morning. Voting for five graduate and six teacher MLC seats in the state took place on 23 October. A total of 152 candidates were in the fray. Counting began at 8 am on 27 October. Around 1.481 million voters were eligible to vote across the two categories, of whom 818,000, or 55%, cast their votes. Go through our LIVE Blog for latest update…

stories.title: Cyclone Arnab brings rain to 20 UP districts:Police announce warning people not to step outside; weather to remain disturbed for 3 days
stories.summary: The impact of Cyclone 'Arnab', which formed over the Bay of Bengal, has begun to be felt in Uttar Pradesh. Today, Thursday, 21 districts have been warned of heavy rain, while 38 districts have been warned of storms and lightning. The weather changed suddenly in Lucknow and adjoining districts on Wednesday afternoon. Clouds gathered over Lucknow, followed by rain. Light rain was also reported in Rae Bareli. Weather experts said temperatures could drop by 5 to 8 degrees Celsius because of the impact of Cyclone Arnab. Professor Javed N. Malik of the Department of Earth Sciences at IIT Kanpur told Dainik Bhaskar that rain and strong winds could affect Uttar Pradesh. In view of Arnab's impact, State Relief Commissioner Bhanu Chandra Goswami directed officials in all districts to remain on alert for 24 hours. IMD and Agriculture Department issue guidelines for farmers Here is how much damage Cyclone Arnab could cause in Uttar Pradesh Crops will suffer the most damage because of Cyclone Arnab. It is the final week of October. At this time, the paddy crop has ripened and is being harvested. Preparations are also under way to sow wheat, potatoes and mustard. In such circumstances, unseasonal rain and strong winds could undo farmers' hard work. Rice to suffer the most damage: Prof. Ravi Shankar Singh, nodal officer at BHU's Rural Agriculture Meteorological Service Centre, and technical officer and meteorologist Shiv Mangal Singh said that the rice crop is currently either fully ripe and ready for harvesting or has already been harvested and is lying in the fields. Strong winds (40-50 km/h) will flatten the rice plants in the fields. If the harvested rice is submerged in water, the grains will turn black and begin to rot. Vegetables and horticulture: Waterlogging in the nurseries and fields of green vegetables such as cabbage, tomatoes and chillies will cause the plants to rot. In addition, banana and papaya trees are at the greatest risk of breaking or being uprooted by the strong winds. Delay in sowing potatoes and mustard: Farmers who were due to sow wheat, mustard or early potatoes in the coming days will be unable to sow them for at least 10 to 15 days because of waterlogging in the fields. This could delay the entire rabi season.

stories.title: Akhilesh Yadav called Uttarakhand’s son-in-law by lady influencer:‘Apologise to your in-laws; did something happen to our daughter?’
stories.summary: Haldwani social media influencer Jyoti Adhikari has mocked Akhilesh Yadav over his statement calling the people of Uttarakhand infiltrators. In a video, she referred to Akhilesh Yadav as Uttarakhand's 'son-in-law' and said she would explain things to her son-in-law and make him apologise to his in-laws. Speaking in a humorous tone, she said that Akhilesh Yadav had become a little confused and would recover in a day or two. However, the protests would continue until he apologised for his statement. Five days ago, Akhilesh Yadav had said that the highest number of infiltrators in Uttar Pradesh were from Uttarakhand. His statement has sparked protests in Uttarakhand. Jyoti Adhikari released a video in Kumaoni and Hindi, taking aim at Akhilesh Yadav. She made the remarks while referring to an invitation to the naming ceremony of her relatives in Uttar Pradesh. It may be noted that Akhilesh Yadav's wife is herself from Uttarakhand. Her family used to live in Pauri, but later shifted to Jogiwala in Dehradun. She said, "Akhilesh is our son-in-law; we will handle him" Speaking in the Kumaoni style, Jyoti Adhikari said, "This Akhilesh ji is our son-in-law. Something has gone wrong with our daughter. We will now call our son-in-law to us and explain everything to him properly." Laughing, she also asked Akhilesh Yadav to apologise to the people of Uttarakhand. Other people accompanying her in the video were also seen engaging in the conversation in a humorous manner. She said, "The Opposition raises issues for political gain" Jyoti Adhikari also questioned the silence of opposition parties in Uttarakhand. She said, "Why are the leaders who take to the streets and burn effigies over minor issues not agitated today?" She alleged that the Opposition raises only those issues from which it expects to gain political advantage. She said that opposition leaders should also come forward when it comes to the honour and dignity of Uttarakhand and the hills. She said that the Uttarakhand government and people were responding to Akhilesh Yadav's statement. The protest would continue until he apologised. She said, "Uttarakhand is a land of sacrifices and brave soldiers" Jyoti Adhikari said that Uttarakhand is not only Devbhoomi, but also a land of sacrifices and brave soldiers. The entire country is aware of the contribution made by the state's soldiers to the nation. She said that calling the people of Uttarakhand infiltrators was an issue linked to the state's honour, and that the people would respond to it. In the video, Jyoti Adhikari also took a swipe at Akhilesh Yadav while describing Uttarakhand as the land of yogis. She said that another 'Yogi ji' had been born in Uttarakhand. She urged people to unite and stop infiltrators. During this, she also said that she would name her 'Bhau' after Yogi ji. Referred to Ganga bathing and Jageshwar Dham A man featured in the video highlighted Uttarakhand's religious and natural attractions through a poem. He said that people visiting Uttarakhand bathe in the Ganga and seek the blessings of Lord Bholenath by offering prayers at Jageshwar Dham. Describing the state's rivers, waterfalls and natural beauty, he appealed to people to visit Uttarakhand and experience its peaceful surroundings. At the end, Jyoti Adhikari asked people to stay away from infiltrators.

stories.summary: Mayawati December 6 Rally: उत्तर प्रदेश में 2027 विधानसभा चुनाव से पहले बहुजन समाज पार्टी (BSP) ने अपनी तैयारियां तेज कर दी हैं। गुरुवार को लखनऊ में मायावती ने करीब 550 पदाधिकारियों के साथ एक घंटे तक बैठक की। इसमें 6 दिसंबर को होने वाली रैली की तैयारियों, प्रत्याशियों के चयन और अगले एक महीने के पार्टी कार्यक्रमों पर चर्चा हुई। मायावती ने रैली को ऐतिहासिक बनाने का लक्ष्य दिया। बैठक से पहले पार्टी कार्यालय के पास ‘दोगलों से सावधान’ रहने के पोस्टर भी लगाए गए। वहीं, आकाश आनंद ने बैठक शुरू होने से पहले मायावती के पैर छूकर आशीर्वाद लिया।

stories.title: From sea to market: How mussels sustain livelihoods along Thiruvananthapuram’s shore
stories.summary: In Thiruvananthapuram’s rocky coastal belt, mussel harvesting peaks between September and February, pushing the shellfish from rocky shores into bustling city markets and restaurants. The mussels, harvested from Vizhinjam, Kovalam, Azhimala, Poonthura and Muthalappozhi, among other nearshore hamlets in the Keralam capital, fetch up to ₹15,000 in auctions, sustaining a community of divers whose livelihood depend on the sea and its seasonal bounty.

stories.title: I will protect the Constitution as long as I live:Chirag Paswan promises participation in 2027, motivates party workers
stories.summary: Lok Janshakti Party (Ram Vilas) national president and Union minister Chirag Paswan launched a sharp attack on opposition parties from Kashi. Targeting the Congress and the Samajwadi Party, he criticised the opposition over reservation, the Constitution and social justice. Chirag said some political parties speak about the Constitution and social justice, but when it comes to giving people their rights, their voices fall silent. Addressing the public rally, Chirag Paswan said his father and former Union minister Ram Vilas Paswan were no longer alive, but fulfilling his dreams was his responsibility as a son. He wanted to work towards building the Uttar Pradesh his father had dreamed of. Chirag's blunt message on reservation and the Constitution Chirag Paswan accused the Opposition of misleading the public during elections by claiming that reservation would be scrapped and the Constitution would be under threat if the NDA came to power. He said there was no need for anyone to be misled about the protection of reservation and the Constitution. Taking a pledge, he said, "As long as Chirag Paswan is alive, neither will reservation face any threat nor will the Constitution be in danger." He said his priority was to move forward with people from every caste and class, guided by the idea of social justice. Questions asked of the Congress and SP Targeting the Congress and Samajwadi Party, Chirag raised the issue of respecting Dr Bhimrao Ambedkar. He asked why parties that speak of respecting the Constitution and Babasaheb should also answer for their political history. Referring to the contribution of his father, Ram Vilas Paswan, he said that Paswan had played an important role in taking forward Babasaheb's ideas and struggles. He also mentioned the recommendations of the Mandal Commission, the rights of backward classes and the efforts made to protect the interests of Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes. Advocating employment and better education for young people Chirag Paswan praised the talent of Uttar Pradesh's youth and said that young people from the state were making their mark in the country and around the world, but were not getting adequate opportunities for better education and employment in their own state. He said that, instead of dividing young people in the name of caste and religion, there was a need to provide them with opportunities for employment, education and development. Questioning the policies of previous governments, he said that young people from Uttar Pradesh had been forced to move to other states in search of employment. "I have set out with a shroud tied around my head; I will not rest until I make Uttar Pradesh a developed state" At the public meeting, Chirag Paswan reiterated his resolve to make Uttar Pradesh a developed state and appealed to workers and young people to support him. He said, "I have set out with a shroud tied around my head to make Uttar Pradesh a developed state. I have resolved that I will not rest until I make Uttar Pradesh a developed state." He said that this goal could not be achieved alone. The blessings of the elderly, the love of mothers and sisters, and the support of the youth were essential for this. Addressing the youth, Chirag said they would have to carry this torch forward. Only when everyone's support and blessings were received could a developed Uttar Pradesh of their dreams be built. Appeal to unite above caste and religion Chirag Paswan called on people to unite by rising above caste, religion and faith. He said it would be necessary to reach every family in the village and every individual in society to raise awareness among them. A new path of development could be created only by taking everyone along. Making an emotional appeal to the people, he said, "Friends, just support me. stories.title: Brahmins, Kshatriyas and Santhals shared common ancestors:DNA scientist makes claim at Kashi cultural parliament; says castes evolved in India
stories.summary: Science has posed a question to a society divided along caste and community lines, challenging beliefs that are centuries old. Were the ancestors of Brahmins, Kshatriyas, Vaishyas and tribal communities different, or did they once share the same roots? At a cultural parliament held in Kashi, DNA scientist Prof. Gyaneshwar Choubey said, citing his research, that the ancestors of several communities with different identities today were once one people thousands of years ago. Citing the study of the Y chromosome, he said that a Brahmin, a Kshatriya and members of the Santhal tribe share a genetic link dating back around 8,000 years. He said the shared ancestry of Brahmins, Kshatriyas and the Gujarati Patel community dates back around 4,500 years. According to him, regardless of caste identities, the roots of various communities in India are interconnected. Castes did not come from outside; they evolved in India itself Prof. Choubey said that the present-day form of castes and tribes in India was not a structure brought by any external group. It developed here amid the country's historical and social conditions. Thousands of years ago, caste identities did not exist in the form they do today. Different social groups developed over time. He said that around 1,700 to 1,800 years ago, the practice of endogamy - marriage within one's own caste or group - became firmly established among communities. This preserved the distinct genetic identities of different communities and influenced the structure of India's population. Shared ancestors found in DNA from north to south According to Prof. Choubey, the DNA of people living in northern, southern, eastern and tribal regions contains several shared genetic components. Although their languages, food habits, physical features and geographical conditions may differ, their ancestors share a deep connection. He said modern genetic studies challenge the colonial view that India's diversity should be seen as a division into different races. Mitochondrial DNA comes from the mother, Y chromosome from the father In the lecture, he also explained the process of studying DNA. He said that mitochondrial DNA is passed from mothers to their children, while the Y chromosome is passed from fathers to sons. By studying the two, scientists can trace maternal and paternal lineages dating back thousands of years. Referring to the worship of Shakti, he described the mother as a source of energy. He also discussed the links between Indian traditions and modern science. Human presence in India dates back 74,000 years Referring to archaeological evidence found in the Jeru Valley of Karnataka, Prof. Choubey said that humans have been present in India for at least 74,000 years. He also mentioned human migration from Africa, the Indus Valley Civilisation and ancient trade links with Mesopotamia. Ancestors from two regions also found in the DNA of the Northeast Referring to DNA studies conducted on the population of northeastern India, he said that the genetic makeup of the region's people reflects contributions from ancestors originating in both the Ganga Valley and Southeast Asia. This also raises questions about the view that the population of northeastern India can be attributed solely to migration from outside. Note: A shared genetic link identified through DNA does not mean that the identities or histories of present-day communities are the same. It indicates a biological relationship between their ancestors.

stories.title: Hardoi girl dies after consuming cough syrup:Mother found her unresponsive when she went to wake her; doctors say overdose caused her death
stories.summary: In Hardoi, a 4-year-old girl died on Thursday after drinking cough syrup before going to sleep. The innocent child had gone with her parents to attend the naming ceremony (Namkaran) of her cousin. There, she mistakenly consumed her grandmother's cough syrup and then went to sleep. Believing the child had fallen asleep out of fatigue, the family members did not wake her up. In the morning, when she did not wake up for a long time, her mother went to wake her. Finding no movement, they immediately rushed her to the medical college, where doctors declared her brought dead. The incident occurred in Peradi village under the Sandi police station area, located 22 km from the district headquarters. Dr. Amit Anand, Emergency In-charge at the Medical College, stated that the child had taken an overdose of cough syrup, which could be one of the reasons for her death. Here is a breakdown of the complete incident: Center's Advisory on Giving Cough Syrup to Children Under 5 Years On October 3, 2025, the Directorate General of Health Services (DGHS) under the Union Ministry of Health issued an advisory to all states and Union Territories regarding the use of cough syrups in children. The advisory stated that cough and cold medicines should not be given to children under two years of age. Such medicines are generally not recommended for children under five years either. If needed, medical examination, doctor supervision, and strict adherence to the prescribed dosage are essential. Many cases of common cough in children resolve naturally without medication. In such situations, it is crucial to consult a doctor before administering any medicine and to strictly follow the recommended dose.

stories.title: Hindu Mahasabha leader dies by gunshot in UP's Barabanki:Family rushes out after hearing gunfire at 3 am; rifle found nearby
stories.summary: Akhil Bharatiya Hindu Mahasabha state vice-president Anupam Kumar Singh, 38, shot himself and died in Barabanki. At around 3 a.m., his family members came outside after hearing the sound of a gunshot and found him lying on the verandah, covered in blood. His licensed rifle was lying nearby. The family informed the police about the incident. The police reached the spot along with a forensic team. The rifle was seized from the scene, and the body was sent for post-mortem. The family said he had been suffering from depression for the past month. He had also stopped going outside the house. The incident took place in Aladaspur in the Ram Sanehi Ghat Kotwali area, 40 km from the district headquarters. Kotwali in-charge Dayashankar Dwivedi said: “Anupam left his room at night and went to the verandah, where he died after being shot. Further action will be taken based on the post-mortem report and the investigation.”

stories.title: Gadkari says no one wins elections without using his photo:Announces launch of 100% ethanol-powered Innova in Jaunpur
stories.summary: Union Minister Nitin Gadkari said in Jaunpur, "I am a farmer. I run four sugar mills. Nobody wins in the 10 Lok Sabha constituencies in my area without putting up my photograph. Everyone puts up my photograph. All the farmers are associated with me. 10,000 farmers in my area have died by suicide. I have been working for them for 30 years." He said, "Our farmers will now become energy providers, not just food providers. I am launching Toyota's Innova this month. It will run on ethanol made by farmers. The vehicle will run on 100 per cent ethanol." Nitin Gadkari arrived in Jaunpur on Thursday. He laid the foundation stones for and inaugurated various projects worth ₹3,677 crore. This included the laying of foundation stones for two projects, bhoomi pujan for three, and the inauguration of three. He then addressed a public meeting at the Public Inter College in Mungra Badshahpur. Gadkari arrived by helicopter at around 1:30 p.m. Rajya Sabha MP Seema Dwivedi and minister Girish Chandra Yadav welcomed him at the helipad on the college campus. He then travelled to the venue in an open e-car. He will remain in the district for around two hours. See two pictures... Read the key points from Nitin Gadkari's speech... I have 10 doctoral degrees: Gadkari Nitin Gadkari said, "I am the Transport Minister. I have launched several motorcycles made by TVS, Hero, and Honda that run on ethanol produced by farmers." "I also have an electric car and a hydrogen-powered car. Its name is Mirai, which means 'future' in Japanese. That vehicle is better than a Mercedes." Gadkari said, "I openly speak about what I do" Union Minister Gadkari said, "I do what I say, and I openly speak about what I do. I work in the agriculture sector itself. I have 10 doctorate degrees for work related to farmers." Every year, we send ₹22 lakh crore out of the country on petrol and diesel imports. If this money is saved, it will benefit the country's farmers. Union minister claims farmers will become hydrogen producers and poverty will be eradicated Gadkari said that farmers would prosper in the coming years through sugar, sorghum, maize and wheat. Farmers themselves would produce fuel for aircraft. These farmers are now set to become hydrogen providers. This would help eradicate poverty. When we decided to produce ethanol from maize, its price was fixed at ₹2,600 per quintal. As a result, farmers in Uttar Pradesh and Bihar received ₹45,000 crore. Greenfield roads being built in Uttar Pradesh at a cost of ₹2 lakh crore Union Minister Gadkari said that he was building greenfield roads in Uttar Pradesh at a cost of ₹2 lakh crore. A six-lane road would be built from Gorakhpur to Shamli at a cost of ₹1 lakh crore. Its proposal has been sent to the Cabinet. A greenfield highway would be built from Gorakhpur to Siliguri at a cost of ₹35 lakh crore. I am getting a road built from Varanasi to Calcutta at a cost of ₹22,000 crore. In addition, an elevated road is going to be built along the Ganga in Varanasi. Its tender has been awarded. Inauguration and foundation laying of these projects Inauguration of three roads, including two bypasses These benefits will follow the inauguration Foundation ceremonies for these three projects Foundation stones laid for these two roads

stories.title: 68,500 teacher recruitment aspirants surround UP Education Minister’s residence:Blow 'shankh' and ring bells; allege police kicked them and broke a leg
stories.summary: Candidates seeking appointments under the recruitment drive for 68,500 assistant teachers staged a protest outside Uttar Pradesh Education Minister Sandeep Singh’s residence in Lucknow on Thursday (5 November). The demonstration continued for around an hour, with protesters raising slogans and demanding that the government issue appointment letters. The candidates repeatedly blew conch shells and rang bells to draw the minister’s attention and urge him to come outside. They said they were resorting to these methods because their voices were not reaching him. Candidates raise slogans over alleged reservation irregularities During the protest, candidates raised slogans such as, “What is the compulsion? This is theft of reservation” and “The Backward Classes Commission has acknowledged it; this is a reservation scam.” Heated exchanges also took place between the protesters and police personnel. Some candidates lay down in front of the minister’s residence with folded hands, pleading for jobs. Police later removed the protesters from the spot and put them on buses. Protester alleges police kicked candidates while removing them One candidate, who was visibly distressed, alleged that police personnel forcibly pushed them into a bus and kicked them during the removal operation. Meanwhile, a candidate who had been on a hunger strike for 11 days fell ill during the protest. Candidates allege police kicked, beat them during removal from protest A candidate who participated in the protest alleged in tears that police personnel forced them into a bus and kicked them. The protesters accused the police of physically assaulting them, hurling abuses and tearing their clothes. One candidate claimed he was unable to lift his leg after the alleged beating and feared it had been fractured. The protesters also accused the government of ignoring the demands of candidates belonging to Dalit and backward communities. Candidate leaves sick three-year-old daughter behind to join Lucknow protest Ghanshyam, who travelled from Azamgarh to take part in the protest, broke down while speaking about his family. He said he had not returned home for two-and-a-half months. His three-year-old daughter is unwell and calls him every day on video, asking when he will come back. He said his daughter had recently spent 15 days in a medical college hospital. She was required to undergo exercises following an operation, but he left her behind and came to Lucknow to join the protest. Ghanshyam said those in the government did not understand the pain he and his family were going through. Candidate misses sister’s wedding to join appointment protest in Lucknow Ashish Kumar, who travelled from Mainpuri, said his sister’s wedding was taking place at home, but he had come to Lucknow to protest for an appointment. He said family members and relatives had gathered for his sister’s farewell, while he was sitting at the protest site, having left his family behind. Ashish described his decision as a compulsion faced by candidates belonging to the Other Backward Classes (OBC). Demand to revise the result after providing a five per cent relaxation According to the candidates, the recruitment of 68,500 assistant teachers was announced in 2018. They allege that the five per cent relaxation available to candidates with disabilities, ex-servicemen, Scheduled Castes and Backward Classes was not provided. As a result, the results for candidates from these categories were declared on the basis of the general cut-off. The protesters are demanding that the results be revised and a new selection list issued, treating 60 marks, or 40 per cent, out of the recruitment examination's total of 150 marks as the passing mark. ‘Wearing out their slippers seeking jobs for eight years’ Ashutosh Verma, who came from Sitapur, said the candidates had been wandering in search of jobs for eight years. He alleged that reservation rules were not followed in the recruitment process. According to him, the State and National Backward Classes Commissions have also directed that reservation rules be followed in the matter. The candidates are demanding that the commission's orders be implemented and the recruitment process completed.

stories.title: Azam says he is being kept in jail for elections:‘I will die in jail at this rate’; SC asks High Court to decide on bail
stories.summary: Azam Khan did not appear before the Supreme Court in person. He conveyed these statements to the court through his lawyer, Kapil Sibal. The court asked the Chief Justice of the High Court to list the case for hearing before a Division Bench before November 16. The bench must pass an interim order on Azam's petition on November 16 itself. On October 31, the Enforcement Directorate (ED) arrested Azam in a money laundering case at the gate of Rampur jail, as soon as he was released from prison. The next morning, a special PMLA court sent him to Ghaziabad's Dasna jail in 14-day judicial custody. Sibal says goats and cows were described as proceeds of crime Kapil Sibal told the court that the ED's arrest was made with malicious intent. The case dates back to 2006, while the FIR was filed in 2019. He questioned how the PMLA came into the picture. He said, "Look at the allegations. There is a list stating that in 2016, the accused entered a house, looted Rs 5,000 and a pair of gold earrings weighing one tola, and demolished the house using a bulldozer." He added, "Another complaint says that on the same day, the accused entered another house, threatened the family and looted cash. They took away four goats and demolished the house. Goats and cows have been described as proceeds of crime. What is all this?" CJI says, 'There may be merit in your argument' CJI Surya Kant told Sibal, "There may be merit in what you are saying, but we do not want to express any opinion at this stage." What is the case in which the ED arrested Azam Khan? The ED's action is linked to the Maulana Mohammad Ali Jauhar University and the Jauhar Trust associated with it. The agency is investigating the alleged misuse of funds and construction materials meant for government projects, land purchases, and the source of funds used to build the university. According to the ED, the investigation began on the basis of 26 FIRs registered at the Azeem Nagar police station in Rampur. During its investigation, the agency alleged that funds and construction materials linked to government contracts were used to build the university campus. The value of 59 buildings and land acquired through 114 sale deeds was estimated at Rs 499.09 crore, while only Rs 72.63 crore could be accounted for through legitimate sources. The agency has treated the remaining Rs 426.46 crore as alleged proceeds of crime. On this basis, the ED provisionally attached university land and buildings worth around Rs 426.46 crore on October 28. Read what happened after Azam walked out of jail Azam Khan walked out of Rampur jail with his son Abdullah at 7.15 pm on Saturday, October 31, after 11 months. An ED team had entered the jail 15 minutes before his release. A total of 24 CRPF personnel were also deployed. At the jail's main gate, a heated argument broke out between the officials, who had arrived in a white car, and Azam's lawyers. Azam also answered the officials' questions during the exchange, but no agreement was reached. The officials then took him away in their car. During this, Azam raised his hand towards the sky and said, "Allah is watching everything. What more can I say now? This is the punishment for being a Muslim. My mistake is that a Muslim built a university. This is our crime." On October 29, the High Court suspended the 10-year prison sentence awarded to Azam and his son Abdullah in the two-PAN-card case and granted bail to both. Following this, they were released from Rampur jail. Two cases pending against Azam Khan 1. First case: On October 14, the Enforcement Directorate (ED) registered an FIR over alleged financial irregularities linked to the Jauhar Trust and the Maulana Mohammad Ali Jauhar University. The FIR was registered at Azeem Nagar police station in Rampur. The ED suspects irregularities in the sources of funds received by the trust and university and how the money was used. 2. Second case: This case relates to alleged irregularities in the sale of land belonging to the Uttar Pradesh State Haj Committee. A Vigilance Department investigation confirmed a revenue loss of Rs 2.08 crore to the committee due to the land sale. Five people, including Azam Khan, have been named as accused in the case. They include then secretary Akhlaq Ahmed, Dr MAA Khan, Aamish Developers proprietor Mohammad Ayub, and Mustaqeem Ahmed.

stories.title: Mayawati says Lucknow will be packed on 6 December:Claims rally will break all records; ‘Beware of hypocrites’ posters put up ahead of meeting
stories.summary: The BSP has stepped up preparations for the 2027 Assembly elections. Party chief Mayawati is holding a key meeting with office-bearers in Lucknow on Thursday. The meeting is reviewing the organisation's grassroots position, election preparations and the selection of candidates. Mayawati will give the office-bearers strategies and necessary directions to ensure victory in the elections. A major decision may also be taken regarding the rally on 6 December. According to information issued by the BSP state office, around 550 office-bearers, including state president Vishwanath Pal, national coordinator Akash Anand, his father Anand Kumar, national general secretary Satish Chandra Mishra and Azamgarh divisional coordinator Indu Singh, have arrived for the meeting. They include office-bearers at all levels of the state unit and presidents of all 75 districts. Ukesh Singh is also present at the meeting. At the meeting, Mayawati will seek a progress report on the instructions issued earlier regarding strengthening the party organisation at the booth and grassroots levels, expanding its support base among all sections of society and selecting candidates. A decision will also be taken regarding Akash Anand's upcoming rallies. BSP to hold major rally in Lucknow on 6 December The BSP is preparing to demonstrate its political strength through a major rally in Lucknow on 6th December. The meeting will discuss preparations for the rally. Office-bearers may be assigned responsibility for bringing workers from different districts, mobilising crowds and managing arrangements for the rally. Political circles are comparing the BSP's rally with the proposed rally of Azad Samaj Party (ASP) chief and MP Chandrashekhar Azad at Lucknow's Ramabai Ambedkar Ground on 26 November. It is being seen as a show of strength by the two parties in Dalit politics. BSP has announced more than 100 candidates The BSP has so far announced candidates for around 100 Assembly seats. Mayawati has directed that the names of candidates for most seats be finalised by November. The meeting will review progress in this process. Mayawati may travel to Delhi after the meeting According to party sources, Mayawati may travel to Delhi after the meeting. She has to take possession of the accommodation allotted to her by the government there. She will also attend her younger sister's daughter wedding.

stories.title: Ban non-vegetarian food on Vande Bharat sleeper trains:Saints raise demand at Kashi cultural parliament, urge Railways Ministry to implement rule immediately
stories.summary: The debate over the food to be served to passengers on the proposed Vande Bharat sleeper train between Kashi and New Delhi has intensified. From the platform of the Sanskriti Sansad, Govind Sharma appealed to the Ministry of Railways to stop serving non-vegetarian food on the train after discussions with saints and with their consent. He also called for only vegetarian food to be served on all trains operating from Varanasi. The issue arose amid discussions about the Vande Bharat sleeper train operating six days a week between Varanasi and New Delhi from 31 October. People associated with Kashi's religious and social organisations have questioned why the same arrangement cannot be introduced on trains running from Kashi when only vegetarian food is served on the Vande Bharat trains travelling from Ayodhya to New Delhi and from Delhi to Katra (the Vaishno Devi shrine). Discussion on religious faith and catering arrangements Those associated with Kashi's religious traditions believe that food served on trains connecting religious cities should take local religious and cultural sentiments into account. On this basis, there are also growing demands for vegetarian food to be served on Vande Bharat trains operating from Varanasi. Swami Jitendranand, national general secretary of the Akhil Bharatiya Sant Samiti, said, “When meat is not served on Vande Bharat trains on the Ayodhya and Vaishno Devi routes, why is the same rule not being applied to this train departing from the religious city of Kashi?”

stories.title: Husband ties wife to chair and burns her alive:Incident in Kannauj over suspicion of an affair; couple had a love marriage
stories.summary: A husband burned his wife alive. He allegedly suspected his wife and believed she was having an affair with someone else in Kannauj. At 7 a.m. on Thursday, the husband tied his wife to a chair, poured petrol over her, and set her on fire. Seeing the high flames, local residents rushed to the spot. The police and fire brigade were informed. The fire was brought under control after around one and a half hours of effort. When firefighters entered the house, they found the woman's skeleton. The incident took place in Jagatpur village, under the Chhibramau Kotwali police station area, 40 kilometres from the district headquarters. The deceased has been identified as Sonam. Her husband, Sukhbir Singh alias Monu, has fled with the children. 3 pictures of the incident- Here is the full case, step by step- Sukhbir Singh, a resident of Jagatpur, had a love marriage with Sonam 11 years ago. They have two children. Their elder son is seven years old, and their daughter is five. Sukhbir lives in Hisar, Haryana, where he works in a private job. Villagers said he had come to the village only 15 days earlier. It was then that he learnt about his wife's affair with a young man from the village. He began keeping watch on her. One day, Sukhbir caught Sonam red-handed. She was talking to the young man on her mobile phone at the time. The couple continued to quarrel at home for the next two days. On Thursday morning, he left home in anger. Half an hour later, he returned with petrol in a bottle. After setting the house on fire, he fled. After receiving information about the incident, Chhibramau Kotwali in-charge Kapil Dubey reached the spot with a police team and inspected the scene. He said, “The husband burned his wife alive and killed her. He has fled the spot. People in the surrounding area are being questioned. Raids are being conducted to arrest the accused.”
