stories.title: Blood smuggling racket busted in Gorakhpur, 2 arrested:Blood brought from Moradabad; accused tore up notice and threw it at police, showing no fear of being caught
stories.summary: Police have arrested two members of a gang involved in illegally smuggling blood in Gorakhpur. One hundred units of blood were recovered from a car in their possession. Disclosing the operation on Wednesday, police said the blood had been brought from the SS Charitable Blood Bank in Moradabad. It was to be supplied to Arogya Blood Bank in Gorakhpur. The two arrested accused were identified as Faheem Ahmed, a resident of Civil Lines in Moradabad, and Taj Guddu of Sirshwagaur in Bhojpur. After catching the accused travelling in the car red-handed, police served them both a notice for further action. The accused refused to sign it, tore up the notice and threw it in the policemen's faces. The police then began questioning them strictly. The Ramgarhtal police and the Drug Department team were involved in the action. According to the police, information had been received about a gang that was bringing blood from Rajasthan, Punjab, Haryana and western Uttar Pradesh concealed in vehicles and selling it in the district at high prices. The names of more people involved in the illegal blood trade in Gorakhpur have also emerged. The police are gathering evidence about them. SSP orders probe According to the police, they had been receiving continuous information about blood smuggling. Following this, Ramgarhtal police outpost in-charge Amit Chaubey began an investigation on the instructions of SSP Dr Kaustubh. On Tuesday, an informant told the police that a consignment of blood was due to reach Gorakhpur illegally from Moradabad. The police informed Drug Inspector Shridhwajeshwar Shukla and formed a joint team. 100 boxes were kept in the boot The team set up a blockade near the LIC office at Bhagat Chauraha and stopped a white Alto car with a UK registration number. A search found 40 blood bags in a cardboard box on the back seat and 60 in a thermocol box kept in the boot. Smugglers sold it at high prices During questioning, the accused said they bought blood at low prices from SS Charitable Blood Bank in Moradabad and sold it at high prices to different blood banks according to demand. The drug inspector took one unit from each of the two boxes as samples and secured them for testing. Police engaged in further investigation Ramgarhtal police station in-charge Shyama Nand Rai said action had been taken against both accused under Section 318(2) of the BNS and Sections 18/27 of the Drugs and Cosmetics Act. The car has also been seized. The police are engaged in further investigation and action.

stories.title: Denied temple entry, they tattooed 'Ram' across their bodies:Ramnami community recounts its story in Kashi; president says people are now reluctant to get the name tattooed
stories.summary: The name of Lord Ram on their foreheads, hands and across every part of their bodies. From their clothes to the walls of their homes, the same name is everywhere. For the Ramnami community of Chhattisgarh, this is more than an expression of devotion. It is a belief that turned centuries-old caste discrimination into a spiritual identity. When members of the community were denied entry to temples, they chose their own bodies as a way to connect with Lord Ram. They began tattooing his name on their skin and made devotion an inseparable part of their lives. For them, Lord Ram does not reside only in idols but in every living being and every breath. His name is central to their traditions, from birth and marriage to death. Kaushal Ramnami, president of the community, spoke to Dainik Bhaskar during the ongoing Cultural Parliament in Kashi about how this nearly 200-year-old tradition has survived across generations. However, he said fewer people are now choosing to have Ram's name tattooed on their bodies. Denied entry to temples, they began tattooing Ram's name Kaushal Ramnami said the roots of the tradition can be traced to caste discrimination around 1860. At the time, members of the community were not allowed to enter temples. In response to this discrimination, they began tattooing the name of Lord Ram on their bodies. Gradually, the practice became their identity and an essential part of their spiritual lives. According to Kaushal, the community believes that in the present age of Kaliyuga, the name of Ram itself represents God. The tradition has continued for nearly 200 years, and he belongs to its fifth generation. Members of the Ramnami community greet one another by saying 'Ram-Ram'. They also use the same words when calling someone. For them, it is not merely a greeting but a way of recognising the presence of Lord Ram in every person. Earlier, children were tattooed on the sixth day after birth Traditionally, children were tattooed with the name of Ram on the sixth day after birth. However, the practice has changed over time. Today, getting the name tattooed is entirely a matter of personal choice and devotion. Kaushal said only some members of the community now follow the practice. Although a few people from the younger generation are also adopting it, the tradition is no longer as widespread as it once was. The Ramnami community lives in several districts of Chhattisgarh, including Raigarh, Janjgir-Champa, Bilaspur and Baloda Bazar. Its population is estimated at around 5,000. Community emphasises simplicity, discipline and staying away from intoxicants For the Ramnamis, tattooing the name of Ram is not just an external identity. Their faith also places importance on a simple and disciplined lifestyle. Community members avoid intoxicants such as tobacco, bidis and cannabis. They also pay attention to maintaining purity in their food habits. Kaushal said those who carry the name of Ram on their bodies also try to reflect their devotion through their daily routines and conduct. No traditional mourning rituals after death The Ramnami community also follows distinctive customs surrounding death. In most families, a death brings a period of mourning. Many Hindu families observe sutak, during which auspicious activities are stopped. However, the Ramnami consider death a natural part of life. When a family member dies, routine household activities continue as usual. The body is kept in the same room where family members normally sit. Food is prepared at home, and family members continue eating their meals normally. Weddings take place without priests, with Ramcharitmanas as witness Marriage ceremonies in the Ramnami community are also closely linked to their religious beliefs. Families do not need to invite a priest to conduct the wedding. The bride and groom's families perform the rituals in front of a Jaitkham, which is an important symbol of the community. A Jaitkham is a wooden or cement pillar built on a raised platform. It is painted white and topped with a white flag. During the wedding, the rituals are completed with the Ramcharitmanas as a witness.

stories.title: KGMU-Professor named in conversion case joins executive council:Decision on the future of 13 named doctors today
stories.summary: A special meeting of the King George’s Medical University (KGMU) Executive Council (EC) will be held on 6 November following the Special Task Force (STF) report into allegations of religious conversion and ‘love jihad’ at the university. The meeting will discuss possible action against the doctors named in the report. However, the name of Prof. Suresh Babu, head of the Department of Pathology and one of the doctors named in the STF report, has also been included in the invitation for the EC meeting. This has raised questions within the university. The STF investigation has reportedly brought several details about his role to light. He has been accused of pressuring the victim’s family members. Teachers’ association to seek action against 13 doctors Earlier in the day, the teachers’ association will hold a General Body Meeting (GBM) at Brown Hall at 2.30 pm. An invitation asking all members to attend was circulated in the group on 4 November. The meeting is being organised to put pressure on the university administration to take action against the 13 doctors named in the STF investigation. Serious allegations against HOD in STF report The STF report contains serious allegations against Prof. Suresh Babu, the head of the Department of Pathology. It states that Prof. Suresh Babu is anti-Hindu. He takes decisions under the influence of Sumaiya Qayum, an additional professor working in the same department. During a conversation with the family members of the victim resident doctor, he had declared Dr Rameez innocent. This made the family feel pressured to reach a compromise. At a departmental meeting, Prof. Suresh Babu also gave Dr Rameez a clean chit, denied the allegations by describing the victim as mentally disturbed, and attempted to suppress the matter. The report also alleges that Prof. Suresh Babu saves categories first and names afterwards in his phone. After taking charge, he had a category-wise list prepared of the residents in each batch. HOD included as the senior-most faculty member Prof. Suresh Babu is included in the KGMU Executive Council as the senior-most faculty member. This is why he has been sent an invitation to the 6 November meeting. It is also significant that he will be KGMU's next Dean of Academics. He is due to take charge of the post once the term of the current dean, Prof. Virendra Aatam, ends in around two months. In such a situation, if action is taken against them after their names appear in the STF report, it could also affect their administrative positions and future claims. Teachers' Association Also Divided into Two Factions There is no consensus within the Teachers' Association on the issue. The teachers appear to be divided into two factions. One faction is defending the doctors named in the investigation, while the other is demanding action based on the STF report. There is also discussion that one faction of the teachers may boycott the meeting. Invitations Sent to 22 Executive Council Members According to a letter issued by the KGMU Registrar's Office on 2 November 2026, a special meeting of the Executive Council has been convened at 3 p.m. on 6 November in the boardroom of the Administrative Building. The meeting will be chaired by Vice-Chancellor Prof. Sonia Nityanand. Invitations have been sent to 22 members of the Executive Council. See the names of the members invited to the Executive Council

stories.title: Husband and wife burnt alive in house fire in Hathras:Couple were asleep when the fire broke out; children had gone out to attend a wedding party
stories.summary: A massive fire broke out at a house in Hathras around 2 am on Wednesday night, killing a 71-year-old man and his 65-year-old wife. The couple were asleep when the fire started and did not get a chance to escape. Neighbours noticed flames and thick smoke rising from the house and alerted the police, fire brigade and State Disaster Response Force (SDRF). Firefighters brought the blaze under control after nearly two hours of efforts. During the rescue operation, two bodies were recovered from inside the house. They were so badly burnt that identifying them proved difficult. According to the police, a short circuit caused the fire. The family was engaged in tailoring work and had stored a large quantity of material at home for the festive season. The material is believed to have helped the fire spread rapidly, engulfing the entire house within minutes. The deceased have been identified as Shahzad (71) and his wife, Salma Begum (65). Other family members had gone to attend a wedding ceremony when the incident occurred. The fire broke out in the Sadabad Kotwali area, around 20 km from the district headquarters. 2 pictures of the incident- First, learn about the family- Shahzad (70), a resident of Kaharan locality in Sadabad, owns a two-storey house. He used to work as a tailor. He married Salma Begum (65) for the second time a year and a half ago. His first wife, Hasina, died of an illness two and a half years ago. They had four sons-Sanu, Salman, Saddan and Sabbu. All of them are married. The youngest son, Sabbu, lived with Shahzad along with his wife and children. The other sons live elsewhere with their families. Sabbu and Salman sell goods by hawking, while Sanu does sewing and embroidery work. Saddan, meanwhile, runs a business selling imitation anklets. Neighbours said Sabbu had gone to Mathura on Wednesday to sell goods by hawking. He then went to his in-laws' home in Agra, where there was a wedding. His wife and children were already in Agra. Now, let us understand the entire matter in sequence- According to police, the husband and wife slept on the lower floor of the two-storey house, while their younger son lived with his family on the upper floor. As the son was not at home on Wednesday, the couple were sleeping on the first floor. They had dinner and went to sleep at night. The house caught fire at 2 a.m. As it was the festive season, a large stock of new clothes for stitching had been stored in the house. Because of this, the fire spread rapidly. On receiving the information, the police and fire brigade teams reached the spot. Given the intensity of the fire, an SDRF team also reached the site and began relief and rescue operations. SDRF officer Rajat Kumar said, "His team was on duty in Vrindavan. As soon as he received information that a house had caught fire in Sadabad, he reached the spot with the personnel and had the rescue operation started." Couple died of suffocation after inhaling smoke, doctor says Dr Neeraj Verma of Sadabad Community Health Centre (CHC) said both bodies had suffered burns covering more than 50% of their surface. Initial findings indicate that the couple died of suffocation after inhaling smoke. Several parts of their bodies were also badly burnt.

stories.title: Fog engulfs 10 UP cities, cold to intensify on Diwali:Visibility drops to 10 metres on roads; air quality deteriorates in Noida and Ghaziabad
stories.summary: Light chill is now being felt in the mornings and evenings in Uttar Pradesh, and fog has begun to form in several districts. On Thursday morning, fog covered 10 cities, including Lucknow, Sambhal, Shravasti and Deoria. In Shravasti, visibility fell below 10 metres, making it hard to see anything on the roads. Weather scientists say the cold will deepen across the state in the week of Diwali. Temperatures to fall further in Diwali week Prof Manoj Srivastava, a weather scientist at Banaras Hindu University (BHU) in Varanasi, said temperatures were likely to fall further during Diwali week. “Fog may persist in the mornings. With the change in weather, the morning and evening chill will increase,” he said. See the weather pictures- Four districts’ air unfit to breathe as GRAP-2 comes into force Air quality in NCR districts has entered the red zone ahead of Diwali. Noida’s AQI has crossed 400, while the air in Ghaziabad, Hapur and Baghpat has also reached the red zone. The second stage of the Graded Response Action Plan (GRAP-2) has been imposed across the NCR. Under the measures: Jhansi hottest, Muzaffarnagar coldest According to figures for 4 November, Jhansi recorded the state’s highest maximum temperature at 33C. Varanasi and Bahraich followed with 32.2C, while Prayagraj logged 32C and Gorakhpur 31.6C. Among minimum temperatures, Varanasi recorded 20C. Lakhimpur Kheri registered 20.2C, Ayodhya 20.5C, Ballia 20.7C and Fatehpur 22C. Muzaffarnagar felt the coldest, with the mercury dipping to 15.3C on Tuesday night. CM orders immediate compensation for crop losses Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath has taken up the damage caused to crops by continuous rain from Storm Arnab between 29 and 31 October. He has directed all district magistrates to go into the field and assess the losses immediately. He also ordered prompt compensation for farmers and said the government would bring a special package for them. With rain likely in November, farmers have been advised to be cautious in managing rabi crops. In Purvanchal in particular, they should keep drainage in fields in good order while sowing wheat, gram, peas and mustard. Farmers urged to take care while sowing rabi crops Waterlogging in low-lying fields can damage crops. Farmers should avoid unnecessary irrigation in fields that already have enough moisture from the rain, and decide on sowing and irrigation based on the weather and soil moisture. stories.title: Lucknow to run buses every 10 minutes for Diwali, Chhath:Fleet to be expanded from November 6 to 17, making travel to Delhi and Gorakhpur easier
stories.summary: Passengers travelling home for Diwali and Chhath will get relief from the shortage of roadways buses. The Uttar Pradesh State Road Transport Corporation (UPSRTC) has arranged around 900 regular buses and more than 350 additional buses for 13 major cities from Lucknow. The services will operate from November 6 to 17. The frequency of buses to Delhi, eastern Uttar Pradesh and neighbouring districts will also be increased according to passenger demand. Buses will be available from Alambagh, Kaiserbagh and Awadh bus stations. Five additional pick-up points have also been designated for passengers. 107 buses for Delhi, 44 for Gorakhpur The highest number of buses, 107, will operate between Lucknow and Delhi during the festive period. The arrangements include 44 buses for Gorakhpur, 37 for Azamgarh and 36 for Bahraich. Additionally, 23 buses each will be available for Prayagraj and Gonda-Balrampur, 20 each for Rae Bareli and Mathura, and 17 for Kanpur. The corporation has also arranged 11 buses for Dehradun and 10 each for Haridwar and Varanasi. These are route-wise bus allocations. Buses available from three major bus stations Passengers will be able to board buses from three major bus stations in Lucknow. The number of buses will be increased depending on passenger demand. Five additional pick-up points designated Apart from the main bus stations, passengers can board buses from five designated pick-up points across the city: These locations will make it easier for passengers living in different parts of Lucknow to board buses without travelling to the main bus stations. Seats available in 120 AC buses UPSRTC has announced that seats are currently available in 120 AC buses. Passengers can book advance or Tatkal tickets through the corporation's official website and the Rahi app. Booking is available for journeys up to November 17. The corporation has advised passengers to purchase tickets only through authorised channels to avoid paying extra money to touts. Ticket booking and helpline details: Drivers and conductors to get incentives of up to Rs 4,800 To ensure uninterrupted bus services during the festive rush, UPSRTC will also provide incentives to drivers and conductors. Employees completing 11 days of duty and covering an average of 300 km per day will receive Rs 4,400. Those completing 12 days and meeting the prescribed criteria will get a lump-sum incentive of Rs 4,800. Contractual and outsourced employees have also been included in the scheme. For every kilometre travelled beyond the prescribed distance, they will receive an additional payment of 55 paise. Drivers operating electric buses and covering 3,300 km in 11 days will be eligible for an additional incentive of around Rs 1,000.

stories.title: Two sisters from Lucknow die in snowfall:Brother learns of tragedy through social media; bodies to reach home today
stories.summary: Two sisters from Lucknow died after being caught in heavy snowfall and an avalanche during a trek to Kedartal in Uttarkashi district of Uttarakhand. The bodies of Vartika Verma and Deepika Verma were recovered during a search operation on Wednesday morning. Of the eight people who went missing in the incident, six have died so far. After the post-mortem examination on Wednesday evening, the family members left for Lucknow with the sisters' bodies. They are expected to reach home at around 1 pm on Thursday, after which the last rites will be performed. The sisters had set out from Gangotri for the Kedartal trek on October 27, along with seven other trekkers and five support staff members. The three-day trek was scheduled to end on October 29. However, the weather deteriorated during the expedition. Heavy snowfall and an avalanche blocked the return route, leaving eight members of the group stranded. On October 30, some members of the group contacted the trekking agency and sought help, reporting that they were stranded near Kachcha Dhang. A rescue operation was subsequently launched. Four members of the support team were rescued safely on October 31. Three more bodies were recovered on Wednesday morning, including those of the two sisters. Both sisters were passionate about trekking Their father, Shree Narayan Verma, originally from Sarai Pandey in Barabanki, is retired from the Agriculture Department. He has three children. Vartika worked for a private company in Noida and was also a freelance influencer. She had gone on the Kedartal trek as part of a tour package provided by her company. Deepika worked as a graphic designer with a private company in Mumbai. She was currently staying in Lucknow while working from home. Both sisters were passionate about trekking and had completed several treks in India and Nepal. Around two months ago, they had returned from a trip to the Valley of Flowers and Hemkund Sahib. A year earlier, they had also completed the Kedarkantha trek in Uttarkashi's Mori area with their brother Atul and some friends. Brother learnt about the tragedy through social media Atul Verma, the sisters' brother, travelled to Uttarkashi with other family members to search for them. According to Atul, the trekking agency did not inform the family about the incident. He learnt about the tragedy after seeing news reports on social media. The family has raised questions about the trekking agency's role. They allege that the trek was allowed to proceed despite bad weather and that the agency failed to inform them promptly after the incident. The family said that if they had received the information in time, they could have reached the area immediately to seek help.

SP inactive in 53 seats, organisation collapsed in 9 districts:Infighting, ticket manoeuvring or PDA formula; why are district president appointments stuck?
stories.summary: With preparations underway for the 2027 Uttar Pradesh Assembly elections, the Samajwadi Party appears to have lost momentum across 53 constituencies. The reason is the complete breakdown of the party organisation in nine districts. Over the past three months, party chief Akhilesh Yadav has taken action against indiscipline, factionalism and inactivity, dissolving the organisational units in seven districts. In two other districts, key posts have remained vacant for a long time. At present, former district presidents are managing affairs in these districts in an acting capacity. As a result, grassroots activities, including booth management and the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls, have come to a standstill. This has raised questions about the delay in making fresh appointments. Sources within the party suggest that the list of new appointments is held up by local factionalism, rival claims over Assembly election tickets and the challenge of maintaining a balance within the PDA (Pichhda, Dalit, Alpsankhyak) social coalition. Why are organisational posts vacant in these nine districts? The reasons behind the vacant posts and dissolved party units in the nine districts are as follows: Etah and Kasganj: A dispute broke out among party leaders on September 19 in Lucknow in the presence of party chief Akhilesh Yadav. Following the incident, Etah district president Wahid Mahmood Zuberi and Kasganj district president Vikram Yadav were removed, and both district units were dissolved. Mathura: On September 16, an FIR was registered against a state office-bearer of the Samajwadi Party’s Minority Wing over allegations of harassment of a woman bank employee. Following this, Akhilesh Yadav directed the dissolution of the party’s district, city and all frontal organisations in Mathura. Gorakhpur: Party workers were involved in a scuffle over a chair during a press conference in the city. Following the incident of indiscipline, both the district and city units were dissolved. Kannauj: The district organisation was dissolved on the instructions of state president Shyamlal Pal after the PDA conference held on October 17 failed to draw the expected crowd. Organisational inactivity was also cited as a reason. Hardoi: On June 13, an objectionable audio-video clip of then district president Sharafat Ali went viral. It contained derogatory remarks about former public representatives. Following this, the entire district executive was dissolved. Sant Kabir Nagar: Action was taken after the district organisation remained inactive during a controversy linked to MP Pappu Yadav. Budaun: The district executive was dissolved a year ago due to internal factionalism. Fresh appointments have yet to be made. Prayagraj (Yamunapar): The post has remained vacant since the death of district president Pappu Lal Nishad. Caste equations complicate the appointment process According to party sources, Akhilesh Yadav may finalise the appointments before Diwali. He wants to ensure balanced representation across all districts under the PDA (backward classes, Dalits and minorities) formula. Of the nine district presidents and two city presidents who were removed, five belonged to the Muslim community, three were Yadavs, one was a Vaishya, one was a Nishad and one was from the Gautam (Dalit) community. The party is now considering new faces while taking local caste equations into account. Ticket aspirants may be moved out of organisational posts: Party sources say district presidents and general secretaries seeking tickets for the upcoming Assembly elections will be replaced once their candidacies are finalised. New individuals will then be given organisational responsibilities to ensure that election-related work is not affected. Five key activities hit by the dissolution of party units

stories.title: Akhilesh’s PDA strategy and Swami Prasad Maurya:From Ramcharitmanas to remarks on Dimple, the story behind his controversial statements
stories.summary: Changing political loyalties is nothing new in Uttar Pradesh politics, but the bitterness between SP chief Akhilesh Yadav and Swami Prasad Maurya has now reached a point of no return. Akhilesh Yadav recently signaled that the doors of the party and alliance are permanently closed for Swami Prasad. Akhilesh stated that Swami Prasad Maurya is no longer a part of their alliance. Having navigated a political journey spanning nearly 45 years, Swami Prasad may now be looking toward the Congress with hopeful eyes, but he appears completely 'unfit' in the current equations due to SP's core electoral strategy 'PDA' (Pichhda, Dalit, Alpsankhyak / Backward, Dalit, Minority) and Akhilesh's personal displeasure. Three main reasons have emerged behind this political tension and the breakdown of relations between the two prominent leaders: Akhilesh 'Politically Unfit' and a Supporter of 'Gunda Raj' Following the 2024 general elections, Swami Prasad Maurya appeared most aggressive against the Samajwadi Party and its leadership. During a podcast, he launched a sharp attack on Akhilesh. When asked who among the major figures in Indian politics is completely unfit for politics, Swami Prasad named Akhilesh Yadav without hesitation. He claimed that Akhilesh's body language and decisions clearly suggest he has entered the wrong field. Swami Prasad Maurya did not stop his aggression there; questioning Akhilesh Yadav's political ideology, he said: "Akhilesh Yadav is a completely confused leader. He is neither a Lohiaite nor a true Socialist. It is deeply tragic that despite being the son of former Chief Minister Mulayam Singh Yadav, he couldn't even become a 'Mulayamite.' He is an expert at ruining a ready-made political advantage. Nowadays, he is merely focused on pleasing the Brahmin community because a Brahmin predicted he would become Chief Minister. The truth is that Akhilesh Yadav favours 'Gunda Raj' (lawlessness)." 'D' in PDA stands for 'Dimple': Personal jibe soured relations In Uttar Pradesh's political circles, it is widely believed that Akhilesh often ignores political attacks directed at him; however, when it comes to his family, wife, or children, he tolerates it at no cost. On February 2, 2026, during the 'Samvidhan Samman Aur Janhit Hunkar Yatra' organised in Lakhimpur Kheri district, Swami Prasad took a direct jibe at Akhilesh's biggest political card, 'PDA' (Pichhda, Dalit, Alpsankhyak / Backward, Dalit, Minority). Addressing a public rally, Swami said that Akhilesh himself is not clear about his PDA formula. In this, the 'D' sometimes stands for 'Dalit' and other times becomes 'Dimple,' depending on convenience. He alleged that Akhilesh never speaks openly on the issues of backward classes and Dalits. Sometimes he says 'P' stands for Pichhda (Backward), sometimes Pandit, and other times he claims that whoever is aggrieved (Pedit) is PDA. Prior to this, on February 20, 2024, when Swami Prasad resigned from the SP and his MLC post, he had similarly remarked that Akhilesh himself had deflated the momentum of PDA through his decisions, and that no outsider, but the party chief himself, was responsible for weakening SP. Continuous controversial remarks on Hinduism, Ramcharitmanas, and deities Until the 2022 Uttar Pradesh Assembly elections, Swami Prasad Maurya had not made many statements on religious matters. However, after losing his own election from the Fazilnagar seat in Kushinagar, his rhetoric changed completely. Right after losing the election, he stated, "Buddhism is the oldest religion in the world, followed by Christianity, and then Islam came into existence." In this statement, he deliberately refrained from mentioning Hinduism. Following this, wherever he went in 2023, he continued to criticise Hindu beliefs and scriptures. Swami Prasad Maurya’s 4 most controversial statements that sparked a storm: 'How is a statement personal?' — Left SP over this very issue Due to Swami Prasad’s continuous rhetoric, the Samajwadi Party was facing political discomfort. Whenever SP spokespersons tried to corner the BJP on TV debates over Hindutva, development, or employment, BJP leaders would immediately bring up Swami Prasad's statements to put SP in the dock. Gradually, discontent began brewing against Swami Prasad within SP itself. During an event in Raebareli, a youth even slapped Swami, and on two separate occasions, shoes were thrown at him. When the media questioned Akhilesh Yadav regarding Swami's statements, Akhilesh dismissed them as his 'personal views' rather than the party's official stance. Akhilesh’s posture did not go down well with Swami Prasad Maurya. Expressing his displeasure, he remarked, "When I am the party's National General Secretary, how can my statements be 'personal'?" Following this, he resigned from the party. Akhilesh Yadav accepted his resignation immediately without any persuasion, and the doors of SP were closed to him permanently. Outspokenness ruined political career According to Rajkumar Singh, a senior political analyst and journalist from Lucknow, Swami Prasad Maurya's loose talk and controversial rhetoric are nothing new; it has been going on since the Bahujan Samaj Party rule. Back then, Mayawati's government was strong in the state, which prevented an open atmosphere from building against him. When he joined the Bharatiya Janata Party in 2017, his statements were somewhat restrained. However, after joining the Samajwadi Party in 2022 and losing the election, his political frustration came out into the open. Due to his uncontrolled language and remarks, he not only lost his own election from Fazilnagar, but also severely damaged the political career of his daughter, Sanghmitra Maurya, who was a BJP MP. Speculation: Congress brought Swami to boost bargaining power Now seeing a ray of hope in the Congress, he has moved there. However, given the kind of personal attacks he launched against Akhilesh Yadav and his family, Akhilesh will never take him back. By commenting on Dimple Yadav, Swami Prasad closed all doors for dialogue with his own hands. Ahead of the upcoming elections, there are clear indications that Congress has brought Swami Prasad Maurya along to increase its bargaining power in Uttar Pradesh. Nevertheless, Congress also appears to be distancing itself from Swami’s ongoing statements, with its state in-charge Ramji Lal also describing his remarks as 'personal.' Swami Prasad has been a prominent face in Uttar Pradesh's ruling and opposition politics for the last four and a half decades. However, over the past five years, his political track record has been completely turbulent.

stories.title: Blue-drum accused Muskan learning stitching and embroidery in Meerut jail:Hoping to escape the death penalty, she plans to start a business after release
stories.summary: Muskan Rastogi, convicted in the widely discussed Blue Drum murder case, is learning sewing and embroidery at Meerut jail. She has already completed a beautician course. While in prison, Muskan has also learnt to make rakhis, kandils (decorative hanging lanterns) and candles. The way Muskan is training herself while in jail suggests that her focus is now on her future. She appears to believe that her death sentence will be commuted. She is thinking that she will be released from jail soon. Once out, she plans to support herself through self-employment. That is why Muskan is continuing to learn various skills in prison. On October 14, the Meerut district court sentenced Muskan and her boyfriend Sahil to death for the murder of Saurabh. Sahil’s family has taken responsibility for seeking commutation of their death sentences. They have filed a petition in the High Court. Muskan has been in jail for 20 months Muskan Rastogi has been lodged in Meerut district jail for around 20 months. She was convicted of murdering her husband, Saurabh Rajput. Muskan and her boyfriend Sahil killed Saurabh on March 3, 2025, cut up his body, and stuffed it into a blue drum. Muskan gave birth to a daughter in jail. Under the prison manual, she cannot be made to perform strenuous work until her daughter turns six. That is why Muskan is doing routine work in jail and learning sewing and embroidery. Training sessions are also organised from time to time for women inmates, and Muskan participates in them alongside other women prisoners. Expressed a desire to learn a new course from a women's organisation Sanjeevani Mahila Sanstha, an NGO that provides vocational training to women inmates in jail, has trained Muskan in these self-employment skills. Muskan had expressed a desire to learn all the new courses. Parul Bansal, secretary of the organisation, which visits the jail to train women inmates, said Muskan had learnt beautician skills, how to make kandils, decorative door hangings known as bandanwars, and rakhis. She is currently learning sewing and embroidery. Parul said, “Our organisation has been helping women inmates at the district jail develop vocational skills for more than 20 years. This enables them to start a new life after leaving prison and earn a living through the skills they have learnt.” Parul said Muskan had first learnt the beautician course from the organisation. She had herself expressed a desire to learn beauty parlour skills. Later, during Raksha Bandhan, Muskan learnt to make rakhis. Now, for Diwali, she has learnt to make kandils and bandanwars. In this way, Muskan is participating in every training programme. The same lawyer is fighting Muskan and Sahil's cases in the High Court The same lawyer is representing Muskan and Sahil in their efforts to get their death sentences commuted. Sahil’s family hired advocate Sushil Shukla in Allahabad. Senior advocate Sushil Shukla is representing both Muskan and Sahil in the High Court. He has filed petitions seeking commutation of their death sentences. The matter is scheduled to be heard on November 30. Sahil’s family has also taken responsibility for trying to save Muskan from the gallows. This suggests that Muskan is now less concerned about arranging legal assistance for her release or seeking commutation of her sentence herself. Her focus appears to be on her life after prison. That is why she is working to secure her future. Muskan believes her death sentence will be commuted because of her young daughters Muskan firmly believes that her death sentence will be commuted and that she will soon be released from jail. She repeatedly referred to the care of her two young daughters before the judge. Rekha Jain, who represented Muskan in the case, also appealed to the court to consider that Muskan had two young daughters who needed care. Muskan therefore believes that the emotional aspect of her daughters’ welfare will help save her from the death penalty and secure a reduction in her sentence. She expects Sahil’s family to handle the remaining legal work. Once released, she plans to open her own beauty parlour and earn a living.

stories.title: Brij Bhushan’s daughter gifts him a helipad:Built for ₹50 lakh, she says, 'Papa made me capable of this'
stories.summary: The daughter of former BJP MP Brij Bhushan Sharan Singh gifted him a helipad in Noida two months before his birthday. At around 5 p.m. on Sunday, Brij Bhushan inaugurated the helipad by breaking a coconut after performing the traditional puja rituals. Brij Bhushan's birthday is on 8 January 2027. His daughter, Shalini Singh, wrote in a post on Facebook and Instagram, "Today, we presented Papa with a newly built helipad in Noida as a birthday gift." Brij Bhushan owns three helicopters. One of them will always remain at this helipad in Noida. It is being said that the helipad was built at a cost of ₹50 lakh. However, the land on which the helipad has been built is estimated to be worth crores of rupees. Brij Bhushan's daughter is currently the executive president of the Noida Citizen Forum. See two pictures... Daughter said, 'Papa made me capable of this' Dainik Bhaskar, Shalini said, "Dad has always loved me very much and given me gifts since my childhood. He made me capable of reaching a position where I can give him something today." "That is why I thought I would give him this gift before his birthday. This helipad will help Dad travel between Gonda and Noida." "Dad has always supported me. No amount of praise for him would be enough. I do not want to reveal the cost of this helipad, because the value of something given as a gift is never disclosed." 3 helicopters in Brij Bhushan's fleet Brij Bhushan Sharan Singh has 3 helicopters in his fleet. The black helicopter will remain at Noida's new helipad at all times, while the saffron and white helicopters will remain at his home in Gonda. Two helipads have already been built at Brij Bhushan's home. This facility will make it easier for Brij Bhushan to travel between Gonda and Noida. It will also make it easier for his daughter, Shalini Singh, to travel to and from her marital home in Bihar. Shalini's Parents-in-Law Were Former MPs from Bihar; She Lives with Her Husband in Noida Former MP Brij Bhushan Singh married Shalini Singh to Vishal Singh, the only son of former Ara MP late Ajit Singh and former MP Meena Singh. Vishal Singh currently lives in Noida. He is also a BJP leader. He is also the chairman of the National Cooperative Consumers' Federation (NCCF). Besides this, he is the president of the Bihar State Cooperative Marketing Union (BISCOMAUN). Shalini and Vishal have a 14-year-old son, Atharv. The book they have written is titled "I Am Fearless, Not Disrespectful". Shalini Singh is currently the executive president of the Noida Citizen Forum and is also a BJP worker in Noida. She is also preparing to contest the election from Noida.

Return flight to Delhi took off Air India flight AI-213, travelling from Delhi to Kathmandu, took off from Delhi at 7:04 a.m. It landed at Lucknow airport at 10:04 a.m. The flight was diverted because of bad weather in Kathmandu. Diversion caused inconvenience to passengers Flight to Kathmandu was later cancelled. The aircraft took off from Lucknow for Delhi at 11:19 a.m. Meanwhile, the second flight, AI-223, was also diverted to Lucknow because of bad weather in Kathmandu. The diversion of both flights caused inconvenience to passengers.

stories.title: Woman dies immediately after receiving injection in Lucknow:She underwent leg surgery three days earlier, family accuses doctors of negligence
stories.summary: A woman died after doctors administered injections at Highway Hospital in Madiyaon, Lucknow. She had been admitted for five days for leg surgery, which had been performed three days earlier. According to her family, her condition was normal until Sunday morning. She was laughing and talking with her family members. During this time, she informed the doctor that she was experiencing mild pain in her leg. The family alleged that the doctor gave her an injection. The woman died suddenly shortly afterwards. Her family members created a commotion at the hospital, alleging negligence. She was supposed to go home from hospital today According to Mohit Sharma, a resident of Munshiganj in Sitapur, his mother, Usha Sharma, had suffered an injury. He admitted her to Highway Hospital on 26 October. Her leg was operated on 28 October. He said that they were due to be discharged from the hospital today, 1 November. They were at home when the hospital called to say that his mother had died. Mohit accused the doctors of withholding the body for two hours. Police reached after receiving information, investigation begins Following the woman's death, chaos broke out at the hospital. On receiving the information, Madiyaon police station in-charge Alok Rao reached the scene with a police team and calmed the family members. Police said the exact cause of death would be established only after the post-mortem report and investigation.

stories.summary: Ramayan Ke Saat Kand: अयोध्या में दीपोत्सव-2026 (Ayodhya Deepotsav) इस बार सिर्फ दीपों की रोशनी और आतिशबाजी तक सीमित नहीं रहेगा, बल्कि रामनगरी की सड़कों पर भगवान श्रीराम की पूरी जीवन यात्रा भी जीवंत होती दिखाई देगी। दीपोत्सव के दौरान निकलने वाली सांस्कृतिक झांकी यात्रा में रामायण के सातों कांडों की प्रमुख घटनाओं को 14 भव्य झांकियों के जरिए दिखाने की तैयारी है। इन झांकियों में 3D मॉडल के माध्यम से बालकांड से लेकर उत्तरकांड तक के प्रसंगों को इस तरह सजाया जाएगा कि दर्शकों को रामकथा (Ram Katha)के महत्वपूर्ण दृश्य अपनी आंखों के सामने होते हुए महसूस होंगे। खास बात यह है कि इस बार रामकथा के साथ उत्तर प्रदेश के सात सांस्कृतिक अंचलों और देश के अलग-अलग राज्यों के लोक नृत्यों की भी झलक देखने को मिलेगी। यह पूरी यात्रा साकेत महाविद्यालय से शुरू होकर रामकथा पार्क तक पहुंचेगी।

stories.title: Five police officers face action for negligence during night patrols:Two outpost chiefs attached to police stations, three sent to the police lines
stories.summary: Lucknow Police Commissioner Tarun Gaba has taken action against five police personnel for negligence in night patrols and duty. Two of them have been removed as outpost in-charges and attached to police stations, while three have been sent to the police lines. Directives have also been issued to initiate departmental action against all of them. The Police Commissioner had directed that night patrols be made regular and effective to strengthen law and order, ensure women's safety and prevent crime. He had also made it clear that action would be taken against police personnel found negligent or absent from duty. As part of this, the DCPs of the Eastern, Southern and Central zones conducted surprise checks of night patrols and duty. Five police personnel were found negligent in their duties and absent. Two outpost in-charges removed in Eastern Zone Eastern DCP Dr Deeksha Sharma removed Aravali outpost in-charge woman SI Archana (Ghazipur police station) and Kamta outpost in-charge Sub-Inspector Shashikant (Chinhat police station) from their current responsibilities with immediate effect and attached them to the police station. Three police personnel sent to lines in Southern and Central zones Southern DCP Mohammad Mustaq sent SI Ashish Kumar and constable Satendra Yadav, posted at Sarojininagar police station, to the lines after they were found absent from night duty. Meanwhile, Central DCP Arpit Vijayvargiya sent Nishatganj outpost in-charge SI Satyendra Kumar to the lines for being absent from duty.

stories.title: Yogi Adityanath ranks No. 1 among 15 Chief Ministers:Beats Pushkar Dhami and Himanta Biswa Sarma in Fame India survey
stories.summary: Fame India magazine and Asia Post released the results of the 'Best Chief Minister 2026' survey on Sunday. Uttar Pradesh Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath secured the top position nationwide. Uttarakhand Chief Minister Pushkar Singh Dhami ranked second, while Assam Chief Minister Himanta Biswa Sarma came third. Yogi secured the top position in the survey with 897 out of 1,000 marks. Pushkar Singh Dhami scored 881 and Himanta Biswa Sarma 874. Punjab Chief Minister Bhagwant Mann ranked fourth with 856 marks, while Jharkhand Chief Minister Hemant Soren came fifth with 844 marks. The survey featured 15 positions for chief ministers. The chief ministers who secured the top 10 positions were selected as the 'Best Chief Ministers', while the five chief ministers ranked from 11th to 15th were selected under the special category of 'Chief Minister Panchratna'. Meet the top 10 chief ministers... Now, get to know the five gems among the chief ministers... In the survey's second category, the five chief ministers ranked from 11th to 15th have been included as the 'Chief Minister Panchratna'. Maharashtra Chief Minister Devendra Fadnavis ranks first in this category with 788 points. List prepared in three stages Fame India magazine conducted the 'Best Chief Minister Survey 2026' in association with Asia Post. The survey lasted around three to four months. Public opinion was gathered in three phases to assess the performance of the chief ministers. First phase: Reports, discussions and public reactions concerning the chief ministers on social media and other media platforms were examined. Second phase: The views of experts and prominent people from different fields were sought. Third phase: People were contacted directly to learn about their experiences and views. Based on the information gathered in all three phases, the chief ministers were assessed on 10 parameters. The scores awarded for each parameter were added, and a total score out of 1,000 was given. The final list of chief ministers was prepared on this basis. The survey was not conducted merely to determine which chief minister was the most popular. It also assessed their working methods, decision-making ability, approach to administration, public recognition and the performance of their governments. Performance assessed on these 10 parameters The survey evaluated the chief ministers on parameters including good governance, law and order, personality, public image, efficiency, influence, understanding of departments, popularity, foresight, and working style and results. Administrative transparency and accountability were assessed under good governance, while security and crime control were considered under law and order. In addition, leadership ability, decision-making approach, public acceptance, the outcomes of government schemes and future plans were also used as the basis for evaluation.

stories.title: Nishant Kumar announces plans to contest the 2027 UP elections:Vows to strengthen the NDA under Yogi’s leadership at JDU workers’ conference in Kashi
stories.summary: A workers' conference of the Janata Dal United (JDU) was held on Sunday at the Ramlila Ground in Rohania, Varanasi. Nishant Kumar, the son of former Bihar Chief Minister Nitish Kumar and the health minister, was also the chief guest at the conference. He said that the JDU would contest the Assembly elections in Uttar Pradesh. However, the elections would be contested as part of the NDA alliance. It would work to strengthen the pace of development in Uttar Pradesh. "The work my father has done in Bihar and the model he has created should be implemented here as well. Yogi Adityanath is also personally carrying out development work here. We stand with him. We can contest the elections under his leadership. His ideology must be taken forward so that the pace of development in Uttar Pradesh is strengthened." Will contest Uttar Pradesh elections as an NDA constituent After the workers' conference, Nishant Kumar spoke to the media. He said that they had come to Uttar Pradesh to strengthen and expand the party. He added that the Assembly election scheduled to be held in 2027 was approaching. They were considering contesting it. They would try to contest the election here as a constituent of the NDA. Their effort would be to contest the election as an NDA constituent. They would take his father's ideology to every person. He said that, as in Bihar, our party will work in Uttar Pradesh for the people and women's empowerment. To achieve this, we will strengthen the Uttar Pradesh government by becoming a constituent of the NDA. We will contest the election together with them. We are strengthening our party in Uttar Pradesh. That is why we are going to contest the election from here. The first workers' convention was held here today for this purpose. Nishant Kumar offered prayers at the Baba Vishwanath Temple Workers welcomed Nishant Kumar when he arrived on stage by presenting him with a mace and a statue of Lord Buddha. The convention began after this. Several senior leaders from Bihar and Uttar Pradesh, along with a large number of workers, were present at the programme. After the conference, Nishant Kumar visited the Shri Kashi Vishwanath Temple. He offered prayers to Baba Vishwanath. Security and arrangements for devotees remained in place on the temple premises during the visit.

stories.title: SGPGI recruitment exam cancelled in Lucknow:Candidates protest, allege OMR sheets were being filled inside office
stories.summary: The SGPGI recruitment examination for nursing and hospital attendants has been cancelled. The second-phase examination was held in two shifts at seven centres on Sunday. Around 8,500 candidates appeared for it. The examination had come under controversy earlier. Candidates created a commotion, alleging irregularities and a paper leak. The students alleged that OMR sheets were being filled in an office during the examination. The candidates also alleged that cheating was facilitated during the examination. Police who reached the spot calmed the students. Biometrics failed, examination began late The examination was conducted at several centres in and around Lucknow, including SDSN Degree College, SDSN Public School and Juris College of Law. Candidates alleged that biometric verification problems occurred at several centres, delaying the start of the examination. Candidates also created a commotion at the centres over the issue. Demand to cancel the first-shift examination The protesting candidates demanded that cancelling the examination at only a few selected centres would not be enough. They called for the entire first-shift examination for hospital attendant posts to be cancelled. The candidates also shared videos and information related to alleged irregularities in the examination. As soon as they were informed about the protest, police forces from several police stations, including Gomti Nagar Extension, reached the spot. The candidates were pacified after being counselled. Candidates said-Why was the technical glitch not fixed? The protesting candidates said they had come to Lucknow to sit the examination from not only Uttar Pradesh but several other states as well. The sudden cancellation of the examination caused them considerable inconvenience. They questioned why the technical glitch was not fixed in time when preparations for the examination had already been made. Examination cancelled at 3 centres Amid the commotion, Dr Vijay Upadhyay, faculty in-charge of SGPGI's Examination Cell, issued an order cancelling the examination at three centres. He cited disruption to the functioning of the examination-conducting agency as the reason. The centres where the examination was cancelled include SDSN Degree College, SDSN Public School and Juris College of Law. New date to be announced later After the examination was cancelled, the SGPGI Examination Cell said that the next date for candidates at the concerned centres would be announced separately. Candidates have been advised to check the institute's official website regularly for updates.

stories.summary: Police arrested Divya, the sister of the prime accused in Lucknow's triple murder case, Rishabh Shukla. She had been absconding since the incident. A reward of ₹25,000 had also been announced for information leading to her arrest. On Sunday, police apprehended her on IIM Road near Kooda Chauraha in Dubagga. A day earlier, police had also arrested her uncle, Rajesh Shukla. Police have already sent seven accused to jail in the case. The incident took place in the Saadatganj area on 26 October. A father, son and uncle from the same family were shot dead over a dispute regarding the construction of a platform. After the incident, Deputy Chief Minister Brajesh Pathak and BJP state vice-president Neeraj Singh met the victim's family. They assured them that strict action would be taken against the accused. The Deputy Chief Minister carried the biers of all three victims. Father, son and uncle were killed in shootings Deputy Commissioner of Police (West) Jitendra Srivastava said the dispute was over the construction of a platform and parking vehicles on vacant land. Because of this enmity, the accused jointly surrounded Shivendra Tiwari, alias Shambhu, his elder brother Shivaji Tiwari and his nephew Suyash Tiwari. The attackers are alleged to have assaulted all three with sticks and stones. They then shot and killed them. Seven accused had already been arrested Several teams were formed to arrest the accused after the incident. Acting on 26, 27 and 31 October, police arrested seven accused. Divya Shukla was wanted in the case. She was also arrested on Sunday. Accused uncle has a criminal record Rajesh Shukla, the uncle of Rishabh Shukla, who carried out the triple murder, already has a criminal record. Police had declared him a goonda and externed him from the district. The family of the murder victims alleges that the uncle is the mastermind behind the accused. Rishabh committed three murders with his backing. Lucknow Police had taken action against Rajesh Shukla seven months ago, on 16 March. The then Police Commissioner, Amarendra Kumar Sengar, declared accused Rajesh Shukla a "goon" and ordered his externment from the boundaries of the Lucknow Commissionerate for three months. DGP met the family on the fifth day after the incident On Friday, the fifth day after the incident, DGP Rajeev Krishna met the family. He met the victim's family. The deceased Shivaji's wife, Usha Tiwari, told him that accused Rishabh Shukla should be hanged and that his absconding uncle and sister should be killed in an encounter. The DGP assured her that action would be taken and justice delivered. After consoling the victim's family, the DGP personally inspected the scene of the incident. What was the case? On Monday morning, Rishabh Shukla (30) shot dead three people in Brahman Tola, Saadatganj, over car parking and a raised platform. The deceased, Shivaji Tiwari (62), was a retired Secretariat employee. He had also served as the RSS district sarkaryavah. Shivaji's brother, Shivendra Tiwari, alias Shambhu, worked at Lucknow University. Shivaji's son Suyash (30) ran a business dealing in electrical goods. He was due to get married on 5 December. The accused, Rishabh, formerly worked for a shipping company.

stories.title: Brij Bhushan calls Rahul Gandhi ‘Bandar Baba’:Says he keeps jumping from one branch to another
stories.summary: Former BJP MP Brij Bhushan Sharan Singh launched a scathing attack on Rahul Gandhi in Baghpat. He said, "The Leader of the Opposition has become like a monkey performing a dance-sometimes on one branch, sometimes on another." "I feel very sad when I see Monkey Baba. I have said little; there is much more to understand. Kings are no longer born from a queen's womb; anyone can become a king through votes." Brij Bhushan arrived at the Kshatriya Self-Respect Conference held at SPRC Degree College at around 1.30 p.m. on Sunday. He appealed to the young people in the community to become aware, educated and organised. Read Brij Bhushan Sharan Singh's 5 key remarks... 1. 'Opposition leaders are dancing like monkeys' “When I see the country's plight, I criticise the young Congress leader the most. He has turned 55 but has not become wiser. If he had played the role of the Opposition properly, the country would have progressed even further.” “Our country has a democracy. In a democracy, there is a role for the party in power as well as for a strong Opposition. But the Opposition leader has become like a monkey dancing.” 2. "It hurts when I see the monkey Baba" “It hurts because my grandfather was a Congress MLA in 1952. He died two years later. This is my grandfather's party. I am not in that party. But because it was my grandfather's party, I sympathise with it. However, it hurts when I see the monkey Baba.” 3. "Cockroaches stage protests on holidays" "The UGC neither came nor will it come. So forget the uproar. Look for the positives now. Do not get caught up with these anger-cockroaches who have come here. They have not come on their own, my brother; they have been sent." “Their protests are not their own. They receive funding from abroad. They stage protests on days when there is a greater possibility of doing business. They protest on holidays.” “The traders wore themselves out trying to explain. We told a senior leader that it was Diwali and asked him to hold the protest two or four days later. He said that they would call the traders and ask them to explain what their loss was. They would explain to the traders that they had suffered no loss and then postpone it.” 4. "Whom Should I Share My Feelings With?" “My brother, whom should I share my feelings with? Who is ready to listen? Who has the time? Everyone is busy with their own affairs; everyone is concerned with their own interests. How long should I remain silent, like a cloud, and endure thunderbolts while speaking? Whom should I share my feelings with?” 5. "Chandrashekhar Is Speaking Because He Has Been Given Security" Targeting Chandrashekhar, Brij Bhushan said, "Oh brother, what can one say about your intelligence? You are saying this because you have been provided security. It is not just you-even if I did the same, I too should not be given government security." Chandrashekhar had said, "I will drag Brij Bhushan Singh out of Vishnoharpur." Advises young people to spend time with successful people Brij Bhushan urged young people to spend time with successful people. He said this has an impact on a person. Sitting with useless people can cause even the things one has achieved to be lost. Referring to his daily routine, he said he oversees the harvesting of paddy in the fields and feeds jaggery to the cow. He makes reels of these activities and uploads them on social media so that other people are also influenced by them.

stories.title: Policeman runs with 2-foot-tall SP worker in his arms:Protesters clash with police for 25 minutes in Lucknow over Gyanesh Kumar
stories.summary: Akhilesh Yadav protested against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar in Delhi on Sunday, while several Samajwadi Party workers held a demonstration in Lucknow. At Hazratganj crossing, the workers raised slogans demanding that Gyanesh Kumar be sent to prison. There was also a heated exchange and pushing and shoving between the police and the workers. As the situation escalated, the police lifted the protesters from the road and put them into vans. Those who resisted were forcibly carried away. One of the protesters, a two-foot-tall party worker, tried to break free, prompting a sub-inspector to laugh as he picked him up in his arms and ran. The workers also accused the police of misbehaviour. See two pictures from the protest... Alleged the theft of 35 crore votes Ganesh, who was protesting, said that Gyanesh Kumar had murdered democracy. "We will remain on the streets until he resigns. The Chief Election Commissioner helped the BJP form governments in different states and at the Centre by stealing more than 35 crore votes." Making the allegation, he said, "Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar and the entire Election Commission, acting at his behest, are working for the BJP. We will not allow this to happen this time, whatever the cost." 'Government formed through vote theft' Protesters said that the Election Commission was dead, had become a BJP stooge and was continuously facilitating fraud. They said these people had looted Bihar and West Bengal and were now preparing to loot Uttar Pradesh. No election would be held in Uttar Pradesh without removing Gyanesh Kumar, they said, adding that the Election Commission had severely weakened democracy. "The opposition had already said that votes were being stolen" Ashish, who was taking part in the protest, said that their leader Akhilesh Yadav had been raising the issue of vote theft for a long time. "We have provided evidence of vote theft several times, yet the Election Commission did not take note of it. Now, the way an English newspaper has exposed the Election Commission's true face in the entire matter..." This has made it absolutely clear that the BJP is coming to power only with the Election Commission's collusion. If there had been no Election Commission, the Bharatiya Janata Party would never have come to power.

stories.title: Akhilesh Yadav asks where BJP will plant its foot:Says UP knows how to give a good send-off, arrives at rally in an open-top bus
stories.summary: Samajwadi Party chief Akhilesh Yadav attended the INDIA bloc rally against SIR at Delhi's Ramlila Maidan. Addressing the rally, he said, "Ramlila Maidan has become the Haldighati of democracy today. New history has been written here several times. Change will come once again. The people of Uttar Pradesh know how to give a warm welcome as well as a good farewell." Akhilesh also responded to Home Minister Amit Shah's "Angad's foot" remark. He said, "Those who have come saying that it is Angad's foot know that if there is no land left, where will you place Angad's foot?" Home Minister Amit Shah had said in Lucknow on Friday that the BJP government in Uttar Pradesh was like Angad's foot, which no one could dislodge. Akhilesh also hit back at the Uttar Pradesh BJP's statement that 1.27 crore Hindu votes would be deleted. He said that just as the public meeting was about to be held at Ramlila Maidan, the BJP said in Uttar Pradesh that the votes of 1.27 crore Hindu brothers had been deleted. “This is the impact of the rally at Ramlila Maidan. The truth is that they want to shift the blame for their defeat onto someone else,” he said. Earlier, he arrived at the rally in an open car along with several leaders, including Akhilesh Yadav, Rahul Gandhi, Mamata Banerjee and Tejashwi Yadav. Akhilesh and Mamata Banerjee were seen sitting next to each other. Leaders of a total of 19 parties attended the rally. The Opposition's march began at Minto Junction at 12 noon and reached Ramlila Maidan at 3 p.m. Here are Akhilesh Yadav's key points. 1- If 1.27 crore votes were deleted, every assembly constituency lost 31,000 votes Akhilesh said, "I can see the voice being raised at Ramlila Maidan. Ever since it was decided that the INDIA bloc and its allies would unite at Ramlila Maidan to raise their voice against all those who have worked to weaken the country's democracy, I hear that they, too, have remembered that they want to join us." “Many of the colleagues from Uttar Pradesh, the state from which I am elected, may have come here. They would know that, just as a public meeting was about to be held at Ramlila Maidan today, the BJP said in Uttar Pradesh that the votes of 1.27 crore Hindu brothers had been deleted.” “Think about the strength of Ramlila Maidan and the voice of the INDIA bloc: even BJP leaders are remembering that their votes, too, have been deleted. If 1 crore 27 lakh votes have been deleted and the figure is applied across 403 Assembly seats, each Assembly constituency has lost 31,000 votes. The truth is that they want to shift the blame for their defeat onto someone else,” he said. 2- If there is no ground left, where will you plant Angad's foot? Akhilesh said, "Those who came saying that this is Angad's foot know that if there is no land left, where will you place Angad's foot? I am pleased that the people of Kashi have given them a double zero, after those who used to talk about a double-engine government." “They were not satisfied with one defeat. Those here would know that the counting continued for two nights and three days. They wanted to use their Chandigarh-style tactic, but they did not succeed.” “The double-engine government has received a double defeat and a double zero in Uttar Pradesh. And which area is that? Those who know it as Kashi also know that it is Kyoto.” 3- BJP knows it can no longer win among the people Akhilesh said that the BJP was continuously plotting and conspiring. It knows that it can no longer win among the people, so it has adopted a route through the Election Commission. Who does not know that the election in Bengal was stolen? No one can forget the images from the Bengal election, when votes were deleted wholesale after forces were deployed in the millions and SIR was conducted before the election. “We in the INDIA bloc are not going to accept defeat. We have caught them and exposed their vote theft. I remember that when the election was held in Uttar Pradesh in 2022, we could not form the government. The reason was that they had stolen votes and removed names from the electoral rolls,” he said. 4-Votes cast in 2019, name removed in 2022 “When the Election Commission was told that you had identified and removed thousands of Samajwadi Party votes, I remember that they issued me a notice asking on what basis I was claiming that thousands of votes had been deleted,” he said. "I remember that our Samajwadi Party workers and PDA sentinels went to each booth to find those voters. There were many people who had voted in 2019 but could not vote in 2022. We formally informed the Election Commission through affidavits, saying, "Look, these votes have been deleted." Not a single complaint by the Samajwadi Party was acted upon. No action was taken against anyone," he said. 5-Ramlila Maidan has become the Haldighati of democracy “Looking at the massive crowd and public support, I can say that the Ramlila Maidan has become the Haldighati of democracy today.” "This is the Haldighati of democracy, and new history has been written on this ground several times. I can say that the public support being witnessed here will bring change once again. These slogans of revolution are proof that change could come at any time." We want to tell you that those who once came from Uttar Pradesh will leave Uttar Pradesh itself. People from Uttar Pradesh are good at welcoming others, but they give an even better send-off. Somewhat of a send-off was given in the Lok Sabha, but in 2027 there will be such a send-off that the BJP and its allies will not be able to return. “Remember, this is the ground of Ramji's Ramlila. We have seen in the Ramlila that the wicked are destroyed. Those sinners will not be able to escape in front of Ramji. Not only are they going to be destroyed, but those who have stolen Ramji's money, those who have stolen donations and those who have stolen offerings will certainly be destroyed. This time, total destruction is on the way,” he said. 6-Neither Moochhua nor Jumlu will survive “The truth is that ever since it emerged that 1.27 crore votes had been cut in Uttar Pradesh, they have been blaming the people of Delhi in their minds. They know they are going to lose. They do not want to take responsibility for the defeat and want to pin it on the people of Delhi,” he said. People say that the Chief Election Commissioner is the biggest link in this chain. A company in the country is also supporting that link. Think about how big a conspiracy is being planned. “We people of Uttar Pradesh have seen the Moochhua come before. This time, the votes have come as Moochhua. And these are Vote Moochhua and some Jumlu as well. This time, neither Moochhua nor Jumlu will survive. Both of them are coming to an end,” he said. 7- Inflation is breaking records; tell us where the rupee stands today “This time, their end is approaching because of the record-breaking inflation that you and I are witnessing today. Those who once asked where the dollar and the rupee were headed should say where we stand in the world today. Those who were talking about becoming a global leader are manipulating their voter lists,” he said.

stories.title: UP woman to become Jain nun after quitting law career:Cuts family ties, gives up luxury life and vows lifelong celibacy
stories.summary: Seven young women in Saharanpur are set to renounce worldly life and become Jain nuns. They include Prakhar Didi and Rangoli Didi. Both had successful careers. Prakhar practised law in London. She was also offered the opportunity to become a judge, but turned it down to pursue the path of spiritual practice. Rangoli, meanwhile, worked as a chartered accountant (CA) in Kolkata for around 10 years. A procession was taken out on Saturday, accompanied by band music and chants in praise of Jainism, to mark Prakhar and Rangoli's vows of renunciation. The procession reached Jain Bagh Temple, where the traditional ‘god bharai’ ceremony was performed. The Shramani Aryika Diksha Mahotsav will now be held at the Sonagiri pilgrimage site in Madhya Pradesh on 22 November. See two pictures... Selected for a judge's post in London, but chose the path of spiritual practice Prakhar, the daughter of Jitendra Kumar Jain and Jyoti Jain, who live in Saharanpur, studied BA LLB and LLM. After completing her studies, she worked as a senior advocate in London. Her career in law was progressing. During this period, she was also selected for the post of judge, but Prakhar Didi chose the path of spiritual discipline instead of becoming a judge. Rangoli returned from Kolkata Rangoli Didi, the daughter of Jinendra Kumar Jain and Savita Jain, who live in Saharanpur, completed her Chartered Accountancy (CA) studies after earning a BCom degree. She then worked as a CA in Kolkata for around 10 years. Despite having a successful career, she quit her job and chose the path of renunciation. What will happen after she becomes a nun? Life changes completely after a woman becomes a Jain nun, becoming entirely centred on discipline, self-restraint and austerity. Nuns must follow the five great vows. They must also renounce wealth, possessions and worldly comforts. According to tradition, they must travel on foot, use only a limited number of possessions and follow prescribed rules in everything from their diet to their daily activities. Their lives are based on the five great vows: non-violence, truth, non-stealing, celibacy and non-attachment to possessions. Five other girls will also take initiation Jain community president Rajesh Jain said, "Five other girls will also take initiation along with Prakhar and Rangeeli. The decision of these sisters to give up promising careers and material comforts and choose the path of restraint is a matter of pride for the entire community. Their decision to adopt a life of spiritual practice after advancing in education and employment will inspire the next generation." It was an emotional moment for the family members Family members of those seeking Jain initiation and members of the Jain community took part in the Binauli procession. For the families, it was an emotional occasion. The families who had raised their daughters by educating them and nurturing their dreams for the future were now preparing to bid them farewell as they embarked on a new path. There was a sense of separation on one hand, while on the other, the families also appeared proud of their daughters' decision.

stories.title: Lawyer abducted and murdered, body dumped in Kanpur:Former four-time Kalpi Bar Association president lured out on the pretext of handing over a file
stories.summary: The president of the Kalpi Bar Association in Jalaun was murdered after being abducted. Gaya Din Ahirwar (70) was abducted by car-borne criminals from Durga Mandir crossing on the Kanpur-Jhansi Highway on Saturday night. His body was found in Kanpur's Sachendi area on Sunday morning. Gaya Din had been called on the pretext of discussing a case file over the phone. He was kidnapped from there and taken towards Orai. His mobile phone then became unreachable. The number from which he had been called was also switched off. SP Suresh Chandra Rawat said the body had been sent for a post-mortem examination. A land dispute has emerged as a possible motive in the preliminary investigation. Two suspects have been detained and are being questioned. Efforts are under way to recover the car and weapon used in the crime. Two pictures of the crime- He was practising law in civil and criminal cases Son gives a detailed account of the entire incident Gaya Deen's son Harsh said that his father had gone to the Orai court on 31 October to represent a client in a case. While returning from Orai at 3:30 p.m., he called and said, "I am returning from Orai. Pick me up from Munna Full Power Chauraha. I have to go and collect a file from a client near Durga Temple." I took my father to the Durga Temple on my scooter. A white Dzire car was already parked there. It had no rear number plate. Three people were sitting inside. My father had already been speaking to them on the phone. Two of them got out of the back seat and said to my father, "Uncle, please have some tea and snacks. We will give you the file after that." They then made my father sit in the car and drove towards Alampur, crossing on the highway. I followed them on my scooter for quite some distance, but after a while the car went far ahead. I returned home. When my father did not return for a long time, I called him. His mobile phone was switched off. When we could not find out anything, we informed the police about the incident. The police formed a team to investigate. After searching for him throughout the night, his body was found in the morning at Gujaini Park in Kanpur, 80-90 km from Jalaun. Those who carried out this incident and the person at whose behest it was done should be given the strictest possible punishment. Feud had been ongoing over a land dispute Fellow advocate Satish Nishad said Gayadin had been involved in a land dispute with a woman named Aparna since 2000. The cases were pending before the Civil Court in Kalpi and the Consolidation Court in Orai. In one of these cases, Aparna had secured a ruling against Gayadin. Gayadin challenged the lower court's order in the higher court and filed an appeal. After the hearing, the lower court's order was quashed, and the case was sent back to the Civil Court in Kalpi for a fresh hearing. Meanwhile, Aparna sold the disputed land to Inderjeet Yadav, a resident of Mainpuri. Once the court was informed of the matter, Gayadeen obtained a stay order. A date was set for a further hearing in the matter. The dispute was over around 4 hectares of land Satish said the disputed land was covered by the Zamindari Abolition Act. It comprises around 4 hectares in Gata Nos. 565, 566 and 576, located in Mauza Hasa in the Kadaura area of Kalpi tehsil. After Gayadeen obtained a stay order on the land, Indrajeet Singh Yadav, a resident of Ghanshyampur in Mainpuri, filed an application in the High Court. It was argued that Gayadeen is the president of the Kalpi Bar Association. In such circumstances, a fair hearing in the Kalpi court could be affected. On this basis, he had sought the transfer of the case to another court. The case was subsequently transferred from Kalpi to the court in Orai. Next hearing in SC-ST Act case on 11 November Satish said that in another case, Gayadeen Ahirwar had lodged a case under the SC-ST Act on 3 October against Inderjeet, his wife Savita Yadav and several others, accusing them of assault. The hearing in the case was held on Saturday, 31 October. After the hearing concluded, the court fixed 11 November for passing its order. On Saturday, after appearing for the hearing at the Orai court, Gayadeen Ahirwar was returning when the incident took place.
