stories.summary: Bageshwar Dham head Dhirendra Shastri has apologised with folded hands for his remark describing Lord Krishna as ‘crooked’. He said Lord Ram and Lord Krishna are one and there is no difference between them. His comment was not intended to create any division or discrimination. He apologised if his remarks had hurt anyone's sentiments. On October 29, during a Ram Katha in Karera, Shivpuri, Dhirendra Shastri had said, “Our Ram is straight, while your Krishna is crooked. Your Thakurji's head is crooked, his name is crooked, and even the way he walks and stands is crooked.” Saints in Mathura express anger over Dhirendra Shastri's remark Saints in Mathura had expressed anger over Dhirendra Shastri's statement. Dinesh Falhari Maharaj said that even Ravana's arrogance did not last forever and that Dhirendra Shastri should apologise. Sadhvi Indulekha and Pandit Rajesh Pathak also expressed displeasure, saying that people from Braj would not tolerate such remarks. Dhirendra Shastri says, ‘Your Lord bends his waist and even his head’ Pandit Dhirendra Shastri told devotees attending the Katha, “Just look at a single picture of your Thakurji. Look at how he sits... in different postures. Your Lord stands bent at three places, with one foot over the other, his waist bent and his head tilted in different ways, while playing the flute.” Comparing Lord Krishna with Lord Ram, he said, “Our Lord stands perfectly straight. His name is straight, his walk is straight, and even his appearance is straight. Your Lord's name is crooked, his walk is crooked, and he even stands crooked.” ‘Playing the flute is child's play, but shooting an arrow is not’ While comparing Lord Ram and Lord Krishna, Pandit Dhirendra Shastri also referred to playing the flute and shooting arrows. He said, “Playing the flute is child's play, but shooting an arrow is not.” He then told the devotees, “All those who worship Thakurji are present here. Today, you must be very happy.” Pointing towards a flute player performing at the event, he said, “Listen, what does your Thakurji do? Play the flute? Playing the flute is not a big deal.” Shastri says, ‘Artists here can also play the flute’ He said, “Grazing cows is child's play, but making monkeys dance is not. Playing the flute is not a big deal. Artists here can also play it. Look, he is playing it too.” He then asked the flute player to continue, and the musician played for a while. Pandit Dhirendra Shastri also asked devotees who worship Lord Ram to raise their hands. He said, “How many of you worship Ramji? Raise your hands. Yes! Today, you will be overjoyed.” He repeated that playing the flute was child's play, but shooting an arrow was not. ‘Grazing cows is child's play, but making monkeys dance is not’ Pandit Dhirendra Shastri also referred to Lord Krishna grazing cows and lifting a mountain. He said people would argue that their Lord grazed cows. Responding to this, he said anyone could graze cows. He sang, “Grazing cows is child's play, but making monkeys dance is not.” ‘Grazing cows is child’s play, but making monkeys dance is no game’ Pandit Dhirendra Shastri also referred to Lord Krishna grazing cows and lifting a mountain. He said people would argue that their God grazed cows. Responding to this, he said anyone could graze cows. Singing a line, he said, “Grazing cows is child’s play, but making monkeys dance is no game.” He then referred to Lord Krishna lifting Govardhan Hill and said, “You will say that your God can lift a mountain. Is that such a big deal? One of our Lord’s disciples blew away an entire mountain.” He was referring to Lord Ram’s devotee, Hanuman. At the end of his remarks, Dhirendra Shastri denied being opposed to Lord Krishna. He said, “This does not mean that we are against Thakur Ji.” Dhirendra Shastri says, ‘I said it out of love’ Dhirendra Shastri clarified his remarks. He said, “I said that Krishna Ji is crooked and our Ram Ji is straight. What is wrong with saying that? Thakur Ji is crooked, isn’t he? I said it in that spirit. Even my name includes Krishna. When you love someone deeply, you say such things to them. I said it out of love.” Referring to Lord Krishna lifting Govardhan mountain, he said, “You will say that your Lord lifts mountains. Is that such a big deal? A disciple of our Lord lifted an entire mountain and flew away.” He was referring to Lord Ram's devotee Hanuman. Supriya Shrinate says calling Thakurji ‘crooked’ is a sin Congress national spokesperson Supriya Shrinate said, “Was dividing people not enough that now they have started dividing their revered deities too?” She said Lord Ram is Maryada Purushottam (the ideal of righteousness), while Lord Krishna is a complete yogi. Both are incarnations of Lord Vishnu. Lord Ram incarnated in the Treta Yuga, while Lord Krishna appeared in the Dwapar Yuga. Both represent truth and justice. Calling Thakurji crooked is a sin.

stories.title: ‘Ram temple stands at very site allotted by the SC’:Apex court rejects plea seeking an inquiry, tells petitioner to approach civil court
stories.summary: The Supreme Court refused to hear a petition challenging the location of the land on which the Ram Temple was built in Ayodhya. On Monday, the court told the petitioner to approach a civil court in the matter. The petition questioned whether the Ram Temple had been built on the same land that the Supreme Court had ordered to be handed over in its verdict. The petitioner sought verification based on land records and other documents. The plea urged the Supreme Court to set up an independent committee or commission for this purpose, comprising qualified experts in surveys, revenue records, archaeology and other technical fields. On November 9, 2019, a five-judge Constitution Bench of the Supreme Court delivered a unanimous verdict in the Ayodhya Ram Janmabhoomi-Babri Masjid dispute, directing that the disputed land be handed over to a trust for the construction of the Ram Temple. The court had directed the Central Government to allot five acres of alternative land to the Sunni Waqf Board at a ‘prominent’ location in Ayodhya for the construction of a new mosque. Ram Lalla's Pran Pratishtha was held on January 22, 2024 Construction of the Ram Temple began on August 5, 2020, with the bhoomi pujan ceremony. Under the supervision of the Shri Ram Janmabhoomi Teerth Kshetra Trust, the sanctum sanctorum and the first floor of the temple were built. The pran pratishtha of the idol of Ram Lalla in his child form was held on January 22, 2024. PM Narendra Modi was the chief host of the rituals at this historic ceremony. After the pran pratishtha, the Ram Temple was opened to the public. Land allotted for the mosque, but not a single brick has been laid yet Five acres of land was allotted in Dhannipur, 25 km from Ayodhya, for the construction of a new mosque to replace the Babri Masjid. The Indo-Islamic Cultural Foundation was subsequently formed to oversee the mosque's construction. In August 2021, the foundation appealed to the public for donations and made its bank account details public. By November 2022, the trust had received donations of around ₹40 lakh from across the country. However, not a single brick has been laid for the mosque's construction so far. Grass has grown on the land allotted for it. The plot is fenced on all sides, and children play cricket there.

stories.title: Azam arrest case:SC refuses urgent hearing; CJI Surya Kant says matter will be listed this week, ED arrested him after jail release
stories.summary: The Supreme Court declined to hear a petition challenging the Enforcement Directorate's arrest of Samajwadi Party leader Azam Khan. However, the hearing is expected to take place this week. On Monday, a three-judge bench headed by Chief Justice of India (CJI) Suryakant said, "The petition may be listed this week." A special court in Ghaziabad had sent Azam to 14 days' judicial custody on Sunday. On Saturday, Enforcement Directorate (ED) officials arrested Azam Khan at the jail gate as soon as he came out. After lengthy arguments, the ED took him to Ghaziabad. Meanwhile, the MP-MLA Special Court will hear the plea for Azam's police custody remand at noon on Monday in a case linked to Rampur's Jauhar University. The court will also decide whether he will be brought from Dasna jail in Ghaziabad to Rampur or produced via video conference. Azam is currently in judicial custody. The case was registered at Ajimnagar police station in Rampur on 13 October on the basis of a complaint by the Enforcement Directorate (ED). It includes allegations of the alleged misuse of government funds and financial irregularities in the construction of the university. The investigating officer has asked the court to issue a remand warrant to question Azam. See two pictures... Case registered based on the ED's complaint Five parties, including Azam Khan, the Maulana Mohammad Ali Jauhar Trust and SS S Enterprises, have been named in the case registered on the Enforcement Directorate's complaint. The complaint alleges the suspected misuse of government funds and financial irregularities in the construction of Jauhar University. The investigating officer filed an application on 29 October The case is being investigated by Tanda Circle Officer Pankaj Pant. On 29 October, he personally submitted an application to the MP-MLA Special Court seeking permission to take Azam Khan into custody and question him. The court summoned Azam Khan while fixing 2 November for hearing the application. Additional Superintendent of Police Anurag Singh also confirmed that the application had been filed. ED took him into custody as soon as he came out of jail Azam Khan came out of Rampur jail on the evening of 31 October after being granted bail in two PAN card cases. During this time, the ED took him into custody. He was produced before the special PMLA court in Ghaziabad on 1 November, which sent him to jail in judicial custody. Lawyers will raise the issue of him being taken into custody earlier According to Samajwadi Party city president Asim Raja, Azam Khan's lawyer will question in court why he was taken into custody on 31 October and taken to Ghaziabad when 2 November had already been fixed for the hearing on the remand application. Azam Khan's lawyer, Nasir Sultan, also said that he would present their side in court. The court's order after the hearing is now awaited.

stories.title: Railway officer found dead in office chair:Sleeping pills found on table; mother and wife allege seniors harassed him in Agra
stories.summary: A 30-year-old officer died by suicide at the DRM office of the Agra Railway Division. Abhishek Singh was posted as an Assistant Operations Manager (AOM). His body was found on a chair inside his chamber. Abhishek had gone to the office on Sunday because the PET examination was being held. When he did not return home by late at night, his family began looking for him. They called the office, following which his colleagues went to his chamber. The chamber was open, and Abhishek was found dead on his chair. Foam was coming from his mouth. Sleeping pills were lying on the table. As soon as they learnt about the incident, his family rushed to the office. His mother fainted upon seeing her son's body and was admitted to hospital. His wife, Aastha, alleged that senior officers had been harassing her husband. Police reached the DRM office after being informed about the officer's death and sent the body for a post-mortem. According to the police, a two-page suicide note was found near the body. In it, Abhishek did not hold anyone responsible for his death. Meanwhile, railway employees were furious when they learnt about the incident on Monday morning. They staged a protest outside the DRM office, raising slogans such as ‘Stop exploiting employees’ and ‘Send the officers to jail’. The employees relented after senior officers tried to pacify them. See some pictures… He was the only son in the family and had been under stress AOM Abhishek Singh was the only son in his family. He had been transferred from Prayagraj to Agra just three months ago. He lived with his wife and children in government accommodation on the DRM office campus. His family comprises his wife, Aastha, mother, Sushila, and two children. His son was born just four months ago. His home is about 200 metres from his office. According to reports, Abhishek had been under considerable stress for quite some time. He took a diary from home to the office but never returned Abhishek arrived at the office on Sunday morning. At 3 pm, he went home and returned to the office with a diary. He did not return home after that. When he had still not returned by 9 pm, his family became worried. They called him, but his mobile phone was switched off. They then contacted his colleagues and informed them that Abhishek had not returned home. Mother and wife break down in tears on seeing his body A short while later, his colleagues informed the family about Abhishek’s death. On hearing the news, his family rushed to the office. On seeing his body, his wife, Aastha, and mother, Sushila Devi, broke down in tears. News of Abhishek’s death caused a commotion at the DRM office. Police and a forensic team arrived at the scene and began an investigation. Wife says, ‘Officials used to threaten to ruin his life’ His wife, Aastha, said senior officers had been harassing her husband. Abhishek would tell her that everything would be fine again. He also said that he was not being allowed to attend training. His name had been selected twice, but his training was cancelled on both occasions. Aastha said the officers constantly reprimanded Abhishek. He would tell her that he was struggling to do the job and that it was very difficult. He said he was frequently scolded at the office. She advised him to ask the officers for some time to understand the work, but they were not willing to give him any time. They would say that he had already been given enough time and threaten to ruin his life. Aastha said she would try to console her husband and tell him not to worry. She would suggest that if he was unable to manage the job, he should quit. They could return to their village, where he could find a private-sector job. Mother says, ‘I have lost my only support in life’ His mother, Sushila Devi, said her son was made to do a lot of work at the office and was subjected to severe harassment. They would threaten to send him to the South. He was not even granted leave. “He was my only support in life. Who will I depend on now?” she said. Left behind a two-page suicide note ACP Sadar Ameesha said the police found a two-page suicide note on the deceased. In it, he did not hold anyone responsible for his death. The note read, “I could not be a good son and husband. I am unable to balance society and my job. I am not fit for this job. Please forgive me.”

stories.title: Builder arrives to demolish Ustad Bismillah Khan’s house:Family protests in Kashi, demands documents; museum to be built with consent
stories.summary: A museum will be built in the three-storey ancestral house of Bharat Ratna Ustad Bismillah Khan in Varanasi. On Sunday, when a builder arrived to carry out demolition work at the house, the family members opposed it. They demanded that the builder show documents related to the demolition and administrative permission. As the dispute escalated, the police were called. Officials initially tried to resolve the matter at the spot. When their efforts failed, both parties were called to the police outpost, where a settlement was reached. Gazi Abbas, the great-grandson of Bismillah Khan, said a museum would be built in memory of his great-grandfather on the second floor of the house, covering an area of 15 × 15 feet, or 225 square feet. Visitors will be able to see the maestro's personal belongings and memorabilia there. Khan Sahib's belongings will be preserved in the museum. For now, they are being moved to another part of the house. What is the dispute about? Ustad Bismillah Khan had five sons and three daughters. After his death, his legacy was inherited by his second son, Nayyar Hussain. However, the house is registered in the name of his eldest son, Mehtab Hussain. Nayyar Hussain Khan's family currently lives in the house and comprises 35 members. Bismillah Khan's grandson, Gazi Abbas, said, “There has been a dispute for the past 10 years between my father, Nasir Abbas, and Mohammad Sibtain, the son of my eldest grandfather, Mehtab Hussain. When the builder arrived on Sunday, we protested. The police then arrived, and both parties were taken to the police outpost, where their sides of the dispute were heard. Now, work has been allowed to begin with mutual consent.” Police officer says peace prevails at the site Chowk police station in-charge Vijay Kumar Shukla said, “The matter is a civil dispute. Both parties have been instructed to maintain peace and follow the due legal process. The party raising objections has been advised to present its case before the court and seek appropriate relief. At present, peace prevails at the site.” Played the Shehnai from the Red Fort on Independence day After India gained independence, Prime Minister Jawaharlal Nehru hoisted the national flag from the ramparts of the Red Fort for the first time on August 15, 1947. On that day, Bharat Ratna awardee Ustad Bismillah Khan played his shehnai from the Red Fort, conveying the message of freedom to the nation through his music. Bismillah Khan received the country's highest civilian honour, the Bharat Ratna, along with the Padma Shri, Padma Bhushan and Padma Vibhushan. He also received awards from across the country. However, he never left Kashi. Municipal corporation to build museum Municipal Commissioner Himanshu Nagpal had said, “It is a matter of pride for Kashi that several Bharat Ratna, Padma Shri, Padma Bhushan and Padma Vibhushan awardees have been born here and continue to live here. The Municipal Corporation has drawn up a plan to develop the areas where these great personalities studied, lived and spent their lives. “We will improve the roads, footpaths, lighting and facades (the main fronts of buildings) in these areas and make them more beautiful. We have arranged a fund of ₹30 crore for this purpose. The lanes leading to their houses will be renovated, and their homes will be converted into museums.” What will the museum house? The Municipal Commissioner had said that Ustad Bismillah Khan's room would be converted into a museum and preparations for it had been completed. Everything associated with the maestro will be preserved there, including his cap, umbrella, lantern, shehnai, hand fan, box, slippers, pen and other personal belongings.

stories.title: 6 killed, including father and 2 sons, in Kushinagar:Trailer collides with Eeco van; victims were returning from Tilak ceremony
stories.summary: A head-on collision between a trailer and a Maruti Eeco van in Kushinagar killed six people, including a father and his two sons. Two children were seriously injured in the accident. All of them were returning from a relative's tilak ceremony. The accident triggered chaos at the spot. The collision was so severe that the van was completely mangled, trapping all eight occupants inside. The impact produced a loud bang. The trailer's cabin was also damaged and twisted, while parts of the van were scattered across the road. The front portion of the van was crushed and pushed back towards the seats. Acting on information from passers-by, police reached the spot and used gas cutters to remove the van's doors and rescue those trapped inside. The bodies were sent for post-mortem, while the injured were taken to the district hospital for treatment. The accident took place around 11.30 pm on Monday on National Highway-28, in the Hata Kotwali area, about 46 km from the district headquarters. The deceased have been identified as Ramvilas Prasad (65), his elder son Kanhaiya Prasad (40), younger son Ram Milan (35), neighbour Mridul Mishra (37), nephew Ranjay (35), and driver Mithilesh (22). Accident occurred 45 km before their home It is learnt that music was playing at full volume inside the van. Meanwhile, about 45 km before reaching home, the van collided head-on with an oncoming trailer near Tharuadih village on the Hata-Pipraich road, under Hata Kotwali police station limits on NH-28. Village head's father-in-law and driver suffer severe head injuries The collision produced a loud bang, and the van was completely crushed. Mithilesh, who was driving the van, and Ramvilas, who was sitting in the front, suffered severe head injuries. Kanhaiya Prasad, Ram Milan, Mridul Mishra and Ranjay Gupta, who were sitting in the rear seats, sustained injuries to their heads and faces. Six people died on the spot, while Ayush and Aryan remained trapped inside the van, crying out in pain after sustaining injuries. The trailer veered off the road following the collision. Its driver fled the spot after the accident. Acting on information from passers-by, police reached the spot, rescued the two injured children and sent them to the district hospital. The bodies were later taken out of the wreckage and sent for post-mortem. CRPF Jawan had come home on leave Ranjay, who lost his life in the accident, was a CRPF jawan posted in Chhattisgarh. He had come home on leave for Dussehra and was scheduled to return to duty on November 5 after his leave ended. However, the accident took place before he could return. He is survived by two daughters and a son. Mridul Mishra (35), son of Narmada Mishra, is survived by a son and a daughter. He worked in agriculture and lived with his family. Van driver Mithilesh Gupta was unmarried. He ran a roadside stall selling chow mein and burgers at a local intersection. He also owned the Eeco van, which he used for bookings. The accident has plunged the village head's family into grief. Mridul's children are inconsolable, while the van driver's mother repeatedly faints while crying. ASP Siddharth Verma said: "A truck and a van collided head-on last night. The two injured people have been sent to Gorakhpur's BRD Medical College. The bodies of the deceased have been sent to the mortuary for post-mortem."

stories.title: Arnab cyclone brings 8°C drop in UP temperature:Late-night rain in Varanasi; fog blankets over 10 districts in the morning
stories.summary: Rain over three consecutive days under the impact of Cyclone 'Arnab' has intensified the cold in Uttar Pradesh. Daytime temperatures have fallen by up to 8°C. Lucknow meteorologist Atul Kumar Singh said daytime temperatures would rise by 5°C to 7°C over the next week. Night-time temperatures will fall by 4°C to 6°C. Light fog covered more than 10 districts, including Saharanpur, in the morning. On Sunday night, Varanasi received heavy rain. In the morning, fog covered 10 cities, including Lucknow, Saharanpur, Shamli, Baghpat and Muzaffarnagar. The roads appeared deserted, and visibility was reduced to just 50 metres. October received 14% more rain than average Uttar Pradesh received 32.1 mm of rain in October, against the average estimate of 28.2 mm, according to the India Meteorological Department. This was 14% more than the average. Light fog is likely in some places in the morning now. Rain likely in eastern Uttar Pradesh in November According to the weather department's forecast, most parts of eastern Uttar Pradesh are likely to receive normal or above-normal rainfall. In western Uttar Pradesh, however, below-normal rainfall is expected. Maximum and minimum temperatures in eastern Uttar Pradesh may remain normal or slightly below normal. In contrast, temperatures in western Uttar Pradesh are expected to remain above normal. In October, the state's average temperature remained slightly above normal, while rainfall was recorded as normal due to western disturbances and cyclonic activity. See the graphics for Uttar Pradesh's 5 coldest districts See the graphics for Uttar Pradesh's 5 hottest districts Exercise caution while sowing and irrigating rabi crops In view of the possibility of rain in November, farmers have been advised to remain vigilant in managing rabi crops. Particularly in Purvanchal, ensure proper drainage in the fields while sowing wheat, gram, peas and mustard. Waterlogging in low-lying fields can damage crops. Avoid unnecessary irrigation in fields where there is sufficient moisture due to rain. Decide on sowing and irrigation only after assessing the weather conditions and moisture in the soil. CM says: Provide farmers with immediate compensation for crop losses Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath has taken serious note of the crop damage caused by excessive rainfall and Cyclone Arnab. He has directed all district magistrates in the state to visit the affected areas and ensure an immediate assessment of the crop losses. The CM said there should be no delay in providing compensation to the affected farmers. Even if the crop damage exceeds the prescribed compensation limit, necessary action should be taken to provide relief to the farmers.

stories.title: BJP national president to lead 'padyatra' in Gorakhpur on 4th:Party leaders prepare roadmap; state president says march will counter opposition’s anarchy
stories.summary: Under its "Save Democracy, Remove Anarchy" campaign, the BJP will organise a march from 3 to 5 November. As part of the campaign, BJP national president Nitin Nabin and Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath will participate in the march to be held in Gorakhpur on 4 November. A meeting was held at the party's regional office in Ranidih on Sunday evening, chaired by state BJP president Pankaj Chaudhary, to prepare for the march. The state president said the Opposition was spreading anarchy in the country. He said there was a conspiracy to weaken constitutional institutions by putting them in the dock. Through the march, the BJP will present the facts to people across the country and respond to the Opposition's anarchy. The state president said that for some time, a concerted effort had been under way in the country to create confusion in the minds of the people and distrust in the democratic system by raising questions about constitutional institutions such as the Election Commission. The tendency to put constitutional institutions in the dock instead of accepting the people's mandate is not appropriate for democracy. In such a situation, it is the BJP's duty to respond to lies and misinformation with facts by reaching out to the people. He said democracy is not limited to winning elections; upholding and respecting the Constitution and its institutions is equally important. The BJP will firmly respond to attempts to weaken democratic institutions by creating an atmosphere of chaos and distrust on the streets. Pankaj Chaudhary said that instead of discussing the real issues facing the people- the welfare of the poor, respect for farmers, the safety of women, and the future of the youth-the Opposition is engaged in creating an atmosphere of confusion and fear. The purpose of the BJP's Save Democracy campaign march is to reach every street and village and place the truth and facts before the people. This foot march to be held in Gorakhpur will further strengthen the public's faith in democracy and constitutional institutions. Party office-bearers and workers have been called upon to reach every mandal, booth and household and connect as many people as possible with the campaign. Public trust is the BJP's greatest asset, and this foot march will serve as a means of further strengthening that trust. Vinod Rai, regional president of the BJP's Gorakhpur region, said that preparations for the foot march were being made on a large scale. He said the foot march would be a historic programme marked by extensive public participation. He said the public itself would respond through the foot march to the questions and confusion being created among people by the opposition over the democratic process and a fair electoral system. He said the BJP would take its message to the people while reaffirming its commitment to democratic values and constitutional institutions. He said there was tremendous enthusiasm among the general public for the march. In Gorakhpur, the march will begin at MP Inter College and proceed to the statue of Sardar Patel near Golghar Kali Temple. State general secretary and the yatra in-charge/co-ordinator Dilip Patel said the "Save Democracy Campaign" foot march was not merely an event but a commitment to take the truth to the people. The opposition is creating confusion by questioning constitutional institutions, and our workers will respond by going from door to door with the facts. Preparations are in the final stage in all 12 districts of the Gorakhpur region, and workers at every level are highly enthusiastic. On 4 November, the foot march will set a new record for public participation. The meeting was conducted by Rahul Srivastava, regional general secretary of the Gorakhpur region. Those present on the occasion included state vice-president Dr Dharmendra Singh, Kameshwar Singh, MP Ravi Kishan Shukla, Minister of State Vijay Lakshmi Gautam, regional general secretary Dr Bachcha Pandey Naveen, Dr Satyendra Sinha, Bhaskar Nishad, regional vice-president and regional coordinator of the padayatra Ranjit Rai Bade, Jai Prakash Shahi, Yudhishthir Singh, Sanjeev Rai, Radheshyam Pandey, Rajesh Gupta, Krishnagopal Jaiswal, regional ministers Brijesh Ram Tripathi, Harikesh Gupta, Dhruv Srivastava, Sunita Agrahari, Siddharth Shankar Pandey, Vaibhav Pandey, Kanhaiya Paswan, Dr Bandhu Prasad Beldar, Rajesh Pal Chaudhary, district president Janardan Tiwari, city president Ramesh Pratap Gupta, MLAs Pradeep Shukla, Fateh Bahadur Singh and Shalabh Mani Tripathi, Mohan Verma, Deepak Mishra Shaka, Mahendra Pal Singh, Vivekanand Pandey, Ajay Singh, former MP Jai Prakash Nishad, Ravindra Kushwaha, Praveen Nishad, Neelam Sonkar, former minister Jai Prakash Nishad, Gorakhpur district in-charge Ajay Singh Gautam, city in-charge Mahesh Shukla, state executive committee member Rajesh Pandey and others.

stories.title: India’s first urban ropeway to launch soon in Kashi:Bhaskar witnesses trial; cabins every 2 minutes, service stops if wind speed exceeds 60 kmph
stories.summary: The country’s first urban ropeway in Kashi is expected to begin passenger services soon, with 96% of the construction work completed. The 3.85-km route between Cantt and Godowlia has five stations. The journey from Cantt to Godowlia will take just 16 minutes. At present, covering the same distance of around 7 km by auto takes 30 to 40 minutes. An air-conditioned gondola (cabin) will arrive at a station every two minutes. Each cabin will have seating capacity for 10 passengers. The ropeway is expected to provide major relief from traffic congestion to devotees visiting the Kashi Vishwanath Temple and the ghats along the Ganga. During a trial run, a Dainik Bhaskar reporter travelled on the ropeway and got a close look at its technology, safety arrangements and passenger facilities. Read on… Five stations to offer passengers an aerial view of Kashi The ropeway will connect five stations: Cantt, Kashi Vidyapeeth, Rath Yatra, Girijaghar and Godowlia. Designed with modern facilities, the stations will also reflect Kashi’s cultural identity. Their architecture features elements inspired by the Ganga, its ghats and Lord Shiva. Designs incorporating damru and trishul motifs are also being developed. The ropeway journey will give tourists and local residents an opportunity to enjoy an aerial view of the city. Full ropeway journey to cost Rs 50, with Rs 10 fare per station The ropeway will operate for around 16 hours daily, from 6 am to 10 pm. The proposed fares have been set with ordinary commuters in mind. A journey from Cantt to Godowlia will cost Rs 50, while passengers travelling between any two consecutive stations will have to pay Rs 10. Passengers will be able to get off at any intermediate station according to their requirements. Each gondola will accommodate 10 passengers at a time. A total of 153 gondolas manufactured by Swiss company Bartholet are being installed along the route. One of the key features of the service is the short waiting time. A gondola will arrive at each station every 120 seconds, or two minutes. Metro-style entry system with baggage screening before boarding Passengers’ luggage will be screened as soon as they enter the station. They will then have to purchase tickets. Like the Metro, passengers will be allowed to access the platform only after scanning their tickets. A large hall has been built inside the station where passengers can wait for some time during busy periods. The arrangements have been designed to regulate passenger movement and prevent unnecessary crowding on the platform. The ropeway station adjoining Cantt railway station has been designed with passenger convenience in mind. The two-floor Cantt ropeway station will have security checks on the ground floor and ticket counters and a waiting hall on the first floor. Gondolas will arrive on the upper level, from where passengers can board them to travel between stations. Gondolas to travel at speeds of 21–22 kmph The ropeway uses a monocable detachable gondola system, with a maximum operating speed of 6 metres per second, or around 21–22 kmph. When a gondola reaches a station, it detaches from the main cable and slows down to around 0.2 metres per second. This process takes approximately 45 seconds inside the station, allowing passengers to board and get off comfortably. Once it leaves the station, the gondola reconnects to the main cable and resumes its normal speed. Backup system to prevent passengers from getting stranded during power cuts The ropeway is equipped with a backup safety system. If there is a power cut or a fault in the drive system, the backup mechanism will be activated to bring the gondolas to the nearest station. This arrangement is intended to reduce the risk of passengers being stranded mid-route. Anemometers have been installed on all towers to monitor wind speed. If wind speeds exceed 60 kmph, the system will automatically shut down. The system is also designed to minimise sudden jolts caused by wind while passengers are travelling. Gondola doors cannot be opened from inside; helpline will connect passengers to control room Each gondola will have a unique identification number. In case of any problem, passengers will be able to contact the control room directly through a helpline and report the number of the gondola they are travelling in. The doors will not open from inside, ensuring that passengers do not violate safety protocols during an emergency and allowing the rescue team to carry out operations in a controlled manner. The ropeway rescue team has received training in Switzerland. A team from the National Disaster Management Authority (NDMA) has also inspected the facility recently. A team of experts from Switzerland is examining the ropeway’s technical and safety arrangements. Pooja Mishra, head of the company involved in the ropeway project, said several layers of safety measures had been put in place for passengers. Each station and gondola is inspected in accordance with separate standard operating procedures (SOPs). A team of experts from Switzerland is reviewing the technical and safety systems, while safety consultants have also been appointed. Security teams to manage crowds at all five stations Managing passenger crowds will be a key priority once the ropeway becomes operational. The plan includes deploying State Security Force personnel along with private security staff. The trained operations team will ensure that passengers follow safety rules and movement protocols. Special attention will be given to entry and exit arrangements, as well as the boarding and alighting of gondolas, at all five stations. Godowlia station work yet to be completed More than 96% of the Rs 807-crore project has been completed. Section One is fully ready. In Section Two, the Girijaghar station has been completed, while work on the passenger boarding and exit facilities at Godowlia station is in its final stages. The target is to complete the remaining work within the next few days. A team of experts from Switzerland is currently conducting technical inspections. Testing of the automation and Supervisory Control and Data Acquisition (SCADA) systems is also pending. An international-level company is carrying out these checks. Ropeway expected to ease road traffic congestion At present, travelling from Cantt to Godowlia by road takes around 30 to 40 minutes due to heavy traffic and congestion. Once operational, the ropeway will cover the same distance in just 16 minutes. The service is expected to provide significant relief to devotees visiting the Kashi Vishwanath Temple, tourists and local residents. It is also likely to reduce pressure on road traffic in the city's busy areas.

stories.title: Fake rape and molestation cases become a business in UP:Woman says, ‘You just spend the money; ruining lives is my job’
stories.summary: The Dainik Bhaskar investigative team has traced an alleged network in Uttar Pradesh involving women accused of trapping people in false rape and molestation cases to extort money. The investigation found that several women had allegedly turned such cases into a means of earning money. The findings raise questions about how the alleged network operates and why the police have been unable to stop it. The investigation comes amid strong remarks by the Allahabad High Court on false rape cases, with the court observing, “Most rape cases that reach the police and courts are false,” and calling for FIRs against those who file false rape cases. During a sting operation, a woman from Kushinagar claimed to a Dainik Bhaskar reporter that she could frame anyone in a false case in exchange for money. We also reached people against whom the woman had allegedly filed false cases. After extracting land and lakhs of rupees from them, these women reached settlements. First in the investigation: The woman we caught red-handed on camera We received information that 45-year-old Zarina Khatoon from Kushinagar had filed FIRs against several people. She allegedly also got POCSO cases registered with the help of minor girls. We met Zarina in Ramkola Urdahan village in Kushinagar. We spoke to her using a hidden camera. Reporter: A man is troubling us a lot. We wanted to get a false case registered. Zarina: It is the festive season, and the girls are busy with their families. We will get it done once they are free. Reporter: How long will we have to wait? We are in a bit of a hurry. Zarina: The work will be done as soon as we find a girl. (Showing a photograph on her mobile phone) Look, this is Chandrabhan Singh. He was the station house officer (SHO) at Ramkola police station. He has now been transferred, but that is not a problem. I have a good relationship with the new SHO as well. We can get your case registered through him too. Reporter: We have come from Haryana. The boy is very troubled. Zarina: People have influence in their own areas. You will not be able to get anything done here. I have influence here. We will get everything done. (Showing photographs on her mobile phone) Look, a girl's case came up just today. We helped her at the police station. We handle all the work at Ramkola police station. Reporter: Do you work in the police? How much money will we have to pay? Zarina: We are the police station's chowkidar. We help people more than the police do. The girl and the police officers will discuss it and then tell you. Reporter: Someone told us that madam is very helpful. They said the case would be registered if she wanted it to be. Zarina: The police are always after me. Whatever we do, the police will not question us. Reporter: Look, the boy who has come with me wants to frame a husband and wife, who are his relatives, in a false case. The wife has a government job. The relatives want both of them to go to jail so that they can take over the entire property. Zarina: It will be done. Do not worry. (Showing a copy of a false case) Look, read the sections. We got this case registered. We have many options. If I tell the sub-inspector, he will register the case. Reporter: Will you get a rape case registered against this boy as well? It should be something that attracts serious charges. Zarina: Yes. His house will have to be sold, and he will also be sentenced. If an attempt-to-rape charge is added, no one will be able to save him. Reporter: His wife could have filed the case, but she has a government job and does not want to get involved. Zarina: Do not worry. We will get it done. We have already got four cases registered. Everyone is troubled and wants to get them managed. Reporter: Can you not file the case yourself? Zarina: No, I will not file it myself. I am employed, so it could cause problems. I have already got several cases registered. Reporter: The girl will be an outsider. What if she withdraws her statement after the case is registered? We could end up getting trapped instead. Zarina: No, that will not happen. That is precisely what she gets paid for. After the case is registered, we will arrange for her to give a statement before a magistrate. Once she gives her statement, she cannot back out. If she does, she will get into trouble herself. Reporter: What if the other party spends money at the police station? Zarina: They can spend as much money as they want. Nothing will happen. There will be a settlement eventually. (Showing a copy of a case) Look, we got this POCSO Act case registered. Bail is not granted in such cases. Once a statement is given, the person will be convicted. Reporter: Will the girl be an adult or a minor? Zarina: We will get the case filed through a minor girl. The money will be settled at that point. I have not spared even my husband and his friend. They, too, have been ruined by cases. Reporter: What if we cannot find a minor girl? Zarina: We will get a married woman to do it. She called a sub-inspector and said, “I need to get a case registered.” To convince us, Zarina called a sub-inspector at the police station. The mobile screen displayed the name 'Naib Daroga'. When the call was answered, she said, “Hello, sir. What is happening? Are you at the police station or at your quarters? I had some work with you. I need to get a case registered. All right, fine. We will come to the police station itself at 10 am tomorrow morning. He will also pay the expenses, and we will keep receiving money later as well.” Reporter: Look, this boy is afraid to go home. His relatives are beating him up there. Zarina: They must have found his weak spot. If they beat him, he should come to me. Transfer some money into this boy's account now. I will put in whatever is needed for his case. It can be done anywhere in Kushinagar or Deoria. Reporter: We will transfer the money into his account by tomorrow evening or the morning after. How will you arrange the girl who will file the case? Zarina: A girl cannot be found immediately. Someone close to the person is usually approached. I have the courage to speak to the district magistrate, the police chief or the SP. We have already spoken to the sub-inspector. We will get the case registered as State versus the accused. You will not have to fight it. The police will fight it themselves. An agent who agreed to arrange a case out of greed for money Zarina: But you will transfer the money to this boy's account. Yes, whatever money you give him, make sure you ask me how much was spent and where. Reporter: How much money should we transfer to his account now? Zarina: Transfer at least ₹1 lakh. Once the case is registered, you will see that they will call you themselves and ask you to come and settle the matter. Everyone will be ready to fall at your feet. The police have immense power through their pen. Reporter: Your man is asking for ₹3 lakh. Zarina: Not ₹3 lakh right now. Pay some amount first. We will ask you for the rest later, as much as is needed. Once the case is registered, we will send you a copy on WhatsApp. Zarina continued to claim on camera that she had links with the police station. After promising to pay her ₹1 lakh, we left her house. We tracked down the people she had mentioned during the conversation. We found that she had allegedly pressured several people by submitting complaints at the police station and later withdrawn the cases after reaching settlements involving money or land. She had reportedly been running this operation for several years. Victim 1: Ramjeet Kharwar A land dispute led to his arrest in a molestation case Eighty-year-old Ramjeet Kharwar of Ramkola had a land dispute with Murtaza. The two had fought several times. After failing to get his way despite repeated attempts, Murtaza allegedly turned to Zarina Khatoon. Zarina got a molestation case registered against Ramjeet. As soon as the case was registered at Ramkola police station, Ramjeet was jailed for a month. He is now struggling to reach a settlement, and a substantial amount of money is reportedly being demanded. Victim 2: Angad He caught Zarina's son stealing, after which an FIR was registered against him Angad said, “I run a grocery shop. One day, Zarina's son stole something from my shop. A quarrel broke out over the incident. Angered by this, Zarina got an FIR registered against me for attempted rape. When I went to meet her, she demanded money from me.” Victim 3: Ranjit Govind Rao 'She filed a false rape case because I refused to give her a passage.' Ranjit Govind Rao and Zarina Khatoon had a land dispute in Chakawat village in Ramkola, Kushinagar. Ranjit's land lies in front of Zarina's house, which is built behind it. Zarina wanted a passage through this land. A fight broke out over the issue. Zarina got a case registered against Ranjit Govind Rao at Ramkola police station for molestation and attempted rape. Ranjit and Govind Rao began suffering mental harassment. Under pressure, they agreed to provide a passage and also paid money to settle the case. Zarina is not a police station chowkidar but a police informer During the sting operation, Zarina claimed that she was a chowkidar at the police station. We investigated the matter at the station and found that a man named Idrish had previously worked as a chowkidar in Urdahan Masjid Tola, the area where Zarina lives. Idrish died seven years ago. Zarina had been trying to secure the chowkidar's position herself, but later began providing the police with information about everything happening in the area. In this way, she started working as a police informer. Now, Shalini from Agra: She allegedly trapped 11 men in false cases A 26-year-old woman from Agra, referred to as Shalini (name changed), filed rape and molestation cases against three people. The men against whom FIRs were registered in Shahjahanpur, Etah and Agra investigated her themselves and discovered that she had been in relationships with 11 men. Complaints of rape and molestation had also been filed against these men in different districts, but most cases ended in settlements. After uncovering these shocking facts, the men submitted evidence against Shalini to the police. The police sent her to jail, but she was later released on bail. We reached young men who said they had been harassed by Shalini. Pawan (name changed), from Shahjahanpur, was studying while living in a rented house in Etah. One day, Shalini, who lived on the floor above him, called him to her room and said that the internet on her mobile phone was not working. When Pawan visited her, she gave him her mobile number. The two then began talking. One day, Shalini suddenly demanded ₹50,000 from him. When he refused, she threatened to frame him in a rape case. Frightened, Pawan transferred ₹10,000 to her. Shalini then demanded ₹1 lakh. When he refused to pay, she got an FIR registered against him at Sikandrabad police station. During a video call, Shalini proposed that she would settle the case in exchange for ₹2 lakh. Pawan approached the police and conducted his own investigation. He discovered that Shalini had filed similar cases against 10 other men. Police action: The police registered an FIR against Shalini and sent her to jail. She is currently out on bail. The Bhaskar investigation revealed three key findings: These issues have come before the courts. The Supreme Court suggested that the government consider amendments. How are these women able to get false FIRs registered so easily? We discussed the issue with Alok Singh, a senior advocate in Lucknow. He said that Section 166A of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) states that if a police officer refuses to register an FIR after receiving information about sexual offences against women, such as rape or molestation, the officer can face criminal proceedings. stories.title: Labrador dog chases away leopard in Uttar Pradesh:Chased it for up to 50 metres after it entered the house boundary
stories.summary: A Labrador dog chased away a leopard after it entered a house in Uttar Pradesh's Lakhimpur Kheri district. The dog not only confronted the big cat but also chased it for nearly 50 metres before driving it out of the property. The entire encounter lasted around 18 seconds and was captured on CCTV. The incident took place at around 4.05 am on Wednesday in Manjhra Purab village, under the North Nighasan Forest Range. The leopard quietly entered the house through its main gate and stepped inside the boundary wall. A Labrador sitting inside the premises sensed its presence. As soon as it noticed the leopard, the dog moved towards it and prepared to attack. The leopard initially stepped back after seeing the dog approaching. However, the Labrador continued barking and charged towards the big cat. Faced with the dog's resistance, the leopard turned around and fled to save itself. The CCTV footage of the incident surfaced on Thursday. Leopard entered house looking for prey The house belongs to Gursaheb Singh, who was sleeping with his family when the incident occurred. According to the CCTV footage, the leopard entered the premises quietly at around 4.05 am. After walking a few steps, it stopped and looked around before slowly moving ahead, apparently searching for prey. It was then that the Labrador came face to face with the wild animal. Instead of backing away, the dog stood its ground as the leopard moved towards it. Within seconds, the Labrador began barking and lunged at the leopard without showing any fear. See 3 pictures... Labrador chased leopard for 50 metres The dog did not stop after forcing the leopard to retreat. It continued chasing the animal for nearly 50 metres and drove it all the way outside the main gate. The Labrador returned only after ensuring that the leopard had left the property. The CCTV footage captures the entire confrontation, showing how the dog stood up to the much larger wild animal and forced it to flee. Encounter lasted around 18 seconds The confrontation between the Labrador and the leopard lasted approximately 18 seconds. The sequence of events, as captured on CCTV, was: Family woke up after hearing dog bark The family members were sleeping when the incident took place. They woke up after hearing the Labrador barking. When they checked the CCTV footage, they were surprised to see their pet confronting the leopard and chasing it out of the house. According to local villagers, leopards have been spotted in the area for the past several days. Their repeated sightings have raised concerns among residents. Forest department installs cage to catch leopard Forest Ranger Bhupendra Singh confirmed that the department had received the CCTV footage showing the Labrador coming face to face with the leopard. He said a forest department team had been sent to the spot to assess the situation. Residents have also been advised to remain alert and take precautions. The forest department has installed a cage in the area to capture the leopard. Officials have urged villagers to remain cautious, particularly during the early morning and night hours, when the chances of encountering wild animals may be higher.

stories.title: Criminals shot a constable three times in Varanasi:One bullet hit his hand and two his abdomen; team had gone to arrest arms smugglers
stories.summary: A crime team went to Nariya Tiraha in Varanasi on Friday evening to apprehend arms smugglers. During the operation, three suspected smugglers opened fire at the team, hitting a constable with three bullets. The constable sustained one gunshot wound to his hand and two to his abdomen. He was rushed to the trauma centre and admitted in critical condition. One of the accused was also shot in the left leg during the exchange of fire. A large police force has been deployed at the spot, and the Police Commissioner has also reached the scene. Three teams have been formed to investigate the incident, which took place in Ashutosh Nagar under the Lanka police station area of the Varanasi Police Commissionerate. See 3 pictures… Third suspect opens fire while police question the group The incident took place in Ashutosh Nagar, behind Sunderpur vegetable market. According to information, four constables from the Lanka police station’s crime team reached the spot after receiving a tip-off that arms smugglers were present there with weapons. The team found three young men at the location and began questioning them. Two of them were detained, but the third suddenly opened fire directly at the police personnel. The sudden firing triggered panic at the scene. As shots rang out, police personnel ran for cover. During the chaos, Constable Amit Shukla was hit by three bullets and collapsed to the ground. The shooter fled the scene. Shukla was rushed to the trauma centre, where he is undergoing treatment. Following the incident, police teams launched a search for the attacker. Amit Shukla is a native of Prayagraj Constable Amit Shukla originally belongs to Varkarganj in Prayagraj. His father’s name is Surya Mani Shukla. He has a three-year-old daughter. Shukla has been posted at Lanka police station in Varanasi for the past three years. Before this, he also worked with the Varanasi Special Operations Group (SOG). He has received training from the Anti-Terrorism Squad (ATS).

stories.title: 'You get nothing through shortcuts; money follows, bro...':Ravi Kishan in Lucknow says earn a name; money will follow
stories.summary: Nothing comes from shortcuts, money follows, bro... Build a name, and money will chase you on its own. This was said by Bollywood star and BJP MP from Gorakhpur Ravi Kishan. At the Content Creators Show organised by Dainik Bhaskar at The Centrum Hotel in Lucknow, he urged young people to move forward with hard work, patience and a positive mindset. Young content creators and influencers from different districts across the state took part in the programme. In an exclusive conversation with Bhaskar, he spoke openly about success, struggle, positive content and spirituality. What advice did he give young people? Read the full interview... Question: How do you view this initiative to help content creators progress? Answer: I wholeheartedly commend Dainik Bhaskar for this effort. People from Uttar Pradesh were invited today as content creators. Two hundred people were shortlisted from around 20,000. They were honoured. Some received tickets to Dubai, some to Goa, while others received a cash amount. This is a different kind of encouragement. Content creators are now the face of the country and society. An 'influencer' is someone who influences society and uses their content to showcase their state-One District, One Product; our culture and traditions; Bhojpuri music and folk music; how my road has improved and my village has improved; how this sportsperson is preparing well; how this girl is studying well and her ranking is improving. Whether it is a cinema story, comedy or one of the many other forms, children today are creating content. These people also promote shops in their cities and earn money. If I talk about Gorakhpur, four influencers from there have won. A major industry is being set up there, and countless projects are under way. These people get jobs and promote the city as well. Flyovers are being built, roads are being constructed and new aircraft are operating. The entire country sees what the city looks like at night, what new changes are taking place, and what changes are occurring in villages, localities, schools and hospitals. This is a very major initiative. Question: It took you 35 years to become Ravi Kishan. Young people want success quickly. What would you tell them? Answer: That's wrong! Look, it simply isn't possible. How long does it take us to learn to stand on our own feet from the time we are born? First, we are born, then we crawl on our knees, and gradually learn by falling and getting back up. It takes 25-26 years to complete our education. Everything takes time-whether it is a tree, a plant, a field or anything in nature. If a crop is growing, it takes time. The rains take time to arrive. You have to wait for summer and winter. This is nature's law. There is no instant shortcut, and whatever comes through a shortcut disappears just as quickly. That is why patience is very important. Once you have made up your mind, stay committed, remain steadfast and continue reading. Studying books is important. Educate yourself and read the newspaper every day. When making reels, think about what good things you can offer. What lessons can you give society, your juniors, your area and your villages and rural communities? Do not serve negativity. Likes come quickly with negativity, but do not spread false news. Check and recheck before commenting on anyone. 'Likes come quickly with negativity' Ravi Kishan said that in the pursuit of likes for perhaps just one of your reels, you could ruin someone's career or destroy someone's home. That is why it is also very important to ensure that, in the pursuit of increasing likes and followers, we are not unknowingly ruining someone's life. Negativity attracts likes quickly. If you abuse someone, people immediately like it. If you say something false about someone, people are interested in hearing it. Your followers and likes increase, but you gradually begin to destroy yourself without realising it. You become completely ostracised from society. The future ahead will be very bright because AI and the digital world have arrived. Prime Minister Modi has made India completely digital. If you travel abroad, you have to spend several dollars and pounds to get a SIM card and use the internet. If the cheapest internet in the world is anywhere, it is in India. We must use its benefits to move forward. Question: Your song 'Gucci-Gucci' was released recently. It went viral on the internet and became a sensation. What would you say about it? Answer: Look, I call Gen Z, as people refer to them, the soul of India. The younger generation saw themselves in me. I am fortunate. I thank them for embracing my carefree nature, my mistakes and my slips of the tongue. They liked my Parliament move. They also liked my films and projects such as 'Mirzapur', 'Dhamaal', 'Laapataa Ladies', 'Maamla Legal Hai' and 'Maa-Behan', which was released on Netflix. For the past two years, they have continued to give me blockbusters. The people of this country are giving them to me. Even after doing 760 films, I consider it Mahadev's blessing that people across the country still show us so much love today, and that we receive so much affection from the youth. They like me as I am and appreciate the things that are part of me. I do not make any extra effort for anything. I am the way I am, and I say whatever comes to my heart. I have won the Best Parliamentarian Award, the Best MP Award and the Best Actor Award. My film Laapataa Ladies even made it to the Oscars. Despite these achievements, I remain normal. I do not carry these achievements on my head and go around under any false impression. 'The youth should embrace spirituality; being spiritual is essential' I know that this is a moment, this is the present. Mahadev is giving this prasad, and his damru is beating. As long as the damru beats, everything, including the nagada, will continue to sound. When the damru stops, the nagada will stop too. I know this is the truth. That is why the youth should embrace spirituality. Being spiritual is very important. If you are spiritual, you will not go into depression, attempt suicide or turn to alcohol and drugs. You have to draw on the powers of spirituality. Falls, bad days, death, accidents, sorrow, hardship and illness will continue to come your way, but you will recover from them quickly and move on. If you have spiritual power and the strength of spirituality, even a major blow will hurt you a little less. This happens to everyone, whether they are important or ordinary, because it is a rule of life. Question: You have a dialogue that says recognition is important - "Money follows, bro." Where does this thinking come from? Answer: Name or money? Since childhood, we had thought that we would make a name for ourselves. We did not want to die unknown. I asked only for a name, and once you have a name, money follows. When someone has a name, money seeks them out. People think that this person has become well known, has some talent, and that the entire country is looking for them-so money seeks them out too. If you pursue money first, you will be ruined. Question: At the regional level, many content creators are doing good work to promote their languages and cultures. What should they keep in mind to make a name for themselves, and how should they maintain discipline? Answer: First, respect your parents, respect your teachers, and respect your neighbours and society. Study spirituality, love your country, love India, and love your soil. Remain completely honest towards India and your culture. Do not look for shortcuts; work hard and spread positivity. When you give something good to society, society and the country will themselves honour you greatly. Pursue recognition, and money will automatically follow you. Question: The MLC election results are being announced. What do you have to say about this? Answer: I have not yet been able to see the full result. Whatever happens, it will be for the best. Whatever Mahadev does will also be for the best. If something has gone wrong, it will be discussed, work will be done on it and the matter will be thoroughly deliberated upon. The Bharatiya Janata Party engages in introspection. It spends all 365 days looking for mistakes, then works hard and remains committed to correcting them. Even if something has gone wrong here or there, every effort will be made to rectify it. Heartfelt thanks to Dainik Bhaskar for this effort. You searched for influencers. There are many such departments. We have entered the world of AI and digital technology. You are taking it across the country. Today, your app is number one after Japan. We understand that you will reach great heights. Heartfelt congratulations to the entire Bhaskar team as well! I salute all those associated with the newspaper, app and media-the intelligent young men and women who are working. Keep it up! Continue showing the truth and reality. Continue showing your love for India as well. I request you to ensure that the spirit of love for India is awakened in everyone. Har Har Mahadev! Victory to Mother India!

stories.title: Lucknow's food culture blends tradition with new flavours:Pan-Asian restaurants and contemporary Indian menus attract diners
stories.summary: Lucknow’s food scene is expanding beyond its famous kebabs, biryanis and traditional Awadhi cuisine, with Pan-Asian restaurants, contemporary Indian menus and international cuisines gaining attention as the city marks one year since UNESCO designated it a Creative City of Gastronomy on October 31, 2025. The recognition made Lucknow the second Indian city after Hyderabad to receive the designation, highlighting its rich culinary heritage, while the growing popularity of diverse cuisines and modern dining concepts reflects how diners in the City of Nawabs are exploring new flavours and experiences beyond traditional food. For many, dining out is no longer just about the food. The ambience, the opportunity to discover new cuisines and the experience of spending time with others have also become important. This shift has attracted hospitality groups looking to expand into cities with established food cultures and growing demand for premium dining. One such group is Bellona Hospitality, the hospitality arm of The Phoenix Mills Ltd. It has introduced two dining concepts in Lucknow: Ishaara, which focuses on modern Indian cuisine and inclusive hospitality, and Eight, which offers pan-Asian food. Restaurants bring new flavours to Lucknow Prashant Issar, managing director of Bellona Hospitality and founder of Ishaara, said Lucknow’s growing interest in new cuisines builds on its longstanding appreciation of food. “Lucknow has never needed to prove itself as a food destination. Its culinary heritage speaks for itself. What makes the city particularly exciting today is the confidence with which its diners are exploring new experiences while remaining deeply connected to their traditions. A city that understands and appreciates good food is naturally curious about discovering more. That’s what makes Lucknow such an interesting market for contemporary hospitality,” Issar said. Located at Phoenix Palassio, Eight offers dishes inspired by Japanese, Chinese, Korean, Thai and other Asian cuisines. Its menu includes sushi, dim sum, aromatic curries and wok-prepared dishes, served in a contemporary setting. Ishaara, meanwhile, presents Indian cuisine through a modern approach. Its menu combines familiar regional flavours with dishes inspired by culinary traditions from across the country. The restaurant has also introduced diners to lesser-explored food histories through special showcases featuring cuisines from undivided Punjab and the Maratha kitchens. Ishaara focuses on inclusive hospitality Alongside its menu, Ishaara follows an inclusive hospitality model that creates career opportunities for people with speech and hearing impairments (SHI). The restaurant's team members play a central role in serving guests. Customers are encouraged to communicate with them through simple signs and gestures, making interaction an important part of the dining experience. Issar said the approach reflects the idea that hospitality depends on how guests feel, rather than only on the food served. “True hospitality is ultimately about how people feel, not simply what is served. At Ishaara, our SHI team members demonstrate every day that warmth, intuition and exceptional service transcend spoken words. Their abilities are recognised, their confidence grows, and guests discover a different, often more personal way of connecting. In a city where mehmaan-nawazi is part of its identity, this philosophy finds a natural home,” he said. Together, Ishaara and Eight represent two aspects of Lucknow’s changing dining scene: an appreciation of India's diverse culinary traditions and a growing interest in international flavours. Premium dining expands beyond metros The trend also reflects a broader change in India's hospitality sector, where premium dining is expanding beyond major metropolitan cities. Established cultural centres such as Lucknow are attracting restaurant brands that see opportunities among diners seeking quality food, authentic flavours and distinctive experiences. However, Issar said restaurant brands need to understand local traditions rather than simply replicate concepts that have succeeded elsewhere. “The future of Indian hospitality will not be shaped by metros alone. Cities like Lucknow bring something invaluable to the table: a deep-rooted appreciation of food, a strong sense of identity and an openness to new experiences. Successful restaurant brands must understand and respect that character rather than simply replicate what works elsewhere. The opportunity is to become part of the city’s evolving dining culture, not to change what makes it special,” he said. As Lucknow marks one year as a UNESCO Creative City of Gastronomy, its culinary identity continues to draw strength from both tradition and innovation. Its kebabs, biryanis and age-old recipes remain popular, even as diners explore a wider range of cuisines and dining experiences. The city's evolving food culture shows how Lucknow is embracing new tastes while retaining the nazakat, tehzeeb and mehmaan-nawazi that define its identity.

stories.title: UP ATS arrests 3 suspects linked to Shahzad Bhatti:Planned to kill Army, police personnel and send videos to Pakistan
stories.summary: The Uttar Pradesh Anti-Terrorism Squad (UP ATS) arrested three members of the banned Shahzad Bhatti network in Lucknow on Friday. A foreign-made pistol and 20 cartridges were recovered from them. The gang was operating on the direct instructions of Pakistan-based handler Rana Bhai. They planned to carry out the targeted killing of an Army or police personnel in Lucknow, record a video of it and send it to Pakistan. Accused reached Lucknow via Delhi from Punjab The ATS had received information that some youths from Punjab were planning to attack a major establishment or security personnel in Lucknow. Acting on the information, the ATS arrested four people in Lucknow on 30 October. The arrested accused include Gagandeep Singh, 26, and Rajat Kumar, 19, residents of Amritsar and Gurdaspur in Punjab, Krish, 21, and a juvenile accused. A foreign-made pistol and 20 live cartridges were recovered from their possession. Were lured with ₹3 lakh and the chance to flee to Nepal During questioning, the accused said they were in contact with Rana Bhai, who was in Pakistan, through Instagram, WhatsApp and virtual numbers. After reaching Lucknow on the night of 29 October, they made a video of Lucknow railway station at Rana Bhai's direction and sent it to Pakistan. Videos and locations related to the reconnaissance of several sensitive sites were also found on their phones. Rana Bhai had sent weapons from Pakistan and, through his local network in Lucknow, arranged for them to receive a pistol and 20 cartridges. Around ₹5,000 was sent to them online from Pakistan for travel and expenses. After carrying out the crime and sending its video, they were promised ₹3 lakh and given a plan to flee to Nepal to evade the police. One foreign-made pistol and 20 foreign-made cartridges recovered ADG (Law and Order) Amitabh Yash said that three people linked to the banned Shahzad Bhatti network had been arrested and a juvenile offender had been detained. All of them are residents of Punjab. They were plotting a targeted killing of a police or Army personnel in Lucknow. One foreign-made pistol and 20 foreign-made cartridges were recovered from their possession. They were all in contact with a Pakistani handler, Rana Bhai, through the social media platforms Instagram and WhatsApp. Interrogation of all the accused is under way. Case Registered at ATS Police Station, Preparation for Custody Remand A case has been registered against the accused at the ATS police station in Lucknow under serious sections of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS), the Arms Act and the Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act (UAPA). The ATS will now produce the accused in court and seek their police custody remand to identify the local facilitators who supplied weapons in Lucknow, the sources of funding, the financial trail and others linked to this network.

stories.title: BJP to contest 2027 Assembly polls with Yogi as face:State in-charge says Shah praised him repeatedly; the message is clear to those who understand
stories.summary: BJP national general secretary Vinod Tawde made it clear on Friday that the 2027 Assembly election would be fought with Yogi Adityanath as the party's face. Speaking at the BJP's state executive meeting in Lucknow, he said, "Today, Home Minister Amit Shah has repeatedly praised Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath. Those who are wise will understand the indication." On the issue of discontent among upper-caste voters over the UGC, Vinod Tawde said that the party would reach out to its voters, engage in direct dialogue with them and explain the matter to them. Tawde said: ‘If the BJP does not return to power, conditions will be like those before 2017’ Tawde said, "It is extremely important to tell the people that if the BJP does not form the government in the state, conditions will return to how they were before 2017." He said, "When you speak to a worker, he says that everything is fine, but... this 'but' is what is ruining everything. If half the glass is empty, we should not say that; instead, we must send the message that we will now fill the glass." Referring to the crackdown on crime, he said, "The Congress government had kept Mukhtar Ansari safe in a Punjab jail, but our government fought the matter all the way to the Supreme Court and brought him to a jail in Uttar Pradesh, where he had to live as a prisoner. Houses for the poor are now being built on land seized from mafias such as Atiq and Ansari." 'Flattery or money will not get you a ticket; only those who work will get an opportunity' On ticket distribution and the ambitions of party workers, Tawde said that there was nothing wrong with wanting to contest an election, but the state had only 403 seats. Some people would get tickets, and others would not, but those who did not get tickets would not work against the party. He issued a stern warning, saying that no one would get a ticket through flattering a leader or using money; tickets would be awarded solely on the basis of work. Tawde said, "I have not come only for the elections; I will remain in charge of Uttar Pradesh for the next three years. I will leave Uttar Pradesh only after fulfilling the promise made to any worker who does the work. You can ask workers in Bihar, Maharashtra and Haryana about me." We will not repeat a mistake like '400-plus' Speaking about the role of social media, Uttar Pradesh in-charge Vinod Tawde acknowledged that the BJP had become sluggish on this front. He said, "The Opposition now understands the power of social media. In 2014, we were ahead of everyone on social media, and at the time Lalu Yadav used to ask what difference it made. But today in Bihar, Tejashwi Yadav has more followers than Nitish Kumar. Our social media presence has weakened somewhat; we do not even like or repost the prime minister's and chief minister's posts. Everyone will have to become active on social media because our schemes are not just about development – they are changing people's lives." Speaking about the election target, Vinod Tawde made it clear that the mistake of the slogan 'Abki Baar 400 Paar' would not be repeated in this year's Uttar Pradesh election. He reminded party workers that they had to win 312 seats in the 2027 election, just as they did in 2017. He assured them that he would continue meeting party workers, engage in dialogue with them and find solutions to every problem.

stories.title: Trader writes killer’s name before dying:Reaches a dhaba in Sitapur covered in blood; was on his way to sister’s home for Karwa Chauth
stories.summary: A young trader was kidnapped and had his throat slit in Sitapur. The attackers fled the scene after assuming he was dead. After regaining consciousness, the young man somehow reached a dhaba on the Lakhimpur Kheri-Sitapur border. The blood-soaked young man could not speak because his throat had been cut. Before he died, he wrote the names of the accused on a slip of paper. He pleaded with people to help take him to hospital. The young man died before doctors could begin treating him at the hospital. A police investigation revealed that the young man had left to visit his sister's house on Karva Chauth. His family has filed a complaint against four people, alleging that he was murdered because of an old enmity. Police have detained some people in connection with the complaint. The incident took place in the Pisawan area, 37 km from the district headquarters. See three pictures... Read the full incident in detail... Nitesh Kumar Maurya (24), a resident of Saraiya Mahipat Singh village in Sitapur district, was the eldest of three brothers. One brother, Niket (20), works in Dubai, while the other, Sachin, is 19. Their father, Dinesh Kumar (45), is a farmer. Besides trading in paddy and wheat, Nitesh also ran an RO plant. Nitesh had two sisters, Neha and Khushboo. Khushboo (26) is married. Uncle said - He was going to his sister's house in Lucknow Nitesh's uncle, Harish Kumar Maurya (39), told the police that Nitesh had left home on Wednesday, saying he was going to Bakshi Ka Talab in Lucknow to get something done for his sister. He was also having a house built in Lucknow. For this reason, he left on his bike with a cylinder tied to it. Nitesh's bike found unattended in Barabanki According to Harish Kumar, Nitesh's motorcycle was found abandoned near the Daffarpur crossing in the Baddoopur police station area of Barabanki on Thursday morning. A cylinder was tied to the motorcycle, but Nitesh was not there. Fearing that something untoward had happened, some people said that Nitesh had been abducted by people travelling in a car. A search for Nitesh began after the motorcycle was found, but there was no trace of him. Nitesh wrote on a slip-Manoj is behind my death According to the police, the family suspects that the attackers abducted Nitesh from Baddoopur in Barabanki and took him to the Maigalganj area of Lakhimpur Kheri. They slit his throat near Lidhiyai's turn and dumped him, assuming he was dead. Badly injured, Nitesh somehow reached Pannu Dhaba in Pisawan on the Sitapur border. His throat had been slit, so he could not speak. Nitesh asked the people at the dhaba for paper and a pen. He wrote a plea asking them to take him to hospital. While he was being taken to hospital, Nitesh wrote the name of his acquaintance Manoj on a piece of paper. He also wrote Manoj's father Vidya Prasad's name, along with the village and post office address, Saraiya Mahipat Singh. Nitesh held Manoj responsible for his condition. Nitesh died at the district hospital After receiving information from the roadside eatery, Pisawan police reached the spot. The injured Nitesh was taken to CHC Maholi. His identity could not be established at the time. After first aid, he was referred to the district hospital, where he died at 3:10 p.m. He was later identified as Nitesh Maurya, a resident of Saraiya Mahipat Singh village. Uncle alleges murder over old enmity Nitesh's uncle Harish said he was murdered over an old enmity. According to him, Nitesh had been locked inside a shop and beaten around a year ago. A dispute had been continuing since the incident. Police are now investigating the links between the financial dispute, old enmity and the case ranging from abduction to murder. Manoj Sonkar, Station House Officer of Baddoopur Police Station in Barabanki – A case has been registered in connection with the murder of the businessman, and some suspects have been taken into custody. They are being questioned.
