stories.title: Chandrashekhar says every household should have a lawyer:Accuses government of giving jobs to favourites; attends lawyers’ conference in Lucknow
stories.summary: Azad Samaj Party president and MP Chandrashekhar said at the third advocates’ conference organised by the party’s legal cell (Kanshiram) and the Bhim Army at the Gandhi Bhavan auditorium in Kaiserbagh, Lucknow, on Friday that every household needs a lawyer today, as advocates stand as a strong wall in the legal fight against injustice. He appealed to advocates to rise above caste and religion and support one another, while taking a dig at Amit Shah’s visit to Lucknow, saying, “The meeting will produce some result; otherwise, the public is in the mood to teach them a lesson this time.” He also alleged that the government was giving government jobs to its favourites. See three pictures... Emphasis on advocates' unity Chandrashekhar said that advocates' unity should be very strong. Anyone wearing a black coat, regardless of caste or religion, should be treated equally. He said that advocates facing financial hardship should receive as much support as other advocates. Advocates should stand against injustice while upholding the dignity of their profession. He said that in today's era, a person may face action simply for expressing their views. At such times, advocates come forward to protect that person's rights. 'The country's system is governed by the Constitution' The MP said the country's system is governed by the Constitution. The government, officials and independent constitutional institutions all function under the Constitution. But the question is whether ordinary citizens have adequate knowledge of the Constitution and its ethical values. He said the Constitution should be made part of school and college curricula so that people learn about their rights and duties from childhood. Takes a dig at Amit Shah's meeting and the BJP's preparations Home Minister Amit Shah is in Lucknow today. He is holding a meeting with party office bearers to discuss preparations for the 2027 Assembly elections. Commenting on the meeting, Chandrashekhar said the BJP should hold it because the party's position is not good. He said the meeting would yield some result; otherwise, the public appears determined to teach the BJP a lesson this time. 'Forget protests, people are not even being allowed to meet the victims' Chandrashekhar Azad said that when the Bharatiya Janata Party was in opposition, it used to hold frequent protests, but the situation in the state today is such that, far from being allowed to protest, people are detained even when they go to meet victims. He alleged that in several cases, victim families are not even being allowed to perform their children's last rites. 'The government is giving government jobs to its favourites' Chandrashekhar Azad said the government was giving government jobs to its favourites. He said that anyone could name a recruitment drive in the state in which allegations of a scam had not been made. He said the government wanted to intimidate protesters under the guise of such laws so that voices raised against it could be suppressed. The British had also enacted similar laws to stop movements against them and create fear among the people. The chairman said, 'The police harassed lawyers' Legal Cell national chairman Mohanshyam Maria said that incidents of harassment and attacks on advocates were continuing to come to light in Uttar Pradesh. In several places, advocates were harassed by the police, while in some cases miscreants entered their chambers and even opened fire. He also raised the issue of chairs and seats recently installed for advocates to sit in Lucknow being removed and demolished by the administration. Demand for security of chambers and independent legal representation Maria said advocates are an important link in the Constitution and the democratic system. They work to ensure justice for every person in society, but when those same advocates are concerned about their own safety, it is a serious matter. Through the conference, demands are being raised for better arrangements to ensure advocates' safety, protect their dignity and enable them to represent cases independently. Justice must reach those at the bottom of society Mohanshyam Maria said that a legal cell had been formed under the leadership of MP Chandrashekhar Azad and Bhim Army national president Vinay Ratna Singh to safeguard the rights and security of advocates. Its objective is to strengthen arrangements to ensure accessible and appropriate justice even for those at the bottom of society. The conference is discussing advocates' problems, their rights and various issues related to the judicial system. The event is being organised by Rajneesh Gautam, advocate and state president of the Azad Samaj Party Legal Cell, Uttar Pradesh. Safety and dignity of advocates are the main issues The main objective of the conference is to raise issues related to the dignity, self-respect and safety of advocates. The organisers say that advocates, who play an important role in the justice system, now feel unsafe themselves. They face challenges including the independence of their profession, their livelihoods, the security of their chambers and the ability to represent clients in cases without pressure.

stories.title: Dengue cases nearly double in a month:Varanasi count reaches 112, up from 60 on October 4
stories.summary: The dengue situation in Varanasi remained under control until September, but cases increased sharply in October. According to Health Department data, the district had reported 60 dengue cases by October 4. By October 30, the number had risen to 112. This means 52 new confirmed cases were reported during October so far. The rise comes after dengue cases in September 2026 were 35% lower than in the same month last year. Dengue cases rise in October Health Department data shows that Varanasi had recorded 60 dengue cases by October 4. The number increased to 112 by October 30. The rise in cases after a decline until September has raised concern. 60 patients reach district hospital, 7 cases confirmed In October, 60 patients with dengue symptoms visited Deendayal Upadhyay District Hospital. Tests confirmed dengue in seven of them, while the remaining 53 were listed as suspected cases. The patients underwent initial NS1 tests. A second test is also required to confirm dengue. The reports of these 53 patients are still awaited, so they have not yet been counted as confirmed cases. Cases in September were 35% lower than last year In September 2025, 57 dengue cases were reported in Varanasi, while 37 patients were recorded in September 2026. Thus, there were 20 fewer cases in September than in the same month last year. This represented a decline of around 35%. Most cases among people aged 15 to 59 Of the 60 dengue patients reported by 4 October, the highest number were people aged 15 to 59. There were 51 cases in this age group. Six cases were reported among children aged 0 to 14, while three cases were reported among people over 60. Total cases lower than last year In 2025, 229 dengue patients were reported in Varanasi between January and December. In 2026, a total of 112 cases had been reported by 30 October. So far this year, there have been 117 fewer cases than the total recorded throughout last year. According to the Health Department, 8,890 dengue tests were conducted between January and October, while 10,555 tests were conducted throughout 2025.

stories.title: Rat tied up and burnt alive in Jhansi:Hung from a gate, doused with petrol and set alight; FIR filed against four Muslim youths
stories.summary: An incident of animal cruelty has come to light in Jhansi, where four youths allegedly tied a rat to an iron gate, poured petrol on it and set it on fire. The youths first caught the rat and tied it with a rope. They then hung it from the gate, poured petrol over it and set it on fire. They also recorded the incident on video. After some time, the rope broke and the rat ran around trying to escape. However, it later died from its burns. The incident took place on October 29 in the Kotwali police station area. After the video surfaced, police registered a case against all four youths. DISTURBING VISUALS below : Rat caught using a cage The police said the accused caught a rat using a cage. They then tied it to a rope. Junaid Qureshi, son of Shafiq Qureshi, and Shafiq Qureshi, who live in Kasai Mandi near Orchha Gate under Kotwali police station, beat the rat with sticks. They then hung it from an iron gate. Junaid Qureshi, son of Safiq Qureshi, poured petrol from a bottle over the rat and then set it on fire with a matchstick, burning it alive. During this, Ashif Qureshi, son of Abad Qureshi, recorded a video on his mobile phone. He also spoke about burning the rat. Action taken after video goes viral The accused filmed the entire incident and posted it on social media. The video went viral and reached the police. After investigating, the police gathered the accused's details. The Kotwali police then registered a case on the complaint of Sub-Inspector Rohit Kumar. Kotwal Anjan Kumar said, "A case was registered on the basis of the video, and the accused, Junaid Qureshi, Ashif Qureshi and Shafique Qureshi, have been arrested. The three are being produced in court. One accused is absconding and is being searched for." Committee demands action People are angry after the video of the rat being burnt alive went viral. The accused are being criticised everywhere. Office-bearers and workers of Shri Mahakal Gau Seva Sansthan reached the Kotwali police station and demanded action. They said that such people should be given strict punishment.

stories.title: Akhilesh retorted, ‘Swami Prasad is not part of our alliance’:Says ignore him; announces more tickets for women than BJP in 2027 elections
stories.summary: Samajwadi Party chief Akhilesh Yadav said on Friday that Swami Prasad Maurya was not part of his alliance. During a press conference in Lucknow, Akhilesh lost his temper when asked whether Maurya would join the INDIA alliance. He angrily said that Maurya could not be included in the party's seat-sharing arrangement. "Avoid him. Ignore him. Keep quiet," he said. Making a major announcement on women's reservation for the 2027 elections, Akhilesh said his party would give tickets to more women than the BJP. Commenting on the MLC election results, he said the results had held up a mirror to the BJP. "Those who were making a big show have fallen flat on their faces," he said. He added that although the figures showed only 5 MLC seats, the BJP had lost in 50 districts. The SP chief said, "The message has reached the public that BJP leaders are dishonest. SP candidates have won on the strength of the people. They have won 6 seats through deceit. Had they not resorted to such tactics, they might not even have won this many seats." Asked about Amit Shah's visit to Lucknow, Akhilesh replied, "You have taken too long to arrive, my lord." Maurya joined the INDIA alliance after meeting Rahul Gandhi in Delhi Former minister and Apni Janta Party president Swami Prasad Maurya met Congress MP Rahul Gandhi on 3 October. Maurya announced that he was joining the INDIA alliance. He said discussions on the number of seats his party would contest would take place later. "We want Rahul Gandhi to become the country's next Prime Minister," he said. He had accused the SP of straying from socialist ideology Swami Prasad Maurya had accused the SP leadership of straying from socialist ideology and discriminating against him. His statements on the Ramcharitmanas and the consecration ceremony of the Ram temple in Ayodhya had triggered opposition within the party. Maurya alleged that the party leadership had failed to defend him when party leaders attacked him and opposition to him grew. He left the SP and formed his own party in 2024 After resigning as national general secretary on 13 February 2024, Maurya tried to speak to SP president Akhilesh Yadav, but his frustration grew when no meaningful initiative followed. On 20 February 2024, he resigned from the SP's primary membership, the post of national general secretary and his membership of the Legislative Council (MLC). Two days later, on 22 February 2024, he formed his own party, the Rashtriya Shoshit Samaj Party. Key points from Akhilesh's press conference 1. Women teachers voted unitedly against the BJP Akhilesh Yadav said, "Educated voters in Varanasi and the surrounding areas have handed the 'double-engine' government a 'double zero' this time." Referring to the passage of the Women's Reservation Bill in Parliament, he targeted the Union government and asked why the legislation had not yet been implemented despite being passed. He said women teachers and women voters had therefore united to vote against the BJP in this election. 2. MLC elections are not just a victory but a fight to save democracy Akhilesh referred to the famous statement by former US President Abraham Lincoln: "Government of the people, by the people, for the people." He said the MLC elections were not merely about winning but represented a major fight to save democracy. He added that the party's leaders and workers had proved that they would never allow the people's voice to be suppressed. 3. Biometric verification should be mandatory during elections Akhilesh alleged that around 26,000 primary schools had been shut down in the state, while thousands of new liquor shops had been opened. He claimed that question papers for more than 20 competitive examinations had been leaked under the current government and that recruitment irregularities had taken place. Questioning the impartiality of the Election Commission, Akhilesh demanded that biometric verification be made mandatory during elections to prevent bogus voting. 4. 'Even if we win all 80 seats, we still want ballot papers' Akhilesh once again advocated holding elections using ballot papers instead of EVMs. He said some of the world's most developed and prosperous countries, including the US and Germany, conduct elections using ballot papers. He also claimed that Germany's Constitution considered voting through EVMs unconstitutional. "I have said this on the floor of the House as well. Even if the Samajwadi Party wins all 80 out of 80 Lok Sabha seats, we will still demand that elections in the country be conducted using ballot papers," he said. 5. 'The courage of party workers is the real foundation of victory' Congratulating the candidates who won the MLC elections, Akhilesh said, "I extend my heartfelt congratulations to all our colleagues who have won. I also thank all the voters who placed their trust in the Samajwadi Party." He said the courage and determination shown by party workers in standing their ground during voting and counting had been the real foundation of the victory. 6. On the Varanasi victory, he said the people had stood by the truth Expressing happiness over the results in the Varanasi division, Akhilesh said the people had stood by the truth in an area where the government had made grand claims. He concluded by saying that the victory was only the beginning. As the truth reached more people, the Samajwadi Party's standing was steadily improving, he added. What did the newly elected MLC members say? Read here Dr Man Singh Yadav (Allahabad-Jhansi Graduates' constituency) said the SP workers' strategy had succeeded despite pressure from the government and administration. He promised that the Old Pension Scheme (OPS) would be restored if his party formed the government. Akash Agrawal (Agra Teachers' constituency) alleged that the SP would have won 8 seats instead of 5 if the administration had not indulged in electoral malpractice. Lal Bihari Yadav (Varanasi Teachers' constituency) alleged that the police had raided the homes of his party workers and office-bearers a day before the election and tried to intimidate them.

stories.title: 3 teams investigate crores buried underground:Police reach Pune to probe links; ₹5 crore cash found in a blue drum in Prayagraj
stories.summary: The mystery surrounding crores of cash buried underground in Prayagraj is deepening. Three teams have reached the spot to investigate more than ₹5 crore hidden in blue drums underground. The teams include officials from the Income Tax Department, the police and a bank. Bank employees will count the notes under the supervision of Income Tax officials. Meanwhile, a police team has also been sent to Pune to investigate the case. The investigation teams are trying to find out where such a large sum came from and how it reached Prayagraj. Cash worth crores was recovered from Rakesh Yadav's house in Baraipur village, 32 kilometres from the district headquarters, on Wednesday night. Bundles of ₹500 notes had been wrapped in cloth and buried underground. The recovered amount is estimated to be around ₹5 crore. See three pictures... Bundles of notes were repeatedly brought from Pune The investigation so far has revealed that Rajesh and Rakesh, residents of Nawabganj, used to bring cash worth crores of rupees from Pune to Prayagraj, fill it into drums and then bury them in the ground. A team has also been sent to Pune after questioning the two brothers. The two brothers worked for several years for a jeweller in Pune. They returned to Prayagraj during COVID-19. It is suspected that cash worth crores of rupees was brought here during this period. Investigating agencies suspect that, apart from the three drums, the family may also have hidden bundles of notes in the house, orchard, vacant plot or another property. Police cut off the village's electricity before conducting the raid Rakesh Yadav, also known as Mahakaal, has his ancestral house in Baraipur village in the Nawabganj area. The police had received information that Rakesh had hidden money stolen in a theft underground inside the house. This information reached Police Commissioner Piyush Mordia. After this, a police team, including DCP (Ganganagar) Sonam Kumar and ADCP Pushkar Verma, reached the spot at 6 p.m. on Wednesday. The electricity supply to the entire village was cut off before the operation. A search operation was then launched. ACP of Soraon, Shyamjeet Pramila Singh, was also present during the operation. Search operation continued for four and a half hours According to the police, three blue drums buried in the ground were found during a search of the house. Bundles of notes wrapped in cloth had been placed inside them. The police seized the cash, sealed the house and cordoned it off. After conducting the search operation for around four and a half hours, the police left the spot at 10:30 p.m. The police have also taken Rakesh's brother Bablu into custody. Police teams took the entire family with them. More than 40 police personnel have been deployed around the house. The police have also cordoned off and secured Rakesh's garden and vacant land adjoining the house. Villagers claim: 22 bighas of land bought within a few years Villagers said that several years ago, Rakesh Yadav had lived in Pune with his brother-in-law and his wife's brother and worked at a jeweller's house. During the Covid pandemic, he returned to his home in Bareipur. He then bought 22 bighas of land worth more than ₹10 crore. He built a house after investing around ₹1 crore. He bought two tractors, a DJ system and a pickup vehicle. He then started a cement and steel-rods business there. Rakesh lives in the village with two brothers Rakesh has six brothers. Of them, Rakesh, Rajesh and Lavkush live in the village, while the other three-Chhotu, Rajendra and Abhishek-live elsewhere. Their father, Ram Aadhar, has died. DCP Ganganagar Sonam Kumar said: Cash worth crores has been recovered from three drums buried beneath the ground at Rakesh's house. Police personnel have been deployed at the site. An investigation team from the Income Tax Department has arrived from Lucknow to investigate the case. A team has also been sent to Pune.

stories.title: Father, son die after falling from 23rd floor in Noida:Man fell while trying to save son, who slipped while plucking flowers on balcony
stories.summary: Father and 11-year-old son fall to their deaths from the 23rd floor in Noida: Father was helping his son pluck flowers using a ladder when the boy slipped; he fell while trying to save him The deceased have been identified as Randeep Patra (40) and his son Aarav (11). The incident took place at around 4.20 am on Friday at Mahagun Mywoods Society in the Bisrakh police station area. The father was helping his son pluck flowers using a ladder on the balcony when the boy lost his footing and began dangling from the balcony. In an attempt to save him, the father also fell from the 23rd floor. Both died on the spot. Family was preparing to visit Khatu Shyam Randeep Patra (40) worked as a section officer at the Central Secretariat in Delhi. He lived with his wife and 11-year-old son Aarav in Tower 23 of Mahagun Mywoods Society. During police questioning, his wife said, "We were supposed to visit Khatu Shyam with the family on Friday morning to register a plot of land. Randeep and Aarav went to the balcony to pluck flowers for the Puja(rituals). I was getting ready inside the house. Aarav slipped from the ladder on the balcony. Randeep rushed to save him, but both lost their footing and fell from the 23rd floor." Deputy Commissioner of Police (Central Noida) Praveen Ranjan Singh said: “At around 4.20 am on Friday, the control room received information through the 112 emergency helpline that two people had fallen from a height at Mywoods Society. The police sent the bodies for post-mortem examination. The matter is being thoroughly investigated from all angles.”

stories.title: Rickshaw driver's son detained by ATS in Kanpur:Mother breaks down, says he claimed to be playing games on his laptop when asked
stories.summary: There was a hole in my liver, and my son was paying for my treatment... How will I get treatment now? His father drove a rickshaw to educate him so that he would support us in our old age, but the police took him away. My son worked in digital marketing; he could not have been involved in terrorist activities. This was said by Savitri, the mother of 12th-pass Ankit Sanghwar, who was arrested by the ATS in Kanpur. The mother said, "When we asked my son, he would say that he was playing games. He worked on a laptop at night." His father, Prahlad, said, "My son cannot do this. He had bought a second-hand laptop on instalments from Govind Nagar only six months ago." On 24 October, the Uttar Pradesh ATS arrested from Kanpur the accused who carried out a bomb blast. He had sent emails threatening to blow up schools in Uttar Pradesh, Delhi and Gurugram, as well as actor Diljit Dosanjh, with bombs. The UP ATS said the accused created and sold fake email IDs to people based in countries such as Pakistan, Bangladesh, Turkey, Egypt and the USA. These IDs were used in anti-national activities. He had sold more than 5 lakh fake email IDs, and the investigation found that he received $20 to $50 for each email ID. Hole in mother's liver, cataracts in her eyes Ankit's mother, Savitri, said tearfully, "I also have cataracts in my eyes. My son was the one getting me treated at a private hospital in the city." She said, "Who will get me treated now?" The family could not believe that their son had become involved in such anti-national activities. Savitri said everything had been going smoothly. But on Saturday, two men in plain clothes arrived and said they were taking him for questioning. However, there has been no trace of him for six days. I have visited the police station and outpost repeatedly. My son is innocent; a friend from Barra has framed him. Received house under PM Awas Yojana in 2025 Prahlad Sankhwar, originally from Anoia village in the Sajeti police station area, moved to Kanpur four years ago. He initially lived in a rented accommodation in Barra's Damodar Nagar. On 20 July 2025, he bought a one-room unit in Block 5 under the Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana in the Sen Paschimpara police station area for ₹2 lakh. Prahlad, his wife Savitri and their younger son, accused Ankit, live in the house. Prahlad drives a rickshaw, while his wife Savitri works as a labourer. Their elder son Atit lives in Block Three in a rented colony with his wife Mamta and their two children. Their middle son Dharmendra works on a contractual basis for a municipal corporation in Arunachal Pradesh. His father, Prahlad, said that Ankit passed Class 12 in 2020. As the family's financial condition was not good, he did not continue his studies. He then started working as a labourer. After saving money, he bought a scooter in 2021. He often remained engrossed in his phone from 9 a.m. to 3:30 p.m. When asked, he said he was investing money in the share market. His sister-in-law, Mamta, said that he invested money in the share market several times, but never made a profit. After that, he became involved in all such activities. Now, read the full story... Police Commissioner Raghubir Lal said the Uttar Pradesh Anti-Terrorism Squad (ATS) received information that threatening emails were being sent from simenbriones9265@gmail.com to various schools in Gautam Buddh Nagar, Uttar Pradesh, Delhi and Gurugram. The emails contained threats, purportedly from the Khalistan National Army and Babbar Khalsa, to bomb schools in various states, a proposed show by Punjabi singer and actor Diljit Dosanjh in the Delhi-NCR region, and his home. When the ATS began investigating the emails, it found that the mastermind with access to the email ID was Ankit Sankhwar, the son of Prahlad and a resident of Anoia village in the Ghatampur police station area of Kanpur. The police commissioner said Ankit used Wi-Fi and proxy networks to create fake email IDs, which he sold to anti-India elements based in Pakistan, Bangladesh and other countries, receiving payment in cryptocurrency in return. After receiving intelligence, the UP ATS conducted a raid on Wednesday and arrested Ankit Sanghwar. The ATS recovered a mobile phone and laptop from the accused. The police commissioner said several Excel files and crypto wallets were also found on the accused's mobile phone and laptop. When the Excel files found on the laptop were examined, they revealed shocking details. The investigation found that the accused had created 5 lakh fake email IDs using a proxy network. During questioning, Ankit said he had been creating fake email IDs since 2021. The police commissioner said the email ID from which threatening messages were sent to schools in Gurugram, Delhi and Noida was also found on the laptop. Another fake email ID, smithjohnson6889@gmail.com, was also found; it had been used to threaten to blow up the Mumbai mayor's office on 23 October. This is how the accused sold email IDs The arrested accused, Ankit, said he used to buy and sell these fake email accounts by joining Buy and Sell groups on Facebook. He had obtained these fake IDs through the groups from people connected to groups in Pakistan, Bangladesh, Turkey, Egypt and other countries. These people based abroad are involved in anti-India activities. Ankit said he sent the fake email IDs in an Excel sheet containing the email ID, its password, recovery email and two-factor code. Fake ID sold to Bangladeshi youth for 6000 USTD Ankit said he had connected with a Bangladeshi youth, Alamin Islam alias Alamin, through Facebook and WhatsApp, and had been asked to provide fake email IDs. Ankit subsequently provided the fake ID simenbriones9265@gmail.com, and 6,000 USDT (cryptocurrency) was paid in return through this fake email. The ATS found evidence of this on Ankit's mobile phone. Ankit said he had sent the simenbriones9265@gmail.com ID to Alamin, and that it was used to send threatening messages to various schools on 12 October. Threatening emails were also sent to the Mumbai Mayor's House on 23 October from the email ID smithjohnson6889@gmail.com. The passwords, recovery email addresses and two-factor codes for both email IDs were sent to Bangladeshi national Alamin via WhatsApp in an Excel sheet. The Police Commissioner said Ankit was connected via WhatsApp with people in Pakistan, Bangladesh, Egypt, Turkey and the USA. The ATS also found a large number of USDT transactions from foreign numbers. The ATS investigation revealed that Ankit was paid $20 to $50 in exchange for a fake email ID, and the ATS also found evidence of this.

stories.title: PET first shift exam concludes peacefully in Gorakhpur:Candidates rate paper moderate, say DI questions were tricky
stories.summary: The first shift of the Preliminary Eligibility Test (PET)-2026 was held peacefully under tight security in Gorakhpur on Friday. Candidates who came out after the exam described the paper as moderate, saying it was neither too difficult nor too easy. However, they said the questions on mathematics and Data Interpretation (DI) took more time to solve. Candidates found the questions on General Knowledge, current affairs and reasoning relatively easy. After the first shift ended, entry for the second shift also began. Strict security and monitoring arrangements were in place at the examination centres. Exam conducted peacefully under tight security Special security arrangements were made at examination centres across the district for PET-2026. Candidates were allowed to enter the examination halls only after proper checking. The entire exam was conducted under CCTV surveillance. After the first shift ended, candidates came out of the centres and shared their experiences. Most described the paper as moderate, while some said the mathematics and DI questions were time-consuming. The entry was closed at 1,372 exam centres across 60 districts in the state. Strict checking was carried out at several centres. In Prayagraj, Lucknow and Pratapgarh, male candidates were asked to remove their shoes and socks for checking. In Gorakhpur, candidates were even asked to remove their handkerchiefs. In Bareilly, female candidates were asked to open their hair for checking. Their hair clips, earrings and chains were also removed. In Sitapur, women candidates removed their jewellery and handed it over to their family members before entering the exam centres. Around 11.80 lakh candidates will appear for the exam in two shifts today. The first shift will be held from 10 am to 12 noon, while the second shift will take place from 3 pm to 5 pm. Entry for the second shift will begin at 1 pm, and the gates will close at 1:30 pm. Schools up to Class 12 have been closed in all 60 districts where the exam is being held. The first phase of the exam took place on October 25. Of the 11.80 lakh candidates scheduled to appear, 8.27 lakh took the exam that day. The final phase will be held on November 1. A total of around 35.41 lakh candidates have registered for PET 2026. Bangle removed during checking in Hardoi Subhashini, who travelled from Lucknow to Hardoi to take the PET, was also asked to remove her bangle and hair clip. She said the staff asked her to remove the bangle during checking. When she refused, she was told that she would not be allowed inside without removing it. She then had to take it off. Candidates reach exam centres in rain in Bhadohi In Bhadohi, candidates reached 13 exam centres despite the rain. Security staff put up tarpaulin sheets to protect themselves and the candidates from the rain while carrying out checks. After the checking, candidates were allowed to enter the centres.

stories.title: PET exam enters second day at 45 centres in Lucknow:Three-level security checks before entry, female candidates asked to remove shoes for frisking
stories.summary: The second day of the PET (Preliminary Eligibility Test) is being held in Lucknow today. Entry for candidates began at 8 a.m. at the capital's 45 examination centres. The examination will be conducted in two shifts. The first shift will begin at 10 a.m., while the second shift will run from 3 p.m. to 5 p.m. Tight security arrangements have been made at the examination centres. Candidates are being allowed inside only after three levels of checking. Female candidates are also undergoing thorough searches. During the checks, they are being asked to remove their shoes for inspection. Security tightened ahead of Amit Shah's visit Union Home Minister Amit Shah is also visiting Lucknow today. The venue for his programme is close to the examination centre. Security arrangements have therefore been tightened along the entire route. Police surveillance has been increased on the roads. A large police force has also been deployed at the examination centre. Security agencies are on alert in view of the examination and the Home Minister's visit. Candidates are being allowed to enter the examination centre only after completing the checking process.

stories.title: ‘BJP's foothold is like Angad’s foot, none can move it’:‘Focus on the target like Arjuna’; Shah attends state executive meeting
stories.summary: Amit Shah is in Lucknow on Friday, where he told BJP workers at the party's state executive committee meeting that the BJP is like Angad's foot in Uttar Pradesh and no one can move it. He urged workers to prepare for the 2027 Assembly elections, saying, "Keep your eyes fixed on the target like Arjuna. We have to form the government." Shah arrived in Lucknow after nearly nine months. Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath and both Deputy Chief Ministers welcomed him. Yogi and Shah were seated next to each other during the meeting. Uttar Pradesh BJP president Pankaj Chaudhary and state in-charge Vinod Tawde were also present. Addressing the meeting at the auditorium of Babasaheb Bhimrao Ambedkar University, Shah discussed the roadmap for the Assembly elections and gave more than 2,500 party workers a strategy to help the BJP secure a third consecutive term in Uttar Pradesh. Pankaj Chaudhary urged workers to remain alert and stay among voters. He said they need to prevent people from being misled, alleging that attempts are being made to create confusion and unrest through foreign funding. BJP MP Ravi Kishan described Shah as the "Chanakya of politics" and said his arrival was very auspicious. Referring to the Bengal elections, he said, "We saw it during the Bengal elections." Shah will remain at the meeting for around four hours before returning to Delhi. CM Yogi Adityanath will address the concluding session at 5 pm.

stories.title: Man jailed for 20-years for kidnapping and sexually assaulting minor:Varanasi court imposes ₹40,000 fine, 70% to go to victim
stories.summary: Varanasi's special POCSO court has convicted Cantt resident Tanveer Khan in a case involving the abduction and sexual exploitation of a teenage girl. On Thursday, the court of Special Judge Nitin Pandey sentenced him to 20 years' rigorous imprisonment and fined him ₹40,000. The court ordered that 70 per cent of the fine be paid to the victim as compensation. The case dates back to 8 March 2023, when the 15-year-old girl did not return home after going to the market. Cantt police registered a case and began an investigation following a complaint by the family. Case registered following family's complaint According to the prosecution, the girl's mother lodged an FIR at Cantt police station. She said her daughter had gone to the market to buy सामान, but did not return for a long time. The family searched for her, but found no information. The family then approached the police and informed them about the entire incident. Based on the complaint, police registered a case against Cantt resident Tanveer Khan. Investigation revealed sexual exploitation The police investigation found that the accused had lured the teenage girl away with him. After a search, the police recovered the girl and arrested the accused. During the investigation, it also emerged that the girl had been sexually abused. The police then completed the investigation and filed a charge sheet in court. Testimony of seven witnesses and medical report formed the basis During the trial, the prosecution presented a total of seven witnesses. The witnesses' statements, the medical report and other evidence were submitted before the court. On the basis of this evidence and the police investigation, the court found the accused guilty. He was then sentenced to 20 years' rigorous imprisonment and fined ₹40,000. Officials and employees of the Varanasi Commissionerate played a role in securing the conviction and sentence in this case.

stories.title: Special train to run between Gorakhpur and Mumbai:Festival travel home to become easier for passengers
stories.summary: Railways has decided to run a festival special train between Gorakhpur and Mumbai's Bandra Terminus to accommodate the additional rush of passengers during the festive season. Train numbers 05091/05092 Gorakhpur-Bandra Terminus-Gorakhpur Festival Special will make two trips in each direction. The train will depart from Gorakhpur on 9 and 16 November, while it will leave Bandra Terminus on 11 and 18 November. This will make travel more convenient for passengers travelling to Mumbai and other cities along the route. According to Railways, train number 05091 Gorakhpur-Bandra Terminus Festival Special will depart from Gorakhpur at 9:55 pm on the scheduled dates. The train will reach Kanpur Central via Basti, Gonda and Lucknow. It will then enter Gujarat via Tundla, Idgah Agra, Gangapur City, Kota, Bhawani Mandi and Ratlam. The train will reach Bandra Terminus at 12 noon the following day, stopping at Vadodara, Surat, Vapi and Borivali stations. Train will depart from Bandra at 1:45 am on its return journey Train will have 21 coaches According to the railway, the Festival Special will have a total of 21 coaches, including two LSLRD, 11 general and eight sleeper coaches. This will give passengers the option to travel according to their convenience.

stories.title: Rain alert in all 75 UP districts:Heavy rain warning in 21; strong winds in Lucknow, hail likely
stories.summary: Rain alerts have been issued for all 75 districts of Uttar Pradesh on Friday due to Cyclone 'Arnab'. A warning of heavy rain has been issued for 21 districts, including Gorakhpur, Ayodhya and Moradabad. Light rain and thunderstorms are expected in the other districts. Meanwhile, skies have been overcast in Lucknow and the surrounding districts since Friday morning. Strong winds are blowing. Earlier, light rain was recorded in 18 districts, including Ayodhya, Ghaziabad and Gorakhpur, on Thursday. Lightning struck the minaret of the Badi Masjid in Saharanpur. Clouds gathered over Lucknow in the afternoon, followed by rain. Meerut and Kashi received heavy rain in the evening. Unseasonal rain in the last week of October threatens to damage the paddy crop that is ready for harvesting in the fields. It could also affect preparations for sowing wheat, potatoes and mustard. In view of the cyclone's possible impact, Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath has directed state officials to remain on alert. The administration has been instructed to monitor the weather situation and take precautionary measures as required.

stories.title: Pennsylvania woman treated for breast cancer had rare lymphoma; court allows family's lawsuit
stories.summary: A Pennsylvania woman received breast cancer treatment for 13 months before doctors discovered she had a rare and aggressive lymphoma. She died in January 2019, and her family sued the treating oncologist, alleging that the delayed diagnosis reduced her chances of survival. After a trial court dismissed the case, the Pennsylvania Supreme Court ruled that a jury should hear the malpractice claim.

Their strategy focuses on addressing the opposition's criticism related to the SIR and electoral setbacks. Young athletes can engage with these recycled nets, fostering a sense of environmental awareness alongside their love for sports.

This ruling highlights the challenges in pursuing financial claims against county governments in Georgia.

stories.summary: A 640-acre farmland donation made to a Texas school district in 1984 has become a source of college scholarships for hundreds of students. Since 2016, the initiative has distributed nearly $3 million to around 300 students, helping them pursue higher education.

Unveiled on November 1, this stupa strengthens the enduring friendship and cultural ties between India and Bhutan. This initiative highlights Bhutan's commitment to boosting its Buddhist identity and serves as a token of gratitude for India's continuous support in its developmental journey.

stories.summary: Bihar's government has signed an agreement with the road transport ministry for river desilting to reduce flooding. On the flip side, Republicans retaining control over both chambers could steer Trump's political agenda. The results await, holding the potential to influence the nation significantly.

India, sharing river systems with Bhutan, has started its own review of disaster preparedness plans.

stories.summary: A High Court judge ruled that specific assets of the deceased were legitimate gifts received by Masudur Rahman before death, dating back to October 2020. Rahman secured costs due to his successful claim, but his plea for an enhanced costs budget was ultimately denied by the judge.

stories.summary: A couple from Tennessee faced a setback as their claim over a strip of land beside their house was overturned by the court. This rise is attributed to the forthcoming 2026-27 El Niño, with sightings of tropical species migrating northward, suggesting significant ecological transformations. These shifts in ocean conditions pose a risk to deep-sea food availability, impacting various marine ecosystems.

stories.title: Bangka Slow Loris Rediscovered: Rescues reveal more than 90 venomous primates; habitat loss still threatens
stories.summary: A groundbreaking study reveals the comeback of the Bangka slow loris, once feared lost or critically endangered. Over 90 individuals have been documented on Bangka Island from 2015 to 2025, shedding light on their survival. Wildlife rescues have been instrumental not only in recording their existence but also in aiding rehabilitation efforts.

stories.title: Navy rescues 20 crew members of fishing vessel from armed pirates over 3,000km from Mumbai, Rajnath praises 48-hr op
Atlanta landlord's $50,000 fundraiser grows into $16.5 million, helping 5,500 families avoid eviction
stories.summary: Jason Dozier initiated a fundraising campaign in 2020, which led to the creation of the Housing Stability Fund. This programme has provided financial assistance to over 5,500 families facing housing insecurity in the Atlanta area. By streamlining processes and collaborating with landlords, the programme aims to prevent evictions and court backlogs. Follow-up surveys indicate that a majority of recipients remain in stable housing a year later.

stories.title: Louisiana woman wins nearly $450,000 after $32,500 river barrier fails and home shifts
stories.summary: After suffering extensive structural damage to her home from a failing wooden bulkhead, Elizabeth Molbert took legal action against the contractor involved and succeeded. The jury assigned 75% of the blame to the contractor and, in a twist, the appeals court ruled that Molbert had no fault in the matter, increasing her compensation to $448,431.34 and adjusting her mental anguish damages to align with her financial difficulties.

stories.title: Row erupts after Scottish govt sends IT contract to Bengaluru to administer welfare payment
Texas opens 3,000-acre state park along the Colorado River with $1 billion expansion fund
stories.summary: Post Oak Ridge has officially opened, marking Texas' latest state park. Spanning over 3,000 acres, it features two hiking trails along four miles of scenic routes. Plans for future camping facilities and river access are on track for completion by 2029. Input from the community has been vital in guiding the park's development, as part of a larger effort to expand public outdoor spaces across Texas.

stories.title: Howard Stern's wife Beth turns grief into rescue mission, helping over 2,000 cats find homes
stories.summary: After the heartbreaking passing of their bulldog, Howard and Beth Stern channeled their sorrow into meaningful change by founding Bianca's Furry Friends Feline Adoption Center, part of North Shore Animal League America. This center improves the conditions for cats waiting for adoption and boosts rescue capabilities. With over 2,000 cats fostered since 2013, Beth's dedicated efforts have played a crucial role in spotlighting the importance of adopting shelter animals nationwide.

stories.title: Farm Becomes Wildlife Retreat: Olivia Newton-John reshaped Dalwood estate; sale tied to cancer work
stories.summary: Olivia Newton-John owned a country estate in Australia that she transformed over nearly four decades. This property included natural features and a significant amount of wildlife habitat that she developed. After battling cancer, the estate was sold in 2019 for $4.6 million, reflecting changes in her priorities. Newton-John's connection to the area continued through her involvement with a wellness retreat she co-founded.

stories.title: Rahul can be PM only in mock Parliament: Amit Shah
Stephen Curry-backed golf teams make history with women's first NEC title and men's third win
stories.summary: Howard University's golf program reached new heights when both men's and women's teams won their conference championships. The women's team claimed its first-ever Northeast Conference title in April 2026. Just days later, the men's team secured its third consecutive NEC championship victory. The successes highlighted the growth of the program, supported by NBA star Stephen Curry's funding.

stories.title: Days after Farooq’s Pak praise, Mehbooba says Abdullahs created distrust between Kashmir & rest of India
Nebraska court rejects handwritten will signed by man but written largely by his longtime partner
stories.summary: In a significant ruling, Nebraska's Supreme Court declared a handwritten will invalid, stating that the primary handwriting was not that of the testator. The court reaffirmed the original 1984 will, which allocated assets to the deceased's sons. This decision underlined the necessity for a holographic will to be solely in the writer's hand to clarify testamentary intent, especially amid disputes from a long-term partner after Douglas G. Todd's death.

stories.title: Maryland court orders new trial over $3.2 million trust after sisters challenge inheritance
stories.summary: A Maryland appeals court has mandated a new trial concerning a $3.2 million trust fund held by three sisters. The court identified procedural errors that prevented two sisters from presenting crucial handwriting evidence regarding the trust. Their claims included accusations of undue influence exerted by their sister, the main beneficiary. The appeals court emphasized issues with the previous trial's allowed testimonies and evidence exclusions.

stories.title: North Carolina sculptor's tiny cabin grew into a 60-foot woodland castle
Paul McCartney-backed Liverpool arts institute celebrates 400+ graduates 30 years on
stories.summary: The LIPA held its 2026 graduation ceremony celebrating its 30th anniversary by awarding degrees to its very first graduates. With over 400 students from 28 different countries in attendance, this event marked a monumental occasion. Sir Paul McCartney was on hand to honor five notable figures for their artistry and impact on the cultural landscape, showcasing LIPA's commitment to nurturing creative talent across various fields, including music, theatre, and film.

stories.title: Fake nuclear threat alert sent to Ukrainians after emergency app hacked
IISc develops 3D-printed model to study how cancer drugs penetrate tumours
RLD leader projects Jayant Chaudhary as NDA's face for 2027 UP polls
Homebuyers body urges PM to recast RERA; separate promotion from protection
ICE officer surrenders after grand jury indicts him for running over immigrant with vehicle in Texas
Trump admin asks Supreme Court to set aside 20,000 California ballots over citizenship row a day before midterms
Power outage hits Washington DC's Foggy Bottom, over 1,100 Pepco customers affected
Indian Sikh couple's New Zealand asylum claim rejected after NZ$336,000 crore debt dispute with Punjab moneylender
Entire police force resigns in Georgia city; Mayor Craig Timmons admits tracking police chief's truck
stories.summary: A small Georgia city is facing a police staffing crisis after its entire full-time police force resigned. Mayor Craig Timmons admitted placing a GPS tracker on Police Chief Lamar Bunn's truck over concerns about his timesheets. Bunn has denied wrongdoing, while the mass resignations have left the city relying on the county sheriff's office for police coverage.

stories.title: Historic Mansion Sale Soars: Nantucket’s Hadwen-Wright House fetches $15.25 million; hidden cistern preserved
stories.summary: The Hadwen-Wright House in Nantucket fetched an impressive $15.25 million, after being originally listed at $15.5 million. This stunning mansion, a prime example of Greek Revival architecture, is steeped in history. Its extensive renovations not only maintained original features but also unveiled a unique brick-lined cistern now preserved for guests. This sale highlights the lasting appeal of Nantucket's historically significant residences.

stories.title: In 2013, divers started placing simple cinder-block pyramids on a Caribbean seabed
stories.summary: Initiated in 2013, the Grenada Artificial Reef Project employs concrete blocks to foster marine life habitats. Remarkable progress was observed shortly after, with algae and various invertebrates flourishing on the structures. However, while research shows these artificial reefs attract species typical of natural environments, further studies are essential to evaluate their role in aiding natural reef recovery and assessing their long-term effects on adjacent ecosystems.

stories.title: US judge dismisses charges against 2 ex-FBI officials over Hunter Biden laptop probe, calls prosecution 'weaponisation'
Iran's supreme leader gave government 'certain authorities' over peace talks with US: Pezeshkian
US midterms: Five flashpoints election officials are watching as America votes
'Look outside, Jack!' Who was the man called out by female pilot Nathalia in final moments of Learjet crash?
First in 47 years: CRPF completes 12 months without any operational casualties
stories.summary: CRPF Director General GP Singh congratulated personnel on the milestone, saying the last operational death in the force was recorded on October 30, 2025. The previous time the CRPF went such a long period without an operational fatality was before January 1979. The milestone comes against the backdrop of another serious challenge facing the force, the rising number of personnel dying by suicide.

stories.title: Meet the couple who couldn't afford a UK home bought an entire French hamlet for £26K, saved £100K
stories.summary: Yip Ward and Paul Mappley went from living in a caravan in England to owning an abandoned French hamlet. The couple bought the property for £26,000, which includes seven cottages, two barns and other buildings. By carrying out much of the restoration themselves, they estimate they have saved more than £100,000 while bringing the historic hamlet back to life.

stories.title: Trump's Justice dept steps into US midterm battles, breaks decades-old practice
'NCP united under Sunetra Pawar': Party rejects rift rumours as she skips Amit Shah meet
stories.summary: The speculation was fuelled by the absence of Maharashtra deputy chief minister Sunetra Pawar and her sons, Parth and Jay, from Sunday's meeting with Shah. The development raised questions about whether the party's leadership was being sidelined in discussions over its future following the death of Ajit Pawar. NCP national chief spokesperson Umesh Patil rejected reports as "incorrect, baseless and misleading".

stories.title: NZ couple turn hillside land into a medieval brick castle with towers and a secret dungeon trapdoor
stories.summary: After three decades of craftsmanship, Denise and Greg Powell are parting ways with their extraordinary recycled-brick castle in Broad Bay. What began as a straightforward home evolved into a medieval masterpiece, complete with a secret trapdoor and various salvaged architectural details. As they downsize to a cozier residence nearby, this unique property has seen its value soar since their acquisition in the early 90s.

stories.title: New Hampshire closed 20 acres of Great Bay to shellfish harvesting for 5 years from November 1
stories.summary: The Fish and Game Department of New Hampshire has initiated a five-year period of closure at Great Bay to facilitate oyster restoration efforts. This move affects two key sites, one near Woodman Point and another near Nannie Island. Significant measures are being implemented to combat the alarming 90% decline in oyster reefs since 1970, involving collaboration between researchers and conservation groups to rejuvenate oyster populations and restore essential marine habitats.

stories.title: New York volunteers spent seven years preparing six 175-pound reef balls for Eastchester Bay
stories.summary: After years of meticulous planning, volunteers from City Island Oyster Reef successfully installed six reef balls in Eastchester Bay. These structures were intentionally seeded with oyster larvae to bolster local oyster populations. This initiative stems from thorough monitoring of both water quality and the ecosystem around City Island. Remarkably, marine species like fish and crabs have started to thrive in the area.

stories.title: Co-pilot of doomed Learjet flight that crashed in Florida identified as Nathalia Gadelha. She got her private pilot's license when she was 17
'Surge in popularity after reality show': Tej Pratap Yadav asks for enhanced security from Centre
stories.summary: In a post on X, Yadav said his recent appearance on a reality show had increased his popularity, with large numbers of people approaching him in public places to take photographs. He said the crowds posed a risk not only to him but also to the lone security personnel currently assigned to him.

stories.title: Russia exits European anti-torture treaty, ends independent prison inspections
Cyclone Murusu: 19 flights cancelled, NDRF on standby as coastal states brace for severe storm - top development
Indian-origin woman Srishti Tarana Sharma charged in US over pro-Palestine intimidation campaign at Michigan university
Cyclone Murasu to make landfall near at Andhra coast tonight; 120 kmph winds expected
stories.summary: Cyclone Murasu has intensified and is predicted to cross the south Andhra Pradesh coast soon. It is expected to bring strong winds reaching up to 120 kmph and heavy rainfall. Several districts in Andhra Pradesh will experience severe weather conditions due to the cyclone. Precautionary measures have been implemented, including rescue operations and evacuation arrangements. Fishermen have been advised to avoid venturing into the sea during this period.

stories.title: 'Azam the, Azam hain': Will the Khan factor help or haunt Akhilesh in 2027 UP elections?
stories.summary: Akhilesh Yadav's recent visit to Azam Khan in jail underscores their deep political connection amidst ongoing legal troubles. Following Azam's fleeting bail, the Enforcement Directorate swiftly took him back into custody, adding complexity to the Samajwadi Party's election preparations. Balancing support for Azam while appealing to Muslim constituents presents a significant challenge for Akhilesh as he navigates potential electoral repercussions.

stories.title: 'Your social media posts amounted to instigation': Bombay HC pulls up actor Imran Khan - top quotes
stories.summary: A bench comprising Chief Justice Mahesh Chandra Tripathi and Justice Advait Sethna remarked that instead of deporting Khan immediately, authorities had shown leniency by issuing him a notice asking him to leave the country. Khan's lawyer, Venkatesh Dhond, responded by submitting an undertaking that the 43-year-old actor would not participate in any protest in the future. He also conveyed Khan's unconditional apology to the court.

stories.title: 'Rahul Gandhi has no vision, will be responsible for Congress's wipeout': BJP's Nitin Nabin at anti-SIR march
'3 crore Bangladeshi infiltrators don't exist on voters' list': Amit Shah counters Rahul's anti-SIR pitch
stories.summary: In a verbal blitzkrieg, a day after Rahul's mega Ramlila Maidan rally in the national capital, Shah said that behind the Congress's criticism of the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) lies an "attempt to protect illegal Bangladeshi infiltrators", three crore of whom, he claimed, were struck off the electoral rolls during the revision.

stories.title: Evening newswrap: Imran Khan apologises to Bombay HC, SC allows green crackers & more
'You became PM because of foreign help': Rahul Gandhi challenges PM Modi for debate
61 detained in Ahmedabad as crackdown on illegal Bangladeshi immigrants intensifies
stories.summary: Ahmedabad's Crime Branch has taken action against 61 suspected illegal immigrants, mostly hailing from Bangladesh, in a city-wide effort to bolster safety ahead of Diwali. The police executed synchronized raids across different localities to pinpoint foreign nationals living without legal status. Deportation processes are currently being initiated, furthering previous measures aimed at curbing illegal immigration from Bangladesh.

stories.title: Centre notifies grievance redressal rules under VB-G RAM G Act, sets 15-day resolution deadline
stories.summary: The Centre has officially introduced grievance redressal protocols as per the VB-G RAM G Act, 2025. Complaints must receive resolution within 15 days, with preliminary inquiries to be conducted in seven working days. Individuals can lodge grievances through various methods, ensuring that all complaints will be recorded. Complainants will have the opportunity to present their cases, and issues that remain unresolved shall be escalated for further scrutiny and resolution.

stories.title: Siddaramaiah sting op row: Kumaraswamy questions SIT delay; Priyank Kharge alleges ED pressure
Charity founder stole millions and spent $320,000 on lavish dining trips
Imran Khan tenders unconditional apology in HC over anti-SIR protest participation
FPCE writes to PM Modi, lists 5 key changes to RERA to strengthen homebuyer protection
SC allows green crackers in Delhi-NCR for Diwali, full ban from November 9
Sonia Gandhi meets Lalu Yadav in Delhi; Tejashwi shares photos, reminisces UPA-era tie
stories.summary: Tejashwi Yadav, Bihar leader of the opposition, said Sonia Gandhi had personally expressed a desire to meet his father after learning that he was in Delhi for a medical check-up. He also pointed out that the then Prime Minister Manmohan Singh's government had allocated more than Rs 1.45 lakh crore for Bihar's development.

stories.title: Texas man arrested after cemetery theft and FBI office bone incident
'Don't travel by air. Next case': SC judge on plea alleging 700% airfare hike
‘Rahul Gandhi fostering chaos’: BJP questions Congress over SIR row
Serena Williams helped build 2 schools in rural Kenya; years later, both remain open and part of national education system
stories.summary: Serena Williams established two secondary schools in rural Kenya to provide local children with education. The Matooni Serena Williams Secondary School opened in 2009, followed by the Wee Serena Williams Secondary School in 2010. Both schools are now integrated into Kenya's national education system and managed by community boards. HP's involvement brought important technology resources to enhance learning experiences for students.

stories.title: A Dutch engineer built a car controlled by a goldfish swimming inside a water tank; earning a Guinness World Records title
stories.summary: In an extraordinary showcase of technology and pet companionship, Blub, the goldfish belonging to Dutch engineer Thomas de Wolf, successfully maneuvered a motion-sensing vehicle for 12.28 meters on a Milan television show aired on January 23, 2025. By translating Blub's natural movements into steering commands, De Wolf envisions applications of this technology to assist people with physical disabilities, merging creativity with functionality.

stories.title: Meet the three former AAP leaders who switched sides to join BJP ahead of Punjab polls
Neymar's centre helps 3,000 children with education, sports and healthcare
US woman returns from abroad to find inherited house sold using forged documents
stories.summary: A Tennessee woman returned from abroad in 2021 to discover that her late brother's house had been sold using a fake identity and forged documents. After she sued the company involved in the sale, a lower court dismissed her case. On Thursday, an appeals court revived her fraud claim but upheld the dismissal of her negligence claim.

stories.title: 'Don't take court for granted': Delhi court summons actor Nora Fatehi again in Rs 200-crore extortion case
Shakira's foundation helps 224,000 children, builds schools and boosts higher education
‘Youth-oppressive NDA govt’: Tejashwi accuses Nitish of toppling Mahagathbandhan regime in 2024
Big setback for AAP ahead of Punjab elections; 3 rebel MLAs join BJP
Oprah Winfrey’s $60 million Maui wildfire relief fund helped thousands; now her donation brings new CT scanner to local hospital
stories.summary: Oprah Winfrey and Dwayne Johnson launched the People's Fund of Maui to support wildfire survivors and provided significant financial assistance. Winfrey made a separate donation for a new CT scanner at Maui Memorial Medical Center to enhance healthcare services. The scanner aims to improve diagnosis and treatment for all patients, benefiting the wider Maui community. This contribution is part of a broader effort to strengthen healthcare infrastructure on the island.

stories.title: Black Hole Blast Shapes Structure: Astronomers trace ‘Treble Clef’ origins; collision revives radio glow
stories.summary: Astronomers have uncovered that the peculiar Treble Clef formation stems from a black hole eruption and the merger of two galaxy clusters. Observations from a variety of telescopes across different wavelengths revealed that the explosive event launched particles, which were later re-energized through the cluster collision. This groundbreaking research enhances our understanding of how cosmic phenomena can fundamentally alter the structures within the universe.

stories.title: 2 Congress workers held for hurling beer bottles at BJP headquarters in Kerala
stories.summary: In a heated political climate in Thiruvananthapuram, two Congress party workers were apprehended for allegedly hurling beer bottles at the BJP headquarters in Kerala. The situation escalated tensions between the rival parties. Following protests and demands from BJP for arrests, the police utilized CCTV footage for a thorough investigation, leading to the identification of the suspects as local Congress members involved in the incident.

stories.title: Teen-Led Wildlife Effort: Georgia student turns Johns Creek into habitat model; certification endures
stories.summary: In a remarkable effort, Malcolm Barnard led a campaign to promote wildlife conservation in Johns Creek, Georgia, achieving the status of a certified habitat community. He focused on educating the community while engaging schools and organizations to adopt wildlife-friendly practices. By 2013, all public schools in the area were recognized by the National Wildlife Federation, fostering a vision of interconnected habitats rather than isolated green spaces.

stories.title: Punjab: AAP to seek cancellation of membership of 2 MLAs after they quit party
Travis Scott's Cactus Jack awards $10,000 fashion scholarships with design training
US man marries dying partner in hospital, court reverses ruling voiding marriage
stories.summary: A Kentucky man who married his partner of nearly 30 years in hospital just 15 days before her death has won an appeal after her daughter challenged the marriage. The daughter questioned her mother's ability to consent and how the marriage licence was obtained. On Friday, the Kentucky Court of Appeals overturned the ruling invalidating the marriage and ordered further examination of the case.

stories.title: '2.5 lakh shops shut, Rs 10,000 crore loss': Delhi traders blame INDIA bloc rally for business disruption
INDIA bloc rally at Ramlila Maidan saw creative expression take centre stage as slogans, posters and placards delivered the message
stories.summary: In a momentous gathering, the INDIA bloc's supporters came together at Ramlila Maidan to address pressing political issues. Leaders from multiple parties spoke passionately about the necessity for change, particularly calling for the ousting of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar. This event highlighted the importance of unity against perceived electoral injustices, with speakers weaving in historical contexts to bolster their arguments regarding voting rights and electoral fairness.

stories.title: Netanyahu pushing Trump for nuclear strike on Iran? US commentator makes big claim
stories.summary: Tucker Carlson has claimed that Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu is pressuring US President Donald Trump for military action. This action is reportedly a nuclear strike aimed at Pickaxe Mountain in Iran, where nuclear activities are believed to be ongoing. Carlson suggests that the pressure could lead to a decision within days, escalating regional tensions. Diplomatic efforts between the US and Iran continue, though military options remain under consideration.

stories.title: Brooklyn woman attacked, stabbed in neck while jogging on waterfront trail
stories.summary: A 28-year-old woman named Katie Suarez was critically injured during a stabbing incident while jogging. The attack occurred along the Shore Parkway Greenway at around 8 pm local time on October 30. Emergency medical personnel transported Suarez to NYU Langone Hospital-Brooklyn, where she was admitted in critical condition. Police are appealing for information from witnesses to help identify the attacker responsible for the incident.

stories.title: Kiren Rijiju jibes at Congress over INDIA bloc's Ramlila rally crowd photo, calls it 'AI-generated'
US explores route to bring Russian gas back to Europe through Ukraine: Report
stories.summary: The US is exploring a plan to resume Russian natural gas supplies to Europe through Ukraine as part of efforts to secure an energy ceasefire and advance peace talks. The proposal could offer Moscow a financial incentive while providing Kyiv with transit revenue, but faces strong European opposition amid concerns over renewed dependence on Russia.

stories.title: Chinese Airlines Face Losses: Jet fuel surge, weak fares hit Q3 margins; stocks sink this year
stories.summary: China's leading airlines are experiencing significant financial losses amid rising jet fuel prices and weak domestic fare competition. Air China and China Eastern are expected to report their seventh consecutive annual net loss since the pandemic began. China Southern, after a brief return to profitability, is also projected to return to losses. Analysts indicate that the fourth quarter may continue to be challenging due to high operational expenses.

stories.title: J&K: NC Srinagar MP Mehdi to quit party tomorrow to fight it back on 'ideological' turf
Fresh Iran strikes after US midterms? Inside Trump-Netanyahu's 'tough' call
stories.summary: Donald Trump and Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu held a tough phone call regarding Iran and military strategies. They discussed the possibility of military action after the upcoming US midterm elections. Trump expressed readiness for diplomacy, while Netanyahu urged immediate strikes against Iran. Diplomatic initiatives continue, with the US Vice President sending a letter to Iran's national security chief.

stories.title: Desi Bullet Train closer to reality as squeeze test nears completion
6 Indian trekkers 'ignore weather warnings', get stranded in Nepal
SC upholds HC order allowing I-T to reassess income of ex-CJI's sons
Could Einstein’s equations explain the universe’s expansion?
stories.summary: Researchers from UC Davis have proposed that dark energy may not be necessary to explain the universe's acceleration. They found weak points in the Lambda-cold dark matter model using Einstein's equations. By examining instabilities in Friedmann spacetimes, they suggest alternative explanations for cosmic expansion. Their work raises questions about the Copernican principle in the context of current models. This research could lead to significant shifts in our understanding of cosmology.

stories.title: Scientists have developed a new technology that could make electric car batteries smaller, lighter and longer-lasting, potentially letting drivers travel farther on a single charge without carrying a heavier battery
stories.summary: Scientists from the Korea Advanced Institute of Science and Technology developed a new technology for anode-free batteries. This innovative approach focuses on enhancing lithium deposition to improve battery efficiency and longevity. By restructuring the copper surface for lithium storage, they have addressed issues with dendrite formation. Applying a thin layer of MXene further stabilizes the battery's performance.

stories.title: Introspect on need to improve judiciary responsiveness: CJI
Ranch Easement Preserves Habitat: Winn descendants shield 165 acres; Blanco River recharge gains
stories.summary: Four Winns Ranch in Texas, a treasured historical site, is preserved through dedicated efforts by the Winn family alongside conservation partners. Spanning 165 acres, this land is vital for protecting local wildlife habitats and water sources. Originally acquired by the noteworthy artist James Buchanan Buck Winn Jr., the ranch possesses rich cultural heritage while fostering agricultural and ecotourism activities, aiding the survival of rare birds and endangered aquatic species.

stories.title: Poverty removal not just slogan: PM Modi on World Bank data
12th century Nepalese Manjushri statue sold for about Rs 166 crore in 2026
stories.summary: A 12th-century Manjushri sculpture from Nepal recently sold for around ₹166 crore, illuminating the exceptional artistry of Newar creators from the Kathmandu Valley. This sculpture's intriguing journey through different collections illustrates its cultural significance and uniqueness. Furthermore, the influence of Newar craftsmanship on Buddhist art permeated throughout Tibet and Asia, showcasing Nepal's profound artistic legacy and its vital role in international art history.

stories.title: 1984 survivors, Sikh groups question timing of INDIA bloc rally on Nov 1, seek apology
Gyanesh has to go, PM & Shah next, says Rahul Gandhi at anti-CEC rally
12-year-old London boy raises £13,000 for wildlife, wins Attenborough's praise

A Neanderthal who died 75,000 years ago may have been killed by a wooden spear deliberately aimed at his heart, scientists say, offering rare evidence of targeted violence among our closest ancient relatives
stories.summary: A recent archaeological find in Shanidar Cave revealed a Neanderthal skeleton showing signs of lethal violence, potentially from a wooden spear, suggesting that early human emotional responses might mirror those of today. The evidence hints at both a targeted attack and social care, as the skeleton bore previous injuries. This discovery serves as a window into the dualities of early human life, showcasing their capacity for both violence and compassion.

stories.title: Fake claims, evasion of Rs 5.3 crore land, techie couple in I-T net
Golden Triangle's North East drug trade thrives on barter
£5 ivory chess piece found in family drawer sells for £735,000 after 55 years
stories.summary: An extraordinary Lewis chessman carving has fetched an impressive £735,000 at auction. Hidden away in a drawer for more than 55 years by the family of the dealer, this remarkable figure was revealed as a warder, part of the legendary Lewis Chessmen collection. Originally found in 1831, this collection comprises 93 intricately carved pieces from 1150 to 1200 AD, though the auction leaves four original pieces still unaccounted for.

stories.title: 82-year-old Florida man’s 70-year collection includes a letter from Elizabeth Taylor
In 1913, an Ohio couple sent their eight-month-old son to his grandmother through the postal service
stories.summary: In the year 1913, the US Postal Service unveiled Parcel Post, permitting the mailing of bigger packages. Ingenious parents even started shipping their small children to reduce travel expenses, gaining notoriety when six-year-old May Pierstorff was dispatched 73 miles away. This phenomenon sparked national debate, leading to the ban of child parceling, although similar incidents lingered until 1915, prompting stricter postal regulations to curb such extraordinary practices.

stories.title: Idaho Supreme Court revives condo owners' challenge to property changes approved by 88% vote
stories.summary: The Idaho Supreme Court has revived a legal dispute involving condominium owners challenging changes to property ownership. The contentious amendments were made by the Crystal Beach Condominium Association, affecting owners' shares and rental rules. A previous dismissal by a lower court has been partly overturned, confirming owners' rights to challenge changes impacting their property. Plaintiffs now have their claims for declaratory relief and title slander allowed to proceed.

stories.title: Texas court reopens insurance dispute after landslide destroys two homeowners' backyards
stories.summary: A legal dispute involving home insurance coverage in Travis County has been returned to court for further hearings. The Texas Third Court of Appeal overturned a previous ruling that held the insurer liable for damages. Homeowners claimed that earth movement caused significant damage to their properties, leading to a denial of their insurance claims. The appeals court requires the insurer to demonstrate the cause of the landslide.

stories.title: Florida has allocated $3 million to acquire a 642-acre property along the Suwannee River; officials say ending its current land use could save 159,000 gallons of water daily and reduce nutrient inputs
stories.summary: Florida has allocated $3 million for the acquisition of property along the Suwannee River to reduce water consumption. The Suwannee Sandhill Tract-Drew Property will help conserve approximately 158,800 gallons of water daily. This initiative is part of a larger $100 million investment aimed at various water conservation projects. The acquisition will facilitate the restoration of the land for wildlife habitats and public recreation.

stories.title: Dorothy Dandridge Home Listed: Former Hollywood Hills residence hits $5.499 million; price up nearly 90% from 2014 sale
stories.summary: A stunning Mediterranean-style home in Hollywood Hills, once owned by the iconic actress Dorothy Dandridge, is now on the market for nearly $5.5 million. Covering 4,368 square feet, the residence boasts four luxurious bedrooms and five opulent bathrooms. Dandridge's impactful legacy as a pioneering Black actress echoes through this property, complemented by breathtaking views of Los Angeles. The current owners have thoughtfully renovated it while respecting its historic charm.

stories.title: 'They'll become garbage': Trump says he'll become 'Mr. Veto' if Democrats win midterms
Poland’s top court turns into battleground as Tusk and pro-Trump president clash
Three held over pro-Khalistan graffiti at Delhi Metro stations after Diljit concert
Bhutan dedicates Buddhist stupa to PM Modi; Rijiju calls it ‘huge honour’ for India
stories.summary: In a heartfelt gesture symbolizing the deep-rooted friendship between Bhutan and India, King Jigme Khesar Namgyel Wangchuck dedicated a stupa to Prime Minister Narendra Modi. This event took place in Gelephu Mindfulness City, where 108 stupas are being raised. Union minister Kiren Rijiju represented India, conveying PM Modi's gratitude. The stupa, numbered 76, represents the strong ties shared by the two nations.

stories.title: CM Mann says opposition parties have nothing to offer Punjab, eyes AAP's return to power in 2027
California doctor Violetta Mailyan gets 15 years for $45 million Medicare fraud and fake Botox claims
stories.summary: California doctor Violetta Mailyan has been sentenced to 15 years in federal prison for defrauding Medicare of more than $45 million through fake Botox injection claims. Prosecutors said she used the money to buy five properties, two Tesla vehicles, including a Cybertruck, and expensive collectibles. She must also pay $32.9 million in restitution.

stories.title: 'Rahul trying to sideline Priyanka': BJP's big attack after INDIA bloc's Ramlila Maidan rally
UK Labour minister under fire for claiming employers are not ‘working people’
Coal India records highest-ever monthly supplies at 70.3 MT in Oct, up 19%
Beavers set to return to Loch Ness after 500 years, with 15 family groups approved for release.
stories.summary: In an exciting development, wild beavers are about to return to Loch Ness after centuries of absence. The Scottish nature agency NatureScot has sanctioned their release as part of a transformative rewilding project. Over the next three years, conservationists will introduce family groups of beavers to the area’s waterways, focusing on enhancing biodiversity and wildlife habitats, while also implementing strategies to resolve any conflicts with local farmers and landowners.

stories.title: Delaware couple wins disputed backyard land after 20 years, despite neighbours' $30,000 demand
stories.summary: After two decades of contention, a Delaware court officially awarded Joseph W.C. Murray, Jr. and Danielle F. Murray ownership of a long-disputed parcel of land. The case arose when the Preradovic family challenged property lines after purchasing an adjacent lot. Failed negotiations led to litigation, ultimately resulting in the court granting the Murrays the rear yard while their claims to the front areas were rejected.

stories.title: Ming royal descendant turned Buddhist monk painted 12 leaves of birds and flowers, sold for Rs 75 cr
stories.summary: Bada Shanren, originally named Zhu Da, was born into the Ming royal lineage in 1626. Following the Ming dynasty's collapse in 1644, he sought solace in a Buddhist monastery for many years. Later, he embraced secular life as a renowned painter, crafting works that emphasize bold simplicity. His masterpiece, 'Flowers and Birds,' comprised twelve ink-on-paper leaves and recently fetched HK$61.9 million at Christie's Hong Kong auction.

Musical performances and dancing were part of the celebrations aboard the boat, showcasing local talent. Bihar Tourism Minister Kedar Prasad Gupta attended and invited Indians to visit Bihar.

Her business has since gained more than 30,000 social media followers and attracted customers at local events and shops.
