A Chester Zoo collection of Dracula orchids has been declared nationally important, drawing attention to rare flowers with bizarre, vampire-like appearances that are increasingly threatened in the wild.
stories.summary: Chester Zoo recently received National Plant Collection status for its impressive collection of Dracula orchids. These unique flowers, which mimic various shapes, face threats from habitat loss and illegal collection. Pollination occurs through specific fungi-attracting smells rather than traditional scents. Chester Zoo's horticulturists are dedicated to preserving these rare species amidst growing environmental challenges. Currently, the orchids are not on public display but contribute to plant biodiversity conservation efforts.

stories.title: Florida is planning 4,800 acres of wetlands at the mouth of the Kissimmee River to remove phosphorus before it reaches Lake Okeechobee, decades after engineers began undoing the river's earlier straightening
stories.summary: Florida is planning a 4,800-acre wetland project to filter phosphorus pollution before it reaches Lake Okeechobee. This initiative involves directing stormwater through treatment areas filled with aquatic vegetation. Wetlands help mitigate impacts of excess nutrients and support local ecosystems. The project has been under development since 2019 and will provide flood protection and recreational opportunities. A public meeting is scheduled for November 2026 to discuss construction details.

stories.title: A cupboard buried when Mount Vesuvius destroyed Pompeii in AD 79 has yielded 38 bronze coins and at least 24 tiny childhood charms; archaeologists say the objects reveal glimpses of a family's lost everyday life
stories.summary: Italian archaeologists recently uncovered a sealed wooden cupboard in Pompeii, revealing artifacts from 2,000 years ago. Among the findings were 38 bronze coins, personal care items, and a unique childhood necklace. The discovery adds to our understanding of daily life in ancient Rome, highlighting ordinary people's lives. It is speculated that the residents could not retrieve their belongings during the volcanic eruption.

stories.summary: Flavio Bolsonaro left Brazil after his electoral defeat, despite having led in several opinion polls. His departure came after a Brazilian Supreme Court justice ordered his passport revoked. He is also facing two federal money-laundering investigations, while police in Brazil had considered him a flight risk. stories.title: India trying to bring Russia, Ukraine & Europe to the table on 3 fronts: Jaishankar

Different interpretations of energy infrastructure complicate discussions on protection measures.

stories.title: Veiled marble bust sells for record €1.925 million in Vienna
stories.summary: A marble sculpture of a veiled lady created by Antonio Corradini recently sold for €1.925 million. The auction took place in Vienna and set a new world record for the artist. The sculpture is 60 centimeters tall and showcases intricate craftsmanship that mimics the look of cloth. Bidders from the saleroom and via telephone competed for the artwork, but a telephone bidder ultimately won.

stories.title: Florida court overturns order against couple accused of disrupting weddings at a historic mansion
stories.summary: In a significant ruling, a Florida appeals court has reversed a previous order aimed at curbing a couple's disruptive activities that allegedly disrupted outdoor wedding ceremonies with loud machinery and gunfire. The appeals court mandates that any new restrictions must strictly adhere to specific evidence criteria.

stories.title: Maya Jama donates £83,500 to charity after losing Celebrity Traitors, matching her potential prize money

stories.title: Inside UK PM’s Diwali party at his residence; Gita chanting to vegetarian snacks, woman shares

At a rally in Delhi, they highlighted the importance of safeguarding voting rights against authoritarian measures.

stories.title: US river straightened 110 years ago to drain land, now set for restoration to reduce floods
stories.summary: Authorities in Tennessee, US, have acquired 985 acres along the South Fork of the Forked Deer River to reduce flooding and restore natural habitats. The river was straightened in 1916 to drain surrounding land, but the changes contributed to flash floods and erosion. The restoration project aims to reconnect the river with its floodplain and eventually open the area to the public.

stories.title: A new fossil from China may reveal the first amphibian known to have lived entirely at sea; the armoured, 2.4-foot creature lived about 237 million years ago, challenging what scientists know about amphibian evolution
stories.summary: A recent discovery of the fossil Gerrothorax maritimus reveals that some ancient amphibians lived completely in marine environments. Dated to approximately 237 million years ago, this species had a flattened body covered in bony armour. The fossils were found in deep-sea sediments, indicating they lived far from landmasses. Geochemical tests confirmed the strontium isotopes matched those in seawater during the Late Triassic period.

stories.title: 'PM Modi, Amit Shah suffering loss': Sanjay Raut on business concerns of traders ahead of INDIA bloc rally

stories.title: NASA-funded study reveals 4.1-billion-year-old history of pink Martian rock found in Sahara

stories.title: Hope Diamond Mailed To Museum: Harry Winston posts $1 million gem; plain parcel reshapes its legacy
stories.summary: The Hope Diamond embarked on a remarkable journey in 1958 when it was sent as registered mail to the Smithsonian Institution for safekeeping. This precious gem, with its origins in India, has a captivating royal history. American jeweller Harry Winston generously donated it to the museum after obtaining it from Evalyn Walsh McLean's estate in 1949.

stories.title: 'Indira Gandhi's assassination cannot justify 1984 anti-Sikh riots': Hardeep Puri ahead of 42nd anniversary
stories.summary: Union minister Hardeep Singh Puri spoke out about the lasting impact of the 1984 anti-Sikh riots, firmly stating that no justification exists for the violence inflicted upon the Sikh community. He lamented the tragic toll and enduring pain endured by victims while commending HS Phoolka's tireless efforts for justice. The fight for accountability persists as the search for answers continues decades later.

stories.title: 82% disapprove of Trump. So why are fewer Indian Americans identifying as Democrats?
stories.summary: Ahead of the November 3 US midterms, fresh polling shows Indian-Americans strongly favour Democrats on the economy and in congressional races. But a six-year decline in Democratic identification, growing political exhaustion and dissatisfaction with both parties suggest a more complicated relationship with the party.

In 1901,sponge divers off the Greek island of Antikythera recovered a gear from 2,000 years ago
stories.summary: In 1900, a remarkable discovery was made when divers stumbled upon the Antikythera Mechanism amidst a shipwreck in the Mediterranean Sea. This ancient artifact showcased astounding knowledge of astronomy and mechanical engineering dating back over 2,000 years. Researchers found it capable of calculating astronomical cycles and predicting eclipses, intertwining science with the cultural tapestry of ancient Greece.

stories.title: In 2003, archaeologists in London found a tin pot nearly 2,000 years old full of face cream
stories.summary: In a remarkable find in 2003, archaeologists unveiled a cosmetic cream container dating back almost 2,000 years in London. Composed of animal fat, starch, and tin oxide, this ancient formula likely served as a moisturizer. Researchers painstakingly recreated the cream to explore its texture and look on the skin, shedding light on the beauty rituals of the past and our enduring human connection to history.

stories.title: 'Keep Rahul Gandhi mock PM for life': BJP's dig at INDIA bloc's 'public impeachment' of CEC
stories.summary: BJP national spokesperson Sambit Patra, who is MP from Puri Lok Sabha constituency, called the "mock parliament" a "drama", and highlighted that the Speical Intensive Revision (SIR) was ongoing and substantiated the claims around the "13 crore delted voters". Earlier, Amit Shah challenged the INDIA bloc to discuss the issue during a special session of Parliament.

Evening newswrap: INDIA bloc holds 'public impeachment' of Gyanesh Kumar; Class 10 girl attacked with chainsaw in Andhra Pradesh, and all news
'Guilty of centralising electoral rolls': Mallikarjun Kharge lists 6 charges against CEC Gyanesh Kumar, makes 3 demands
stories.summary: Mallikarjun Kharge has initiated a significant public impeachment against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar, charging him with vote theft through six detailed allegations, including the controversial deletion of voters and the centralization of electoral authority. The opposition also sought CEC Gyanesh Kumar's removal and an end to the SIR exercise.

stories.title: Man Turns 600-Sq-Ft Apartment Plant Business Into Million-Dollar Venture in Six Years
stories.summary: Brandon Hurst began his journey into plant selling in 2020 as a side project to boost his income. What started as a small venture has blossomed into a thriving family enterprise, with annual sales surpassing 100,000 plants. Leveraging social media, he incorporated livestream auctions that dramatically boosted profits. Now operating from a vast 3,000-square-foot greenhouse in Los Angeles, Hurst aims to expand while ensuring meaningful connections with his customers.

stories.title: Buyers' promise to save Melbourne family home moves longtime owners to tears
stories.summary: In a heartfelt farewell, a Melbourne couple bid adieu to their beloved Maidstone home, a cherished sanctuary for over four decades after immigrating from Lebanon in 1982. Reassured by the buyers' intention to cherish the house rather than demolish it, the couple found solace in their memories. This sale marks a poignant shift as they prepare to embrace a new chapter in Taylors Lakes.

stories.title: In 2014, the 5.5-carat Ocean Dream sold for about $8.5 million; in May 2026 the same blue-green diamond, the largest of its kind known, sold at Christie’s Geneva for $17.3 million, roughly double
stories.summary: Ocean Dream, a unique blue-green diamond weighing 5.50 carats, was auctioned at Christie's Geneva for $17.3 million. This diamond, initially sold in 2014 for approximately $8.5 million, experienced a significant increase in value. Its distinct colouring results from natural radiation exposure during its geological formation. Notably, the Ocean Dream was previously showcased at the Smithsonian National Museum of Natural History in 2003.

stories.title: Persson Lists Beverly Hills Mansion: asks $70 million again; ultra-luxury LA market cools
stories.summary: Markus Persson, the mastermind behind Minecraft, is putting his lavish Beverly Hills mansion on the market for $70 million. This expansive property boasts eight bedrooms and 15 bathrooms, along with one-of-a-kind features like a candy room and a nightclub. Acquired in December 2014 after selling Mojang to Microsoft, this listing highlights both the opulence of the home and the difficulties of navigating the high-end Los Angeles real estate landscape.

stories.title: UK PM rejects slavery reparations despite Caribbean demands, open to formal apology
stories.summary: The transatlantic slave trade lasted from the 15th to the 19th century, during which millions of Africans were captured, transported and sold into slavery by European traders. According to the Transatlantic Slave Trade Database, Britain transported an estimated 3.2 million Africans across the Atlantic. At least 12.5 million Africans were abducted and forced into the trade.

stories.title: 'Intention is to ensure EC works impartially': Mallikarjun Kharge moves CEC removal motion in mock parliament - top quotes
'It's done bro': J&K CM Omar Abdullah marries Nidhi Razdan; shares photos of 'new journey'
Georgia woman wins $975,000 after falling at Walmart, but appeals court overturns verdict
stories.summary: A Georgia woman who won $975,000 after a fall at a Walmart store in 2020 will face a new trial after an appeals court overturned the verdict on October 29. The court found that her lawyer had improperly compared compensation for pain and suffering with an expert witness's $8,000 daily fee and minimum-wage rates. Judges ruled that these unrelated comparisons could have influenced the jury's decision.

stories.title: First Phase Restoration: Basilica’s $7.7m repairs halt leaks; visitors face limited hours
stories.summary: The historic basilica in Asheville, North Carolina, recently marked the successful completion of its first restoration phase, costing $7.7 million. This essential initiative concentrated on addressing water damage and safeguarding the architectural masterpiece. Key upgrades included the replacement of the copper dome and reinforcing key masonry sections, paving the way for future restoration phases that rely on ongoing fundraising efforts and the building's status as a cultural treasure.

stories.title: Man And Bear Sanctuary: Bosnian electrician’s rescue reshapes family home; future of bears uncertain
stories.summary: In 2019, electrician Petar Tubic stumbled upon a deserted bear cub named Masa in the woods. Over time, he nurtured Masa, eventually establishing a sanctuary for rescued animals, which now includes an additional bear, Ljubica. However, Tubic is troubled by their strong human bonds, raising concern over the bears' future. The sanctuary has transformed into a community attraction and draws attention to the complexities involved in wildlife rescue.

stories.title: In the 1960s, scientists studying the venom of Brazilian pit viper found a compound lowered BP
stories.summary: The Brazilian pit viper, Bothrops jararaca, has been a focal point in research leading to significant medical breakthroughs. In the 1960s, Sergio Ferreira uncovered a peptide from this snake that plays a crucial role in blood pressure regulation. This groundbreaking discovery eventually paved the way for captopril, the pioneering ACE inhibitor approved in 1981, which has transformed the treatment landscape for hypertension and heart ailments.

stories.title: UK PM Burnham signals possible apology for Britain’s role in slave trade
'Already been uprooted': Akhilesh, Awadhesh target Amit Shah over 'Angad's foot' remark
stories.summary: Akhilesh Yadav condemned Amit Shah's claims about the BJP's stronghold in Uttar Pradesh, pointing out the alarming rise in violence against women and Dalits. Responding to Shah's confidence in the BJP's future following recent electoral defeats, MP Awadhesh Prasad underscored the party's vulnerabilities. Shah also emphasized the intent to implement the Uniform Civil Code as part of the BJP's agenda, highlighting the shifting political landscape in the state.

stories.title: Hundreds evacuated from Oleshky as Melania Trump brokers rare Russia-Ukraine ceasefire
stories.summary: Hundreds of residents were evacuated from the Russian-occupied town of Oleshky during a humanitarian ceasefire. The evacuation allowed individuals to leave amidst dire conditions of starvation and exhaustion. Three planes carrying evacuees successfully landed at an airport in Belarus as part of a coordinated operation. Both Russian and Ukrainian authorities confirmed the operation was conducted without any incidents.

stories.title: India's roads kill quietly while crashes in the sky make headlines
stories.summary: A tragic helicopter crash in Uttarakhand resulted in six fatalities, reigniting urgent discussions on aviation safety. Daily road accidents claim over 500 lives, underscoring a critical transport issue. While train accidents have decreased, thousands still fall victim to railway incidents each year. The increase in smaller aircraft accidents highlights a concerning trend, although aviation remains statistically safer than road travel.

Court revives Pennsylvania couple's six-year fight to add drive-through at truck stop
stories.summary: After almost six years of legal back-and-forth, a Pennsylvania convenience store finally received the go-ahead for a drive-through window. Jyotsna and Anil Jivani's 2020 proposal faced initial denial from township officials. However, in a significant ruling from the Pennsylvania Commonwealth Court in October 2026, judges overturned the lower court's verdict, affirming that the drive-through serves as a natural extension of their business, paving the way for construction approval.

stories.title: 'Won't move forward without public': Arunachal CM Pema Khandu amid protests over Siang mega dam
stories.summary: Arunachal Pradesh CM Pema Khandu has assured residents that the proposed 11,200-MW Siang hydropower project will not be imposed on them, saying a decision will be taken only after its feasibility report is completed. The project, seen as a strategic counter to China's mega dam upstream, faces opposition from indigenous Adi communities over displacement, submergence of villages and environmental concerns.

UK Supreme Court rejects Rogano restaurant’s lost profit claim
stories.summary: Glasgow's renowned Rogano restaurant faced catastrophic circumstances after being ravaged by both flooding and fire, leading to its permanent closure. Forthwell Limited aimed to claim lost earnings for Lynnet Leisure, but the UK Supreme Court dismissed their case, stating that the legal exception they sought wasn't applicable in Scots law.

stories.title: Judge Blocks Farm Amphitheater: court backs conservation easement; landowner may appeal
stories.summary: A recent ruling by a Superior Court judge has put the brakes on the proposed outdoor amphitheater at Union Grove Farm, North Carolina. The Triangle Land Conservancy raised alarms over land-use regulations intended to safeguard agricultural landscapes. This dispute stems from a conservation easement put in place during the 1990s, underscoring the ongoing conflict between developmental ambitions and environmental protection in the area.

stories.title: US organ donation group faces decertification after Kentucky man’s near-fatal ordeal
stories.summary: TJ Hoover II's case raised critical alarms when he showed signs of life just before organ retrieval, prompting intense scrutiny of patient safety protocols. Testimony from Donna Rhorer revealed disturbing insights about operational practices. Federal investigations uncovered multiple alarming incidents, leading to possible decertification for the Network for Hope, as the family demands accountability.

Atlanta Bilateral Meeting: Jaishankar meets Rubio on G20 FMM sidelines; focus on India–US cooperation
stories.summary: External affairs minister S Jaishankar had a productive meeting with US secretary of state Marco Rubio in Atlanta to explore avenues for enhanced bilateral ties. They shared reflections from their recent talks during the G20 foreign ministers' summit. Jaishankar's itinerary also included dialogues with both the US ambassador to India and India's ambassador to the US, highlighting active diplomatic channels.

stories.title: Florida installs 1,500 tons of recycled concrete to create three artificial reefs in Gulf waters
stories.summary: Workers are currently deploying three million pounds of recycled concrete drainage pipes to create artificial reefs on the seabed. This innovative project intends to boost marine habitats for local fish species, enhancing both fishing and diving experiences. Positioned between four and eight nautical miles off East Pass, the varied depths of the sites will facilitate diverse marine life.

stories.summary: Mayar Othman Al Shourbagy, an 11-year-old student from Egypt, won the 10th Arab Reading Challenge. Sheikh Mohammed bin Rashid Al Maktoum presented her with a badge to commemorate her achievement. She read 60 books as part of her preparation for the competition. The challenge attracted over 40 million participants from 60 countries, promoting a culture of reading. Mayar's family and school supported her throughout her reading journey.

stories.title: Chuck Lorre-backed LA charity campus breaks ground on final building after kitchen opening
stories.summary: On October 29, 2026, Project Angel Food initiated construction of the Community Outreach Center in Hollywood. This new building will enhance client services and nutrition education for individuals facing serious illnesses. The project, supported by The Chuck Lorre Family Foundation, aims to expand meal preparation and outreach programs. As part of a multiyear campaign, the expanded facilities will elevate the organisation's role in the Food Is Medicine movement.

stories.title: Scientists covered part of a Chinese glacier with fabric to slow melting
stories.summary: A recent study illustrated that utilizing artificial fabric to cover Dagu Glacier yielded a notable decrease in ice melting, with a remarkable 27% reduction within the initial two months, thereby safeguarding substantial ice reserves. Nevertheless, the fabric's effectiveness diminished over time due to factors such as reduced reflectivity, ultimately resulting in an annual melting reduction of 15%. Researchers also pointed out the practical difficulties in scaling this solution.

stories.title: Couple’s restored 170-year-old Wisconsin grain mill home sells for $750,000
NMC invites applications to empanel 17 standing counsels across Supreme Court, 16 High Court positions
stories.summary: The National Medical Commission is seeking applications for standing counsels aimed at bolstering its legal expertise. Eligible advocates should possess significant experience in medical law and institutional matters before High Courts, meeting defined criteria such as years of practice and court appearances. Selected advocates will be responsible for drafting legal documents, conducting research, and updating on case progress.

stories.title: A first-grade teacher in Kansas started ending each day with children repeating positive affirmations; the simple routine spread beyond his classroom as other teachers adopted the idea
stories.summary: An elementary teacher in Kansas has implemented positive affirmations at the end of each school day. This practice has spread across various grades, enhancing students' sense of belonging and value. While affirmations alone do not replace effective teaching methods, they contribute to a supportive classroom atmosphere. Parents can also foster encouragement in their children by acknowledging their feelings and individuality.

stories.title: Over 42,000 candidates to take FMGE on Saturday; NBEMS deploys 4,500-plus personnel, live CCTV surveillance
stories.summary: This Saturday, over 42,000 aspiring doctors will participate in the Foreign Medical Graduate Examination. The NBEMS has officially registered 42,438 candidates, with 42,109 now holding their admit cards. To ensure a smooth process, more than 4,500 personnel will monitor the exam across 104 centers in 30 states, while a central command center in New Delhi will supervise everything through live CCTV feeds.

Indiana landlord loses $3,800 in apartment damage claim after failing to send notice
stories.summary: An Indiana landlord who won $6,200 from a former tenant over unpaid rent and apartment damage has had the award reduced to $2,400. In an October 29 ruling, the state appeals court found that the landlord had failed to provide the tenant with a written list of damages as required by law. The court allowed the unpaid rent claim but rejected the additional cleaning and repair costs.

Utah Yard Becomes Charity Haunt: Resident builds Terroride-style display; visitors come for the scares
stories.summary: In an imaginative twist on Halloween festivities, Kelly Hertel evolved his childhood fears into an engaging front yard display dubbed Terroride. Generating significant charity donations, the attraction is an elaborate homage to his past. With over 400 hours of meticulous effort, Hertel's themed sections offer both thrilling entertainment and a chance for the community to unite in giving this season.

Nightmare On Moore Street: Boston couple build free Dracula castle; crowds return yearly
stories.summary: In East Boston, a couple has turned their residence into a Halloween wonderland dubbed Nightmare on Moore Street. This extraordinary setup lures visitors from various regions, creating a free, festive atmosphere that delights families and Halloween lovers alike. Utilizing hand-carved foam and chilling light effects, they've crafted a captivating experience for all ages.

Clooney foundation provides free legal aid to 9,000 women and children, expands mobile clinics
stories.summary: The Clooney Foundation for Justice is dedicated to empowering women and girls by providing them with free legal assistance. Since its establishment, over 9,000 women and children have benefitted from these crucial legal services. Partnering with local organizations, they have set up mobile legal clinics in underserved areas, ensuring wider accessibility.

stories.summary: A federal judge has sanctioned a settlement of $47.75 million in a securities lawsuit involving Hawaiian Electric Industries. This case focused on accusations of misleading wildfire preparedness disclosures. The judge notably slashed the legal fees demanded by the investors' attorneys. From over 67,000 claims submitted, only more than 24,000 were approved, highlighting a substantial rejection rate. Payments to eligible claimants will proceed according to a loss-based distribution strategy.

stories.summary: By 2026, Robin Rinearson’s ventures, Jake’s Ice Cream and Jake’s Gourmet Popcorn, have emerged as crucial employers for individuals with disabilities. With 35 staff members, these businesses emphasize skills enhancement and sustainable positions. Employees express fulfillment in their jobs and frequently refer friends for openings. A notable waiting list represents the success of Rinearson's inclusive hiring efforts, earning recognition for fostering a supportive community for disabled individuals.

stories.summary: Prince William and Kate Middleton may have been made aware of serious allegations against Meghan Markle’s father, Thomas Markle Sr., after a letter was reportedly sent to their shared Kensington Palace office in 2019. The development comes as police investigate separate claims involving suspected child sexual abuse images found at his former home in the Philippines.

stories.title: Isro’s GSLV-F18/NVS-03 mission successful: Next-generation navigation satellite placed in orbit; NavIC constellation gets a boost
stories.summary: GSLV-F18 carrying 2,250kg next-generation navigation satellite -- NVS-03 -- lifted off from the second launch pad at the Satish Dhawan Space Centre (SDSC-SHAR) in Sriharikota at 11.51pm on Friday, as scheduled. Around 18 minutes later, NVS-03 satellite was placed in a geosynchronous transfer orbit (GTO) of 37,023km apogee and 170km perigee.

stories.title: Green Card lottery: Judge freezes reopening of Diversity Visa program for 2027. What happens next?
New York appeals court blocks tenants' $321,728 mould damage claim over delays and missing proof
stories.summary: Recently, a New York appeals court dismissed further claims from tenants regarding property damage in their ongoing case. The court determined that the tenants significantly postponed presenting evidence for their $321,728.79 claim linked to health problems from mould exposure, which initially surfaced in 2018. Adding such claims post-discovery was seen as prejudicial to the landlord, but the case will continue with original personal injury allegations.

Kate Winslet joins Storyline Online, reads Room On The Broom
stories.summary: In a delightful initiative by Storyline Online, Kate Winslet recently narrated 'Room on the Broom,' a whimsical story that encourages literacy among children. Featuring a witch and her feline companion, the tale emphasizes themes of generosity and camaraderie, perfect for the Halloween spirit. Winslet's animated narration captivates young audiences, making reading a joy. With various celebrities contributing, Storyline Online provides a treasure trove of literature for families and schools alike.

Scotland’s AirShip 002 Holiday Rental Business Listed for Over £750,000
stories.summary: AirShip 002, a remarkable holiday retreat nestled in the picturesque Morvern Peninsula of Scotland, is now available for over £750,000. This architecturally stunning property not only attracts international visitors but also yields impressive income streams. Included in the sale are two additional lodgings, paving the way for potential success in the hospitality sector. Buyers will benefit from established operations and a commitment to community engagement and sustainable tourism practices.

stories.title: New York’s High Line to Open Final Garden Featuring 2,000 Perennials in November
stories.summary: This November, New York City's High Line will unveil its final garden at West 34th Street, culminating a transformative journey from an old freight line to a vibrant public park. Boasting 2,000 perennials alongside newly paved pathways and informative signage, this garden is distinctive in its grounded plantings. When finished, the High Line will welcome millions of annual visitors to enjoy its beauty and tranquility.

stories.title: ‘Class 12-pass mafia’: Bengal LoP Ritabrata Banerjee hits back at Abhishek's warning to cops
stories.summary: Ritabrata Banerjee has responded strongly to Abhishek Banerjee's warning issued to West Bengal police officers. He accused Abhishek of arrogance and urged the state government to take action against him. Additionally, Ritabrata challenged Abhishek to visit a temple alone without security, disputing his claim of public support. Abhishek had recently expressed concerns about police targeting TMC workers and claimed to have a list of implicated officers.

Woman's 1981 land investment helps protect 140 acres of Canadian island forest 45 years later
stories.summary: Domena Diesing took a significant step by investing her grandmother's legacy to safeguard 140 acres of Lasqueti Island, Canada. By teaming up with the BC Parks Foundation, she secured a permanent conservation status for the land, enhancing a vast connected reserve now exceeding 1,000 acres in the Salish Sea. This project commemorates Alfred Gaensbauer’s enduring dedication to environmental preservation, ensuring a legacy of rich coastal habitats for generations to come.

Penn's Cave, family-owned since 1908, goes up for sale for $34 million after 118 years
stories.summary: The Campbell family has put Penn's Cave and Wildlife Park in Centre Hall up for sale, ending a remarkable 118-year legacy. With a listing price of $34 million, this expansive estate includes an impressive limestone cave system, a vibrant wildlife park, and a private airport. As the sale process begins, state officials in Pennsylvania are looking into potential conservation strategies, with the family promising a smooth transition of current operations.

stories.title: Martha Washington’s 1760 Letter About Daughter’s Illness Sells for $47,500, Joins Library of Congress
stories.summary: A personal letter from Martha Washington, describing her daughter's recovery, has found a new home at the Library of Congress. This 1760 correspondence, directed to Margaret Green, sheds light on Martha's motherhood journey and is the first handwritten piece by her in the library's archives. Its acquisition underscores women's vital roles during colonial America, adding depth alongside Mary Todd Lincoln's letters.

How two US friends turned a small haunted house into a multimillion-dollar Halloween business
stories.summary: Two friends, Chris Stafford and Warren Conard, opened a haunted house in a Denver shopping complex in 2002, charging $15 per ticket. What began as a side business has grown into a multimillion-dollar company with 18 seasonal Halloween attractions across the US. The company paid around 4,500 workers during the 2025 Halloween season and is now expanding into Christmas entertainment.

stories.title: 17-Year-Old’s Campaign Against Plastic Cutlery Prevents 8.1 Million Single-Use Utensils
stories.summary: Landon Hoberman, a 17-year-old from New Jersey, has made remarkable strides in reducing plastic cutlery usage in restaurants. His campaign has succeeded in keeping over 8 million utensils out of landfills, while restaurants collectively saved more than $200,000 by making cutlery optional for takeaway. This initiative showcases how small changes can lead to significant environmental impact and financial savings, presenting a scalable model for communities seeking to tackle single-use plastics.

stories.summary: Sophia Parekh, a 12-year-old from Westfield, New Jersey, has distributed more than 8,000 free books to children across the US through Sophia's Book Stand, a project she started at age seven during the Covid pandemic. She personally selects books based on children's ages and interests and also supports teachers in underserved schools. Her efforts earned her recognition as a runner-up for the 2026 Gloria Barron Prize for Young Heroes.

stories.title: 'No' to peace bond, 'yes' to INDIA bloc: Has Neha Bora outsmarted CJP leaders?

Established in 1995, this program ensures that young readers receive free books every month until the age of five, proudly distributing over four million books to date.

stories.summary: Pradhan Mantri Viksit Bharat Rozgar Yojana (PMVBRY) is introduced to enhance formal employment across various sectors. Lost Renaissance plaques found in English home sell for £100,000 after 142 years
stories.summary: A pair of exquisite 16th-century maiolica plaques by renowned artist Francesco Xanto Avelli recently fetched an impressive £100,000 at auction after lying unnoticed in a Dorset home for years. The family unearthed these extraordinary pieces while seeking expert advice, discovering they were part of a significant series illustrating the tale of Cyrus the Great. This auction underscores the remarkable rarity and cultural value of these Italian Renaissance treasures.

stories.title: Quebec home built from 200,000 recycled bottles, assembled in just three days
stories.summary: In a remarkable development, a two-bedroom house located in Saint-Rémi-d'Amherst, Quebec, has been built using an innovative construction method known as PakVert. This technique employs panels crafted from recycled plastic bottles, resulting in a building process that took merely three days. By minimizing construction waste and cutting costs by approximately 35 percent, this initiative contributes significantly to affordable housing and environmental sustainability in Canada.

Husband’s home valuation rejected in Tennessee divorce appeal
stories.summary: In a contentious marital dispute, a Tennessee appeals court confirmed the trial court's assessment of a marital home valued at $160,400, awarding the wife 75% of the home's equity—approximately $47,139. The husband's higher valuation based on comparable sales was dismissed by the court. Moreover, the court invalidated the husband's artwork and tool valuations, mandating their reassessment. It also made essential amendments to the permanent parenting plan concerning visitation rights.

Search and rescue teams were deployed to locate the crash site amid adverse weather conditions, including heavy rain and snowfall.

Did Lacy misunderstand his Japan restaurant bill? Streamer reveals what actually happened
stories.summary: Twitch streamer Nick "Lacy" has addressed a mix-up involving a $12,000 restaurant bill he thought he owed in Japan. Initially confused due to language issues, he later discovered he was only responsible for extra food. Realizing the impact of his comments, Lacy has since apologized to the restaurant for inadvertently causing them negative publicity and acknowledged the necessity of clearer communication.

stories.title: Brittany and Patrick Mahomes’ Allergy-Friendly Restaurant Gets First Approval in Kansas City
stories.summary: Brittany Mahomes is spearheading a valuable initiative aimed at enhancing food allergy safety in restaurants throughout Kansas City with the 15 and FARE program. This initiative educates both eateries and locals on effective allergy management, with Joe's KC proudly becoming the first restaurant to earn this designation by implementing crucial safety practice improvements.

stories.title: 'A win is a win': Israel opposition leader Lapid reacts to Netanyahu's poll setback
stories.summary: Yair Lapid stated that the anti-Netanyahu bloc won the election while indicating the need for coalition talks. The bloc secured 67 seats in the Knesset, insufficient for a majority. Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's coalition obtained 53 seats, lacking a clear path to govern. Lapid emphasized the importance of patience during the ongoing discussions amidst uncertainty. He assured the public that negotiations are active, though results may not be immediately visible.

Scientists discover silk traces on 101 ancient objects in China, uncover clues to ancient rituals
stories.summary: Scientists studying 3,000-year-old objects from China's Sanxingdui archaeological site have found silk traces on 101 artefacts, including bronze masks, gold, jade and ivory objects. Published in the journal Antiquity, the study suggests that ancient Shu people used silk to wrap or cover objects during rituals. Researchers also identified red pigments and different weaving patterns, offering clues about ancient textile practices.

stories.title: INDIA bloc postpones 'public impeachment' of CEC Gyanesh Kumar due to rains
'Modi nahi jayenge' slogan raised at PM's Gujarat event; Congress retorts, 'you wish!'
stories.summary: Prime Minister Narendra Modi visited the Bharat Bovine Breeding and Research Centre in Gujarat on Friday, unveiling development projects totaling over Rs 14,000 crore. He also released the latest PM-KISAN installment, benefiting farmers with Rs 19,000 crore. The trip included plans to enhance Ahmedabad's metro network and state roads, while also announcing new initiatives for the dairy and childcare sectors.

stories.title: Appeals court revives lawsuit over eyewear retailer sharing customer data with Meta
Australia’s stingless bees may help fight antibiotic resistance
stories.summary: Researchers at the University of Sydney are investigating the medicinal properties of honey from stingless bees. The honey has shown effectiveness against various bacterial and fungal pathogens, including difficult-to-treat strains. Findings suggest that sugarbag honey is comparable in strength to well-known medical-grade honeys. While propolis displayed selective antimicrobial activity, the reason for honey's potency remains unclear. Further research is needed to identify the beneficial compounds within the honey.

stories.title: Arkansas couple pays $8,000 for access to landlocked property, loses court battle with neighbours
stories.summary: An Arkansas couple who paid their neighbours $8,000 for an 18-foot-wide road to access their land near Beaver Lake have lost a dispute over its location. The Arkansas Court of Appeals upheld a route along the neighbours' property boundary, despite concerns about construction costs and difficult terrain. One judge disagreed, warning that the approved route could be unusable without expensive work.

stories.title: German teacher on sick leave for 16 years, collected nearly €1 million in salary; now faces fraud charges over €248,000
stories.summary: A 62-year-old German educator faces fraud charges after reportedly taking a 16-year sick leave, during which she allegedly collected over €248,000 in salary. Investigators believe she fabricated medical documentation to support her prolonged absence from the classroom. Although she engaged in scuba diving, there’s no evidence of her undertaking any other professional work. The court is currently reviewing the case to determine if a full trial is warranted.

stories.title: Israel election results: Neither Netanyahu nor oppn wins majority; what happens next?
stories.summary: Israel faces a political deadlock after Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's bloc fell short of the 61 seats needed for a majority. With Arab-led parties holding 19 seats, opposition leader Gadi Eisenkot could seek their support to form a government. However, ideological differences complicate the numbers. A unity government, opposition defections or another election are among four possible scenarios, according to CNN.

University of Georgia secures $8 million NOAA grant to plan restoration of acres of salt marsh
stories.summary: University of Georgia has received an $8 million grant to restore salt marsh habitat across four coastal states. The initiative, which spans from North Carolina to Florida, will assess the use of dredged sediment. This project aims to elevate marshes and support diverse wildlife while addressing rising sea levels and pollution. Proposed restoration sites include Bird-Long Island, Cape Lookout National Seashore, Cape Romain National Wildlife Refuge, and Julia’s Island.

stories.summary: An Ohio appellate court has confirmed a zoning restriction prohibiting short-term rentals in a suburban area. Michael A. Clevenger, an owner looking to operate an Airbnb, faced opposition from neighbors concerned about excessive noise, parking congestion, and heightened safety risks from frequent guests. This ruling emphasizes the importance of adhering to local zoning regulations that maintain the integrity of residential neighborhoods, reinforcing existing legal frameworks against short-term rental operations.

stories.title: A $295 million Malibu mansion by Pritzker Prize-winning architect Tadao Ando was quietly on the market when Kanye West came unannounced
stories.summary: Kanye West made an unplanned visit to a stunning Malibu mansion crafted by Tadao Ando, spending four days there. He secured a stay without prior arrangement, likening his presence to that of Elvis Presley. Meanwhile, the estate was later sold to Jay-Z and Beyoncé, breaking sales records. West's personal Ando-designed property, however, is grappling with legal and financial troubles, leaving its future uncertain due to ongoing foreclosure issues.

stories.title: Maine Forest Protections Secure Jobs: Coalition preserves 27,000 acres; working forest still supports timber, recreation
stories.summary: In a remarkable achievement, over 27,000 acres of forestland in western Maine have been safeguarded through collaborative conservation efforts. This extensive initiative spanned six years, bringing together environmental groups, state agencies, and local trusts. Preserving this land is vital for ensuring clean drinking water for more than 200,000 residents while supporting timber jobs and enhancing recreational opportunities and habitats for wildlife in the area.

He noted the potential of emerging technologies like AI to enhance maritime security while also posing new risks. The representative emphasized the need for safeguards and clear responsibility regarding technological deployment.

stories.title: Once a textile giant, now homes and offices: Virginia’s abandoned mill gets a $110 million makeover
stories.summary: Dan River Falls embodies a transformative redevelopment of the historic White Mill, originally constructed in 1920, located in Danville. Completed in November 2024, the first phase features 190 residential apartments. Plans for the future include developing a vibrant riverfront park and retail area. This public-private collaboration strives to maintain the mill's historic integrity while breathing new life into the community and catering to workforce housing needs.

stories.title: Cleopatra’s eye makeup secret? Ancient Egyptians used lead-based kohl
stories.summary: In ancient Egypt, kohl was more than just a cosmetic; it served dual purposes, enhancing beauty while protecting the eyes. Studies indicate that its ingredients could boost immune responses, making it a valuable tool for health. Both men and women embraced the use of black and green powders, and ancient texts highlight the fusion of cosmetics with medicine, revealing the intricate beliefs surrounding beauty and wellness in that era.

stories.title: Common daily fiber supplement was found to significantly reduce knee pain and improve strength
stories.summary: A recent study from the University of Nottingham unveils exciting findings regarding inulin supplementation for knee osteoarthritis. Participants not only experienced a reduction in joint pain, but they also enhanced their grip strength and sensitivity to pain. This research underscores the intriguing link between gut health and joint management, suggesting that dietary strategies might positively affect physical capabilities beyond just the painful areas.

stories.title: Normal blood pressure may not tell the whole story: Scientists discover a brain ‘switch’
stories.summary: Hypertension impacts approximately 1.4 billion adults across the globe, with numerous individuals unaware of their status. A recent study by the University of Virginia uncovers essential brain cells responsible for maintaining stable blood pressure. These cells contribute to consistent blood pressure levels during daily activities and may mitigate abrupt changes.

The discovery of his body underneath a hearth, with a stone in his mouth, implies an effort to silence him.

stories.title: How UKHarvest turned food waste into 10 million meals

This ecological transformation highlights the beneficial effects of eradicating invasive species, fostering a healthier food web and aiding in the survival of native bird species. Long-term observation is crucial for comprehending the recovery dynamics of island ecosystems.

stories.title: Texas’s Historic Imperial Sugar Char House Gets $15M Rescue After 20 Years Vacant
stories.summary: Sugar Land City Council has given a green light for a $15 million initiative to safeguard the iconic Imperial Sugar Char House. stories.title: Taking antibiotics? Eating a lot of sugar at the same time may make the damage to your gut worse, scientists have found, suggesting that what you eat during a course of antibiotics could affect how well your body recovers
stories.summary: Research findings indicate that a diet high in sugar can significantly affect the diversity of gut bacteria in patients undergoing antibiotic therapy. The study monitored the food intake and gut microbiome of hospitalized cancer patients treated with broad-spectrum antibiotics, revealing a strong connection between elevated sugar levels and shifts in gut bacteria.

stories.title: In 1987, an amateur fossil hunter found a T. rex in South Dakota; the $31.8 million skeleton now stands in Abu Dhabi
stories.summary: In 1987, Stan Sacrison found a T. rex skeleton in South Dakota, which was later sold for $31.8 million. Initially misidentified, the bones were correctly recognized as belonging to a T. rex in 1992. After years at the Black Hills Institute, the skeleton was auctioned and purchased for a museum in Abu Dhabi. Stan is now displayed in a dramatic scene depicting conflicts with another T. rex.

Texas Jury Finds No Legal or Informal Adoption in $1 Million Inheritance Dispute
stories.summary: In a complex Texas inheritance case, a stepson referred to as 'my child' in a will navigated a treacherous dispute following his father's passing. Despite his claims of informal adoption, the family remained unconvinced. Ultimately, the jury affirmed that no formal or informal adoption occurred. This outcome highlights the necessity of clear legal documentation in estate planning to avoid misunderstandings, particularly within blended families concerning rights to inheritance.

stories.title: Steven Spielberg pulls $29.9 M LA ranch off the market
stories.summary: Filmmaker Steven Spielberg listed his Los Angeles ranch for $29.9 million but has now taken it off the market. He and his wife purchased the property in 1999 for $5.75 million, intending to create equestrian facilities. After facing opposition from local residents, their renovation plans were significantly reduced over the years. The ranch, known as Dogwood, features a main house with numerous upscale amenities and a 20,000-square-foot riding arena.

stories.title: In 1600, William Gilbert called Earth a giant magnet; his book sold for Rs 58.5 lakh in 2026
stories.summary: William Gilbert's pivotal publication, De Magnete, emerged in 1600, marking a significant shift in the exploration of magnetism and electricity. It introduced key terms and experimental approaches that influenced future electrical studies. The concept of Earth as a colossal magnet was groundbreaking. Recently, a first edition fetched $61,440 at a Christie’s auction, highlighting its enduring significance and the continued fascination it holds in scientific discourse.

stories.title: In 2022, conservators X-raying a Van Gogh painting in Edinburgh found a hidden self-portrait of the artist on the back of the canvas, concealed for more than a century under layers of glue and cardboard
stories.summary: A self-portrait of Vincent van Gogh was discovered concealed behind another painting after many years. The hidden portrait was found during routine examinations ahead of an exhibition. This discovery highlights Van Gogh's habit of reusing canvases due to financial difficulties throughout his life. Conservators are now working to reveal the portrait without damaging the original painting. Visitors to the exhibition were able to view the hidden portrait's X-ray image.

stories.title: Netanyahu's unity government gambit: Can he lure Eisenkot from opposition?

This shift follows a jury's March 2022 decision that found developers had breached fiduciary duties, prompting residents to reevaluate governance due to rising association fees. The final handover on August 20, 2026, empowers homeowners over shared facilities, symbolizing a hard-won victory for community representation.

stories.title: 'Don't push us': SC warns of harsh stand on firecrackers if orders go unenforced
stories.summary: The Supreme Court tackled the persistent air pollution crisis in Delhi-NCR, stressing the importance of adhering to current firecracker laws. Authorities were cautioned against inaction, as deteriorating air quality poses a threat to public health. The bench underlined the necessity for collaboration among all parties to effectively manage firecracker usage. Measures taken by the Delhi government include restrictions on older vehicles and staggered work hours.

stories.title: A 3,106-carat diamond pulled from a South African mine became the 530-carat gem in Britain's royal sceptre
stories.summary: Frederick Wells discovered the enormous Cullinan diamond in South Africa in 1905 while working at the Premier Mine. Its exceptional size caught public attention, leading to its purchase by the Transvaal government for King Edward VII. The diamond was carefully cut into several gemstones over eight months, resulting in noteworthy pieces for the British royal collection. Following Edward VII's death, the largest stone was incorporated into the Sovereign's Sceptre.

stories.title: An Indy charity started in 2016 with $9k raised in 45 mins; 10 yrs on, it reached 175k bouquets
stories.summary: Random Acts of Flowers Indianapolis marked ten years of service, delivering its 175,000th flower arrangement to Eskenazi Health. This charity reuses donated flowers to create arrangements for hospital patients in need. Volunteers collect flowers from various local sources to prevent waste and support emotional well-being. The organization was founded after a successful fundraising effort in 2016. It aims to continue its work through community partnerships and ongoing donations.

stories.title: Newly identified bird like dinosaur from Cretaceous period may be first dinosaur eating fruit
stories.summary: Scientists have recently uncovered a small dinosaur named Infernogallus jamesi, believed to have predominantly dined on fruit. By examining its skull and jaw muscles, researchers gained insights into its dietary habits. Existing during the Cretaceous period, as flowering plants flourished, this dinosaur displays anatomical traits akin to modern fruit-feeding parrots, deepening our comprehension of the varied lifestyles in the era of dinosaurs.

stories.title: 'Educated voters don't turn up in assembly polls': UP minister OP Rajbhar plays down MLC results

The palace added that he would “not shy away from the darkest days of our past.” As monarch, Charles represents Britain abroad on the advice of the government.

stories.title: The asteroid that wiped out the dinosaurs 66 million years ago may have also set the stage for ants to conquer the planet, with scientists finding a surprising boost from so-called jumping genes hidden in ant DNA
stories.summary: Since the dinosaurs vanished, ants have flourished, with more than 15,000 species recognized globally. New research, spearheaded by Dr. Lukas Schrader, highlights the role of jumping genes in their evolution and resilience. Significant surges of these genes occurred during the early Paleogene period, enhancing ants' olfactory receptors and social communication skills, thus providing a genetic edge for survival in diverse environments.

stories.title: Why do some people stay mentally sharp even when their brains show clear signs of Alzheimer’s disease? Scientists have found an important clue hidden in a rare group of resilient brains
stories.summary: Recent research from the Netherlands Institute for Neuroscience has revealed intriguing findings about Alzheimer's disease. Scientists examined brain tissues from different groups, including those with and without dementia symptoms. They discovered that immature neurons acted differently in cognitively healthy individuals despite Alzheimer's brain changes. This suggests that these neurons may play a role in supporting brain function rather than simply replacing damaged cells.

stories.title: He wrote a book on 'Black Money', Feds tracked his $900K loan fraud: Indian-origin accountant jailed in Texas, investigator says 'I can only imagine his shock...'

He attributed the victory to teachers and young voters while alleging electoral manipulation by the BJP. The Samajwadi Party leader believes this defeat sets the foundation for the upcoming 2027 assembly elections. Yadav emphasized unity among marginalized communities and expressed gratitude towards supporters for their vigilance during the counting process.

stories.title: Mississippi father gives wife home promised to three children; daughter loses court battle
stories.summary: A Mississippi father left his family home and 0.86 acres of land equally to his three children in a 2008 will but transferred the property to his wife in 2021. After his death, his daughter challenged the transfer, claiming he had been improperly influenced due to his declining health. On Tuesday, an appeals court rejected her challenge, finding insufficient evidence of undue influence.

The incident was caused by overcrowding, panic, and a misleading announcement about structural failure. Experts emphasize the importance of effective crowd management to prevent similar tragedies in the future. Investigators are examining various factors contributing to the disaster, including narrow exits and inadequate safety measures.

stories.title: WhatsApp co-founder Jan Koum's $36 million donation helps expand Los Angeles Jewish school
stories.summary: WhatsApp co-founder Jan Koum's $36 million donation has helped Milken Community School open a new campus in Bel Air, Los Angeles, for students in grades 9 to 12. Inaugurated on Sunday, the campus has expanded the school's total footprint to 28 acres across three locations. The opening comes as the school reports a 40% rise in applications.

stories.title: 'What is wrong with victims': CJI on digital arrest cases; calls for compensation from banks
SC disposes of Mahua Moitra's plea seeking public disclosure of AIF, FPI beneficiaries
4-year-old Tennessee boy donates $150 from lemonade stand to soup kitchen
From Hitler’s rise to farmers’ misery in India: How the Great Depression changed lives far beyond America
stories.summary: The October 1929 stock market crash in the United States ignited a global economic disaster that resulted in widespread unemployment and business closures. In Germany and India, the crisis led to heightened political unrest and movements for independence. Falling agricultural prices devastated Indian farmers, pushing them closer to revolution against British oppression. Meanwhile, Britain faced significant industrial downturns and job losses, highlighting the urgent need for international economic collaboration.

stories.title: Sneako reportedly sends legal demand to Akademiks over post about alleged intimate video threat
stories.summary: DJ Akademiks’ platform recently revealed threatening claims involving potential release of intimate videos related to Sneako, which arose from a group call conflict. The legal notification regarding these video allegations lacks independent verification, casting doubt on its legitimacy. Despite a request to eliminate the post, Akademiks TV stood firm on their reporting rights.

stories.title: MLC election results: BJP wins big, but Congress and Samajwadi Party send a message from Nagpur, Varanasi
stories.summary: While the BJP-led NDA won big in the MLC elections across four states, it suffered setbacks in two politically significant constituencies: Nagpur and Varanasi where the Congress and SP held their ground.

stories.title: NJ homeowner challenged neighbour's plunge pool over flooding; appeals court upheld case dismissal
stories.summary: In Toms River, New Jersey, a family contested a neighbour's pool due to flooding fears. David Faloba represented his parents in challenging the project, citing environmental concerns. The court found the DEP had approved the pool based on compliance with relevant regulations. The appellate court upheld the dismissal of Faloba's lawsuit, emphasizing correct legal processes were not followed.

stories.title: Gavin Newsom-linked San Francisco cottage sells for $5.85 million, up from $2.8 million in 2019
stories.summary: A beautifully preserved redwood cottage in San Francisco, formerly owned by the family of Gavin Newsom, has recently fetched $5.85 million at sale. Initially on the market for $4.5 million, the residence located in Cole Valley drew numerous cash offers, driven largely by its spacious potential and the allure tied to its former ownership.

stories.title: ‘This is the future you want?’ White House cites France riots to slam Democrats ahead of midterms
stories.summary: In France, recent demonstrations regarding education and living costs have spiraled into significant unrest and violence. Initially sparked by issues in educational facilities, the protests quickly broadened to encompass widespread frustration with public services. The Trump administration seizes upon these events to castigate Democrats, linking them to growing disorder in America.

stories.title: US releases rare image of China's secretive space plane docked to another spacecraft
stories.summary: A US military intelligence agency has released a rare photograph of China's secretive Shenlong space plane, showing it attached to another spacecraft in orbit. Taken in May 2024 and made public in October 2026, the image reveals its open payload bay and another satellite with extended solar panels. However, the purpose of the connection remains unknown.

stories.title: Why did Kick suspend Vitaly after his latest livestream? Here’s what we know
stories.summary: Recently, streamer Vitaly faced suspension from Kick due to breaches of the platform's endangerment policies during his 'Catching Predators IRL' livestream featuring Lil Pump. While the suspension email referenced specific evidence, it failed to clarify the exact reasons behind the decision. Past incidents related to his controversial predator-catching streams have sparked debate about his approach, and there is still uncertainty regarding the length of the suspension and possible reinstatement.

stories.title: 'Ballot paper, still we ask': Kharge dares BJP to dissolve Parliament after MLC poll setback
'Vote chori' row: INDIA bloc to hold 'mock Parliament' to 'impeach' CEC Gyanesh Kumar; mega rally on Nov 1
Wendy Schmidt's $1.4 million oil-cleanup challenge after Deepwater Horizon
Minnesota neighbours lose $148,500 award as court settles nine-year lake access dispute
stories.summary: A nine-year property dispute over access to Minnesota's Prairie Lake has taken another turn after an appeals court upheld a ruling in favour of the Blackwood Trust. The Monday decision confirms the trust's direct access to the lake and leaves an earlier $148,500 trespass award to neighbouring property owners cancelled. The dispute centred on conflicting land surveys dating back to 1997.

stories.title: 10-year-old Georgia boy raises $400 selling bracelets to help homeless people
A vitamin clue to stroke in the young? Bengaluru study finds low B6 levels
stories.summary: A recent study from Bengaluru finds lower levels of vitamin B6 in young adults with ischaemic strokes compared to healthy individuals. This study involved comparing vitamin B6 levels in 171 stroke patients and 249 healthy controls. Researchers found that vitamin B6 insufficiency was more prevalent among stroke patients than in the control group. Although vitamin B6 is linked to stroke risk, further research is essential to understand the implications.

stories.title: Congress calls Rahul Gandhi's 'Sitarama' misspelling in Tata post 'typo marketing', mocks BJP
Thousands of years of knowledge, struggle shaped India as cultural nation: Gajendra Singh Shekhawat
stories.summary: At the launch of 'Timeless India' held at Dharohar Bhawan, Union Culture Minister Gajendra Singh Shekhawat passionately articulated the essence of India's cultural heritage, which has been shaped through centuries of learning and trials. This book is a clarion call for the preservation of our historical sites and a deeper understanding of our cultural narrative.

stories.title: Demolition damaged Miami home in 2014; Florida court upholds woman's $240,000 insurance victory after 12 years
stories.summary: In Florida, Sandra Moise faced significant challenges when her home was damaged due to vibrations from nearby demolition activities. Initially, her insurance provider, Homeowners Choice, denied her claim citing policy exclusions against earth movement. After enduring a prolonged legal battle, a jury ultimately sided with her, confirming the damage's cause.

stories.title: At 62, Marcelle Flowers feared AI until two young founders changed her career
California couple's garden dispute ends in court after 1955 deal involving $250 and babysitting
stories.summary: A California couple who bought a home in 2019 found themselves in a legal battle after their neighbour claimed ownership of a 20-by-20-foot garden they believed was theirs. The dispute centred on a 1955 agreement involving $250, babysitting services and land access rights. On Monday, a California appeals court upheld the couple's exclusive right to use the garden.

stories.title: US midterms: FBI, ICE agents will not serve as election monitors, DOJ says
stories.summary: The US Department of Justice has decided that FBI personnel will not oversee polling sites during upcoming elections. Concerns were raised regarding potential intimidation of voters, especially from minority communities. Civil rights groups, led by the NAACP, filed a lawsuit to prevent federal law enforcement at polling places. Federal election monitors will be present but will not have law enforcement powers.

stories.title: Forces fortify key Arunachal bridge to fight dam objectors
stories.summary: Protests against the dam at the Dite-Dime bridge have prompted a strong response from law enforcement. The Central Armed Police Forces have been deployed to ensure order in the affected districts. Recent confrontations during a bandh left several people injured, including four women, escalating tensions. As supporters clashed with security, the Dite-Dime bridge emerges as a focal point of strife near the India-China border.

stories.title: Washington appeals court upholds anti-harassment order after neighbour allegedly disrupts utilities
stories.summary: A dispute between a couple and their neighbour escalated into serious harassment concerning driveway access and utilities. The couple claimed that their neighbour blocked the shared driveway and cut off their water supply. This pattern of interference led them to seek legal protection from the court. The Washington Court of Appeals confirmed that their claims warranted an anti-harassment order.

stories.title: Cyclone Arnab: Amit Shah speaks to four CMs, says relief operations on 'war footing'
stories.summary: Amidst the aftermath of Cyclone Arnab, Union home minister Amit Shah coordinated efforts with chief ministers of the impacted states, pledging essential assistance to alleviate the disaster's effects. With nine fatalities reported in Andhra Pradesh, evacuations were necessary, and significant crop damage affected about 2 lakh hectares. Restoration work is underway, with unwavering support from the central government for the affected regions.

stories.title: An animal-borne virus called Shamonda, which normally circulates in livestock, has infected and killed a human for the first time
stories.summary: A 61-year-old man in France has tragically lost his life to the Shamonda virus, a disease previously only observed in animals. The man, who was battling leukaemia, contracted the virus likely through a midge bite. With documented cases of infected animals in Europe and previous outbreaks in Africa and Asia, health officials are investigating how the virus spreads and its possible risks to humans.

stories.title: North Carolina city restores 27 acres of wetlands to reduce flood risks for 93 properties
stories.summary: Hendersonville celebrates the successful completion of the first phase of its Lower Mud Creek Floodplain Restoration Project. This significant endeavor aims to mitigate flood risks for surrounding properties, boosting community safety. Key efforts include reconnecting Mud Creek with its floodplain to enhance water quality and flood management. Financial support from various organizations has been crucial in the project's design and construction.

stories.title: Henry F. Porter Preserve Deal: 181 acres permanently protected; cross-border pact links key habitats
stories.summary: A groundbreaking conservation project has successfully preserved 181 acres of forests and wetlands straddling Maryland and Delaware. Championed by the Porter family alongside multiple conservation entities, the Henry F. Porter Preserve focuses on safeguarding vital ecosystems. This initiative not only emphasizes sustainable practices but also plays a pivotal role in the overall protection of the Chesapeake Bay watershed.

stories.title: 'Don't worry about lathis': Rahul calls on people to join INDIA bloc's 'Delhi chalo' march
stories.summary: Rahul Gandhi invited everyone to partake in the upcoming Chalo Delhi march at Ramlila Maidan. This initiative seeks to challenge purported electoral malfeasance and uphold democratic integrity. He stated the march embodies the nation’s collective desire and is open to all political groups. Student bodies from throughout the political spectrum are encouraged to join. The Congress party plans a significant opposition rally on November 1.

stories.title: Michigan appeals court upholds $9.7 million verdict after mother dies following tummy tuck surgery
stories.summary: In a landmark decision, a Michigan court has affirmed a nearly $9.7 million ruling against Henry Ford Macomb Hospital for negligence that led to Cathleen Allen's tragic death after cosmetic surgery complications. Medical testimony highlighted that prompt action could have preserved her life. The jury attributed liability to both the surgeon and hospital, underscoring the urgent need for stringent patient safety measures.

‘Unwavering commitment’: Rajnath Singh backs ASEAN centrality, calls for stronger defence ties
JeI functionary met Indian intel official in secret: Bangladesh PM aide
MEA says 22 Indians killed during West Asia conflict
'From the river to the sea': Hundreds rally across Israel advocating Jewish-Arab gov
stories.summary: Around 300 demonstrators gathered in Jerusalem, Tel Aviv, and Haifa to demand a Jewish-Arab government. Protesters held signs advocating for freedom and inclusive governance, reflecting their unified call. The demonstrations coincided with ongoing vote counting following Israel's closely contested election. Pro-Netanyahu parties secured 53 seats, while the opposing bloc held 48, leaving no clear majority. Opposition leader Gadi Eisenkot emphasized a need for change, criticizing Netanyahu's government.

Isro to launch NVS-03 on Oct 30, but NavIC has a long way to go
IN-SPACe picks 6 AI space projects for grants of up to Rs 1-cr each
Sunshine Buns, started in 2022 by four Utah friends, raised $7 million
stories.summary: Sunshine Buns has successfully secured $7 million in Series A funding, allowing them to broaden their store presence. Founded by four friends using a family cinnamon roll recipe, their frozen delights are now featured in major retailers like Target and Costco. This new funding will support production and marketing efforts, and the founders attribute their success to local mentors and the nurturing startup community in Utah.

stories.title: Diver searching the bottom of England’s River Wear has pulled a huge three legged iron cauldron
stories.summary: An ancient iron cauldron, potentially from the medieval or Iron Age, was found submerged under water. Underwater archaeologist Gary Bankhead led a team of divers in this ambitious recovery mission. Experts are currently investigating the cauldron's design and historical relevance. This intriguing find prompts speculation about its origin and journey into the river, with plans underway for a public exhibition at a nearby museum.

stories.title: Megan Fox settled $5M Malibu home lawsuit for $100K after three-year fight
Florida man pays HOA debt five days after home auction; court overturns sale cancellation
stories.summary: A Florida homeowner paid his outstanding homeowners' association fees five days after his property was sold at a foreclosure auction in October 2024. The sale was subsequently cancelled, but the winning bidder challenged the decision, saying it had not been heard. Nearly two years later, a Florida appeals court overturned the cancellation and ordered a fresh hearing.

stories.title: Israel poll results deadlocked amid historic showing by Arab parties
Monitor welfare schemes closely: PM Modi to chief secretaries
SC summons Sanjay Raut in contempt case
Yet to test legality of logical discrepancy in SIR: Supreme Court
Historian Charles Greig donated 50 paintings and watercolours to Tate; from colonial India
stories.summary: In a remarkable gesture, Tate London has received a donation of 50 artworks from the British colonial era in India, showcasing the talents of both Indian and European artists. This diverse collection, meticulously curated by British art historian Charles Greig over 40 years, will be publicly exhibited at Tate Britain in 2028, enhancing public access to these invaluable historical pieces and underscoring the importance of art preservation.

stories.title: Texas barber returns $128,514 found at ATM despite rent struggles
stories.summary: In Lewisville, Texas, a barber stumbled upon two bags at an ATM, one filled with an astonishing $128,514 in cash. Struggling with rent and financial issues, he made the commendable choice to report this to the authorities. The bags belonged to a Brink’s team who had accidentally left them behind. Though no financial reward was given, the barber's honesty was recognized and celebrated by the police.

stories.title: Georgia siblings fight over 95-year-old mother's care and assets; court backs daughter
stories.summary: A dispute between three siblings over their 95-year-old mother's care reached the Georgia Court of Appeals after one son restricted his sister's visits and questions emerged over the handling of their mother's money. The woman, who has advanced dementia, had previously authorised her son to manage her affairs. However, the court upheld her daughter's appointment as guardian.

stories.title: NDA wins 1 6 of 28 seats, Congress falters in MLC polls
Rahul lashes out at government over Tatas, FM Nirmala Sitharaman hits back
In SC, biological women oppose equal rights for transgender women
Vance tests diplomatic route to Iran as Trump weighs escalation
The UK plans to send giant robotic claws into orbit to grab two dead satellites; 2029 mission
stories.summary: In a groundbreaking initiative, the UK plans to unveil a pioneering spacecraft in 2029, designed specifically for the cleanup of space debris. Utilizing advanced robotic arms, the mission aims to snatch up and incinerate inactive satellites, tackling the escalating issue of orbital pollution that threatens current satellite operations. A nationwide competition to name the spacecraft is in progress, underscoring the project's significance in fostering sustainable space practices.

stories.title: Delhi HC rejects PIL against passport fee hike for NRIs
Maui Estate Fetches $18.5 Million: Renovated Makena home tops 2026 sale; big price cut reflects cooling market
stories.summary: Recently, a stunning oceanfront estate in Makena, Maui, fetched a remarkable $18.5 million. After undergoing extensive renovations to boost its allure, this property saw an adjustment in its listing price from an initially higher value. While Hawaii's ultra-luxury housing market, especially for homes over $10 million, has been experiencing a downturn, this sale highlights ongoing interest in distinctive coastal properties.

stories.title: To empower panchayats, gram yojana gets nod
Two California brothers face 35 felony charges each after hundreds complain of unfinished homes
stories.summary: A retired nurse in California paid more than $40,000 in 2023 for a backyard home that was never built. The company, Anchored Tiny Homes, later faced more than 200 complaints across 18 counties over unfinished projects and missing payments. Its founders, brothers Austin and Colton Paulhus, now face 35 felony charges each, while affected homeowners remain uncertain about recovering their money.

In 2012 and 2013, Maine removed two old Penobscot River dams to restore migratory routes; by September 2026, the Milford fish lift had counted a preliminary 5.85 million river herring returning upstream
stories.summary: In a significant ecological feat, the Penobscot River restoration in Maine has revitalized migratory fish numbers dramatically. The removal of the Great Works and Veazie dams has paved the way for essential fish migration pathways once again. As a result, the population of river herring has surged from just 556 to over 5 million.

stories.title: Australian couple sells 1832 Georgian Mansion for A$1.6M after 14 years
Harris V Natural England: court faults regulator over Catfield Fen; campaigners eye next steps
stories.summary: In an impressive legal battle, two Norfolk farmers have secured a significant ruling for the Catfield Fen wetland, which faces threats from pollution. The High Court determined that Natural England neglected its duty to shield this vital habitat from agricultural runoff. The couple, who have invested approximately £1.5 million over the past 15 years to combat environmental challenges, stress the importance of strict enforcement of ecological regulations.

A community in South Australia’s first dark-sky reserve is opposing a proposed hyperscale data centre; residents fear the development could change the rural landscape and threaten the darkness that draws visitors
stories.summary: Residents of Tungkillo, South Australia, are concerned about a proposed data centre that could disrupt their dark-sky reserve. The development may introduce light and noise pollution that affects the rural landscape. Community members believe preserving their unique nighttime environment is crucial for stargazing and natural experiences. The project's economic benefits are being weighed against potential environmental impacts. Ongoing discussions will determine the future of digital infrastructure in the region.
